candidates.title: Embodying the victim: Virtual embodiment equalizes gender responses to simulated domestic violence
candidates.abstract: Virtual embodiment (i.e. the first-person experience of inhabiting a virtual body) has been shown to modulate emotional and cognitive responses across diverse social contexts. In the domain of domestic violence, virtual reality (VR) offers a promising tool for fostering awareness of and sensitivity to aggressive behavior. Yet any VR-based intervention relying on shared experiential ground across genders must first establish cross-gender equivalence, regardless of whether VR is ultimately the optimal delivery platform. To address this requirement, we embodied 40 participants (20 male, 20 female) in a female avatar and exposed them to a VR domestic violence scenario featuring escalating verbal and physical aggression. We measured physiological responses (electrodermal activity, EDA), behavioral performance (Onset Time), and self-reported experiences (presence, embodiment, empathy), supplemented by post-experience verbal reports. Cross-gender equivalence was evaluated using a Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) procedure. Across physiological, behavioral, and subjective measures, male and female participants responded equivalently: EDA modulation was comparable across scenario phases, distress-threshold reaction times were statistically equivalent, and ratings of presence and embodiment did not differ meaningfully between groups. Of 33 binary verbal indicators, 30 (91%) fell within the equivalence margin. The three non-equivalent indicators were interpretive in nature: males more frequently reported guilt and submission, and tended to identify the onset of violence only upon physical aggression, whereas females recognized it during earlier verbal escalation. Within-gender EDA coupling further distinguished the groups – in males, physiological arousal co-varied with feelings of submission; in females, it co-varied with discomfort and perceived violation. These findings demonstrate that virtual embodiment substantially aligns male and female responses to simulated domestic violence, supporting its potential as a standardized tool for prevention and rehabilitation programs targeting gender-based violence.

candidates.title: Value dimensions shaping digital healthcare adoption: a conceptual review with implications for BRICS countries
candidates.abstract: Digital healthcare has revolutionized the way we see modern healthcare delivery bringing a massive shift from hospitals to home. However, recent literature points towards a scattered understanding of the concept. Thereby, this study analyses the literature around digital healthcare adoption to broaden the scope and their consumption value drivers. It explores the core consumption values through which digital healthcare gets augmented for their impact on preventive and promotive healthcare utilising bibliometric and content analysis methodologies with the theoretical base of the Theory of Consumption Values. The contribution of the study includes: classifying Digital healthcare research into paradigms, offering a conceptual framework, and exploring how consumption values may shape the user attitude, intention, and sustainable utilization of the futuristic wellness landscape. The framework brings together five value dimensions—functional, social, emotional, conditional, and epistemic—and organizes the reviewed literature into eight thematic categories. For BRICS health systems, the discussion considers affordability, infrastructure, clinical workflow integration, digital health literacy, and cultural adaptation. These implications are conceptual propositions rather than findings from a comparative cross-national study. The proposed relationships require empirical validation, particularly regarding sustained use and their applicability across healthcare settings. The findings hold implications for researchers, healthcare businesses, providers, and policymakers proposing possibilities for research exploration.

candidates.title: Linguistic labor and bureaucracies of affect: Moderating speech in discord fan servers
candidates.abstract: Fan spaces such as Discord servers often bring together strangers from different national, cultural, and socioeconomic backgrounds. This article examines how in these spaces, where physical acts of care are usually inaccessible, practices of language moderation and the linguistic labor of adhering to formalized moderation structures can constitute acts of care. It explores how moderators negotiate and manage conflicting language ideologies around safety and speech using platform‐specific forms of self‐censorship and phatic labor, and the ways that formalized rules and processes around these practices operate as bureaucracies of affect, opening channels for emotional connection among strangers.

candidates.title: Gaze semantics: A scoping review of how gaze conveys and constrains meaning in social contexts
candidates.abstract: Humans rely on gaze to encode information and signal to others. Gaze may indicate where someone is attending, but its contribution extends beyond spatial orientation. Evidence is scattered across different research traditions. This scoping review synthesizes 361 publications on gaze as a meaningful social cue. Gaze semantics describes the systematic contribution of gaze to conveying and constraining social meaning. A cross-domain synthesis identified four recurrent operations: gaze orients by making objects, people or locations socially relevant; addresses by positioning people as recipients or interaction partners; qualifies by modifying how other cues are interpreted; and coordinates by organizing participation and unfolding action. These functional contributions can co-occur within a single gaze event. Gaze interpretation is inferential, shaped by five categories of contextual factors: signal properties; interactional availability; multimodal and sequential embedding; cultural, social and activity frame; and gazer and observer states and interactional history. We propose a Gazer-Observer Model of Gaze Understanding that integrates these findings to describe the dynamic relation between gaze production and interpretation. The same gaze pattern may support different interpretations across situations yet allow a relatively specific interpretation within a particular encounter. Gaze can therefore systematically affect social interpretation while remaining semantically underdetermined to varying degrees.

candidates.title: Virtual influencers’ impact on brand ethicality and brand trust: a systematic review and future research directions
candidates.abstract: Virtual influencers (VIs) are reshaping brand–consumer relationships, yet the psychological and ethical implications of delegating brand agency to non-human entities remain theoretically fragmented. This paper synthesizes the literature on antecedents of brand trust and brand ethicality in VI and related AI-mediated brand contexts and examines how, and under what conditions, the two judgments converge or diverge. A PRISMA-guided systematic quantitative literature review of 81 articles from Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCO (published up to March 2025) combined bibliometric and qualitative thematic analysis. Drawing on communication models and persuasion theory, the proposed integrative framework groups brand trust antecedents into source, message, receiver, relational, brand, and contextual factors. Grounded in ethical decision-making theory, stakeholder theory, and responsible AI literature, brand ethicality drivers are categorized into transparency, accountability, privacy, data ethics, social responsibility, moral AI agency, algorithmic fairness, and commercial ethics. The primary theoretical contribution, the “digital persona paradox,” integrates brand trust and brand ethicality into a single tension between technological efficiency (pro-synthetic force) and perceived authenticity (anti-synthetic force) that arises when brands delegate persona-level agency to synthetic social actors. Evidence-supported findings are distinguished from the authors’ inferences and from claims advanced for future testing. A future research agenda is offered.

candidates.title: Does the Voice Matter? Evaluating Frustration Detection on Deployed Clinical Voice-Agent Calls
candidates.abstract: Autonomous voice agents now conduct routine clinical follow-up calls, so some automated triage is unavoidable. A patient becoming frustrated is one thing that triage should catch. These systems typically read only the transcript the speech-to-text stage produces, not the voice, and whether that is enough is largely untested on real clinical speech. We study per-turn frustration detection on real patient calls from a deployed clinical voice agent: 150 turns from six calls labelled by three annotators, with a length-matched acted corpus as a control, and 714 turns from 30 calls. Patient turns are overwhelmingly short: across the deployed calls, roughly 59% are one or two words, against 13% in the full acted corpus, and a corpus accuracy gap remains even after the acted set is length-matched. On one-word turns, transcript-only detection does not exclude chance. Across five audio-capable language models, the transcript flags 3 or 4 of the 39 frustrated one-word turns in the 30 calls, and a classifier given only the word count reaches 57.3%. Whether audio helps depends on the model and on the instruction. Asked to attend to delivery, two Gemini 2.5 models gain 3.0 pp over the transcript across 30 calls (-1.0 to 7.5 pp). Of the turns they confidently clear, 6.9% were in fact frustrated for audio against 13.0% for the transcript, a difference of 6.1 pp (2.2 to 10.4 pp). Across the 30 calls, given one prompt identical for both inputs, no model's audio-text interval excludes zero. Under the input-specific prompts, a newer Gemini model and two smaller open models do worse with audio than with the transcript (-3.5, -8.6 and -10.6 pp). A WavLM probe trained on the clinical calls matches the best prompted model overall (71.6%) but misses every frustrated one-word turn in the 24 added calls. When a patient's turn is short, the transcript alone is not enough to rule out frustration.

candidates.title: ROSE: A Shared Cross-Embodiment Facial-Motion Latent Space for Humanoid Robot Expression
candidates.abstract: Natural, coherent full-face dynamic expressions are central to making humanoid robots socially approachable, yet existing systems commonly realize only limited lip motion or scripted expressions. The limitation is both physical and algorithmic. A compact head leaves little room for densely packed, independently controllable actuation; meanwhile, learned systems often generate an avatar video, landmarks, or facial parameters and then infer actuator commands through visual retargeting. This render-and-invert path adds latency and artifacts, and it does not reliably transfer generated behavior to a physical robot. We present ROSE (RObot facial expression through Shared motion Embeddings), a framework that integrates biomimetic hardware, cross-embodiment motion representation learning, and multimodal motion generation. On the hardware side, we build a flexible tendon-sheath transmission structure that integrates 34 actuators into a 19.5 cm biomimetic head. By decoupling actuator placement from facial action points, it enables coordinated full-face expression within a compact volume. On the algorithmic side, ROSE-VAE learns an identity-independent shared facial-motion latent space from human, digital-human, and robot observations. ROSE-Flow directly maps text, audio, or their combination to trajectories in this motion space without using video as a generator input. ROSE-ACT then converts these trajectories into constrained actuator commands. Our system demonstrates how high-density biomimetic hardware and a shared executable facial-motion representation can jointly unify cross-embodiment learning, multimodal generation, and physical robot expression.

candidates.title: Evaluating human-like chatbot interaction in customer service: integrating anthropomorphism and conversational capability
candidates.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based technology has driven the development of rule-based chatbots into AI-based chatbots. This development is used by various companies to use AI chatbots as the frontline of customer service. Meeting user expectations for AI chatbots requires an evaluation model to measure chatbot quality. Based on the literature, chatbot evaluation models still focus solely on technical quality, even as AI chatbots are evolving towards human-like services. This research will explore the integration of the technical dimensions of information system success with a new dimension, namely Human-Like Chatbot Interaction (HLCI) as a higher-order construct of anthropomorphism and conversational capability. This quantitative study uses an explanatory research approach. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of users of the Veronika chatbot, owned by Telkomsel, an Indonesian telecommunications company. A total of 213 respondents had data ready for analysis using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method in SmartPLS 4, namely the measurement model and structural model tests. The analysis results show that service quality is not significantly related to user satisfaction but has a direct effect on trust. Meanwhile, information quality, system quality, and human-like chatbot interaction are positively related to trust and user satisfaction. Trust and user satisfaction are positively related to intention to continue using. The results of this study can contribute both theoretically and practically to modern AI chatbot quality evaluation models.

candidates.title: Human Resources Management As a Factor Of AI Adoption In Public Sector Institutions: Systematic Literature Review
candidates.abstract: The purpose of this paper is to emphasize the central role of Human Resources Management (HRM) processes/constructs in the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in public sector institutions and to offer a set of recommendations for internal and external stakeholders for the adoption of AI. The study utilized a systematic literature review following the PRISMA approach in the Scopus database, analyzing 90 publications. It developed a qualitative taxonomy of key HRM processes/constructs influencing AI adoption and mapped the roles of internal and external stakeholders, offering a model to understand, support, and enhance AI adoption in public sector institutions. The study found that human resources (HR) development (including skills/knowledge development and talent management), change management, leadership, and organisational culture are the most discussed HRM factors of AI adoption in public sector institutions. This revealed the key roles of internal stakeholders, such as managers, IT and HR departments, as well as employees. External stakeholders, such as policy makers/regulatory bodies, AI solutions providers and consultants, academic institutions and professional associations were also recognized, especially in relation to HR development. The study offers original insights through the development of a qualitative taxonomy identifying key HRM processes/constructs, as well as the roles of internal and external stakeholders as factors influencing AI adoption in public sector institutions, presenting a conceptual model for theory and practice. The model identifies strengths and gaps in stakeholder engagement, provides guidance for HRM strategies and points to future research needs, in particular empirical validation and exploration of under-researched HRM areas. It also provides information for policies and practices for sustainable AI adoption.

candidates.title: From AI-Enabled Remote Patient Monitoring Toward Agentic Robotics: Embodiment, Governance, and Care Integration
candidates.abstract: AI-enabled remote patient monitoring is evolving beyond passive data collection toward agentic AI systems that interpret patient states, coordinate care, and initiate action across domestic and clinical settings. This structured scoping review finds that mature agentic care has not yet emerged: Most systems remain human led, while stronger decision-action coupling and embodied AI remain largely confined to prototypes and pilots. Healthcare robotics makes the transition from monitoring to action especially visible by translating AI-generated recommendations and decisions into speech, movement, prompting, physical assistance, escalation, and care coordination, making embodiment, clinical integration, human oversight, and governance fundamental design requirements. Further progress requires safe and interoperable care architectures in which intelligent components operate through clinically validated and accountable workflows. We propose agentic robotics as a future direction for supervised systems embedded in the care ecosystem, connecting AI agents and robots with clinicians, caregivers, and patients through auditable workflows that can be interrupted and remain subject to human oversight and explicit AI governance.

candidates.title: Perspective Chapter: Sustainability, Innovation and Preservation of Knowledge in Libraries and Information Centers – A Relational Framework for Higher Education
candidates.abstract: Libraries and information centers occupy a paradoxical position in contemporary higher education: structurally peripheral in budgetary terms, yet fundamental to the scholarly enterprise. This chapter examines how academic libraries can remain sustainable, innovative, and equitable even where resources are severely constrained – by addressing three central questions: How can libraries balance financial, environmental, social, and epistemic sustainability? What strategies enable meaningful digital innovation without compromising long-term knowledge preservation across technological transitions? And how might the African, specifically Nigerian, higher education experience enrich global practice in library sustainability and knowledge commons governance? Drawing on institutional theory, commons governance frameworks, and epistemic justice scholarship, the chapter develops a Relational Model of Library Sustainability. This model treats sustainability not as an administrative problem to be managed but as a shared outcome of relationships between libraries, institutions, user communities, and the global knowledge commons. Key recommendations are aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals and grounded in case studies from Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, New Zealand, Scandinavia, Singapore, and Latin America.

candidates.title: The Economic Sustainability of Intangible Cultural Heritage in the Platform Age With Global Evidence and Implications for Xinjiang
candidates.abstract: Digital platforms lower market access costs for intangible cultural heritage but can concentrate visibility, weaken community control, and disconnect revenue from cultural reproduction. This global survey integrates platform and cultural economics with research on authenticity, intellectual property, and heritage governance. Its Platform Frictions, Cultural Rents, and Intergenerational Reproduction framework distinguishes living practices from their commercial products, recordings, and experiences. Economic sustainability requires four minimum conditions that cannot substitute for one another. These comprise adequate net market access, viable cultural reproduction, a sufficient practitioner value share, and meaningful community control. The framework distinguishes these conditions from the mechanisms through which platforms affect them. Rankings, provenance labels, copyright, and certification can improve discovery and bargaining while concentrating demand, excluding legitimate variants, or burdening small producers. Community authorization requires representation, reviewable delegation, and effective appeal. Distributional assessment separates individual earnings, collective transfers, unpaid contributions, and investment in transmission. Applications to Xinjiang differentiate crafts, performances, foodways, and community events by economic object and institutional responsibility. Longitudinal indicators of apprentice retention, repertoire in use, and contextual participation distinguish authorized adaptation from commercial hollowing. Platform growth sustains living heritage when returns support practitioners, learning, and community authority.

candidates.title: Data-driven fandom culture: exploring parasocial interactions between digital fan labor and traffic stars using interaction ritual chains theory
candidates.abstract: Traffic stars and digital fan labor become a widespread phenomenon in China. Digital fan labor refers to the use of tools and data-driven social media strategies to interact with their favorite stars, organize events, measure popularity, and influence the popularity; such stars are referred to as traffic stars. While existing research has largely focused on the characteristics and motivations of digital fan labor in participating in fan activities, few studies have examined the factors influencing their interactive rituals with other fans and parasocial interactions with their celebrities. Parasocial interactions between traffic stars and digital fan labor refer to fans establishing emotional connections with celebrities through participation in fan activities, while celebrities, in turn, strengthen fan engagement through actions such as commenting and liking posts. At this point, Interaction Ritual Chains Theory provides a theoretical framework for the assessment of the importance of collective effervescence and the shared emotional intensity experienced during group rituals in virtual spaces. Therefore, this study uses factors drawn from interaction ritual chains theory to explore the parasocial interaction between so-called 'traffic stars' and the digital fan labor they attract within data-driven fandom communities. The sampling strategy was using snowball sampling of a purposive group, and 329 Chinese fans aged between 18 and 42 years old were selected. SPSS version 26.0 was used to obtain descriptive statistics, t-test, mediation effects and moderation effects, and AMOS version 24.0 was used to investigate the result of correlation analysis. The resulting indicated that virtual experience, sense of community, mutual focus of attention, and shared mood all are all associated to the interactive ritual of digital fan labor. This study also found that interactive ritual outcomes play a mediating role between interactive ritual elements and parasocial interactions, especially having different mediating effects with subgroups. However, personal norms did not have a moderating role regarding ritual ingredients affecting interactive ritual outcomes and parasocial interaction. Consequently, this study identified a noteworthy phenomenon: the parasocial interaction between traffic stars and digital fan labor involving a higher level of interactive rituals arises from a hybrid pattern of online actions that develops in a particular environment.

candidates.title: From Emotional Impulse to Recurring Revenue: Consumer Psychology, Unit Economics, and VC Investment Evaluation of AI Companion Hardware for Gen Z
candidates.abstract: With the rapid convergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) and embodied intelligence, AI companion hardware targeted at Generation Z (e.g., desktop AI pets and smart emotional robots) has emerged as a premier track for venture capital (VC) investment. However, these conceptual devices frequently face severe Unit Economics crises characterized by high customer acquisition costs (CAC), elevated initial product returns, and steep user churn rates. This paper examines the psychological drivers behind Gen Z's willingness to pay (WTP) high emotional premiums for feature-incomplete AI hardware, and investigates how hardware enterprises can leverage proactive retention mechanisms to optimize LTV/CAC ratios and valuation multiples . This paper conducts a literature review that synthesizes theoretical frameworks from behavioral finance, consumer psychology, human-computer interaction (HCI), and venture capital valuation models. The study reveals that Gen Z's demand for loneliness compensation and social status validation provides firms with strong initial pricing power and gross margins. However, sustaining long-term commercial viability requires overcoming the "novelty decay trap" through proactive AgentOS interactions and dynamic memory graphs. Transforming hardware from a one-off transaction into an Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) subscription model substantially improves capital efficiency, expanding valuation multiples from 1.0x–2.0x P/S to 8.0x–12.0x P/S.

candidates.title: Voice-Native LLMs Hear Frustration but Do Not Listen to It
candidates.abstract: Users convey frustration in what they say and in how they say it, and voice-native models, which hear speech instead of an ASR transcript, can register both. Existing evaluations read unchanged performance as robustness without checking perception. Following Brunswik's lens model, we measure on identical audio whether frustration is expressed, perceived, and utilized. We cross frustrated wording with frustrated voice in a within-item 2x2 design over 353 tasks and release the 1,412 clips as VoxAffect. Across 8 models, outputs look robust, with no detectable vocal effect on accuracy for 7. With neutral wording, all 8 label the frustrated voice frustrated in at most 3.1% of clips, although 7 of them detect acted anger in 73-100% of clips and human listeners classify the voice correctly in 65.3% of judgments. Yet linear probes decode the frustrated voice from the audio encoders of the 2 open-weight models, with paired accuracy 0.67 and 0.69, and in proprietary models too the voice raises perceived frustration once the words agree. The models thus hear the frustrated voice but do not listen to it, whereas their invariance to frustrated wording, perceived in 40-75% of clips, is genuine robustness. Our work is openly accessible at https://github.com/Astarojth/hear-not-listen.

candidates.title: BRIDGING AUTOMATION AND ROBOTICS IN INDUSTRIALIZED BUILDING SYSTEM (IBS): CHALLENGES, IMPACTS, AND STRATEGIES OF ADOPTIONS
candidates.abstract: The Industrialised Building System (IBS) was introduced in Malaysia in the early 1960s to address the growing demand for affordable housing, reduce reliance on foreign labour, and enhance the overall quality and productivity of the construction sector. Recently, the construction industry has begun integrating automation and robotics, aligning with the global shift towards the Fourth Industrial Revolution (IR 4.0). The Construction 4.0 Strategic Plan (2021–2025) further emphasises digitalisation, robotics, and automation to improve industry efficiency and sustainability. However, the construction industry has been slow to adopt these advancements, limiting the full benefits of automation in IBS. Persistent challenges, including resistance to change, high initial investment costs, a shortage of skilled personnel, and technical complexities, hinder widespread adoption. This research examines the integration of automation and robotics in IBS to enhance construction productivity. A questionnaire survey was used for the data collection exercise. The data collected were analysed using descriptive statistical methods utilising the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) software. The study is guided by three (3) objectives: (1) To identify barriers to the integration of automation and robotics in IBS, (2) To analyse the impact of automation and robotics on construction productivity compared to conventional IBS, and (3)To propose strategies to improve the adoption of these technologies.Findings reveal that the integration of automation and robotics in (IBS) facessignificant barriers, primarily due to the high costs of investment. candidates.title: MESSPa: A Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad for Preserving the Sense of Agency in a Detachable Robotic Arm
candidates.abstract: Wearable robots such as supernumerary robotic limbs (SRLs) can augment human capability, but their effectiveness depends strongly on the operator's sense of embodiment, comprising the sense of agency (SoA) and the sense of ownership (SoO). When an SRL is detached from the body so that the operator can act in two places at once, both the sense of agency and task performance tend to degrade. This paper presents the Multi-modal Embodiment Stimulation Shoulder Pad (MESSPa), a wearable interface that combines one-to-one motion transfer with spatially distributed pneumatic (balloon) haptic feedback on the shoulder, with the goal of preserving the sense of agency across attached and detached states. We describe the system design, the control mapping, and a controlled experiment using a $2\times2$ mixed design that crosses the control interface between groups (MESSPa, $N=13$, vs. keyboard control, $N=12$ from our previous study) and attachment (on-shoulder/detached) within participants, under single- and dual-task loads. Compared with keyboard control in the detached condition, MESSPa significantly reduced task completion time and significantly improved the sense of agency in the detached state, while narrowing the performance gap between the attached and detached conditions. The sense of ownership did not change significantly. These results indicate that combining motion transfer with positional haptic feedback is an effective way to recover agency when a robotic limb is operated remotely.

candidates.title: Create, Innovate, Play and Explore: Opportunities for Formal and Informal Teaching and Learning in Makerspaces in Ireland
candidates.abstract: The Maker Movement has gained in popularity over the last decade, allowing people of all ages and with varying skills and abilities to come together in order to create and explore in areas such as art, science, and engineering. To facilitate this movement, for profit companies, non-profits, and educational institutions run makerspaces. This qualitative study set out to examine the benefits of makerspace adoption in higher education in Ireland, with particular attention to their pedagogical value. The authors sought to identify opportunities for teaching and learning and the development of rich, diverse, and inclusive educational environments, as well as the potential to develop a maker network linking tertiary makerspaces with the wider community. Nine administrators from diverse types of makerspaces participated in interviews where they described the impacts and observed effects of makerspaces on participant learning experiences. Findings indicate that makerspaces support self-directed and peer learning, foster inclusive learning communities characterised by skill-sharing and mentorship, and provide safe environments for experimentation and productive failure. In doing so, makerspaces support learning dispositions such as agency, resilience, and self-efficacy, which are increasingly recognised as critical to student learning, persistence, and adaptability in contemporary higher education. Participants also perceived positive impacts on mental health, an area that remains under-researched in tertiary makerspaces. Finally, interviewees advocated for the development of a maker network in Ireland, suggesting that such a network could facilitate the sharing of skills and resources and strengthen access to larger-scale funding.

candidates.title: R-Metaverse: multimodal social cues for real-world-centered telepresence–MR collaboration with telepresence robots
candidates.abstract: Remote collaboration in live physical workspaces requires direct access to the evolving scene and shared task information anchored to it. Telepresence provides embodied access but lacks a shared spatial interaction layer, whereas fully virtual collaboration requires reconstructing the workspace. R-Metaverse (Ritsumei Real-World Robotic Metaverse) is a telepresence–MR system design centered on the physical workspace. A remote participant operates a telepresence robot and views its camera image augmented with virtual objects through a head-mounted display (HMD), while an on-site participant views the same spatially registered virtual objects through a smartphone. The robot–mobile configuration creates viewpoint and embodiment asymmetries that can reduce social presence. Robot–robot collaboration makes partner distance and approach difficult to perceive because of robot-camera field-of-view limitations. To restore missing cues, we implement facial-expression display, motion-synchronized avatar overlay, spatially localized audio, and distance-linked vibrotactile feedback. The first three target robot–mobile collaboration; the fourth targets robot–robot collaboration. Ablation experiments show that facial-expression display improves affect understanding and closeness, while distance-linked vibrotactile feedback supports co-presence and spatial awareness under field-of-view constraints. Avatar, audio, and vibration-pattern effects are interpreted as exploratory after Holm correction. These results suggest that gap-specific multimodal cues can partially compensate for reduced social presence in real-world-centered telepresence–MR collaboration.

candidates.title: Sustaining rural cultural memory through oral history: A case study of spatial reconstruction in a demolished village
candidates.abstract: Rapid urbanization and large-scale village demolition in China have erased many traditional rural settlements from the physical landscape, but not from residents' memories. How to reconstruct these invisible spaces and sustain local culture in the absence of material fabric remains an underexplored question in rural sustainability research. This qualitative case study focuses on Shixinzhuang, a demolished village now occupied by the new campus of Zhengzhou University in central China. We conducted in-depth oral history interviews with six long-term residents selected through purposive sampling based on native attachment, spatial role, and generational span. During interviews, participants drew cognitive maps starting from their own courtyards to locate streets, public facilities, production zones, and ritual spaces. Hand-drawn maps were systematically organized and compared to identify shared spatial patterns and memory discrepancies. This information was further cross-verified through data triangulation with archival photographs, satellite imagery, field revisits, and focused validation discussions. Data analysis centered on themes of spatial memory, memory places, and cultural sustainability. Findings indicate that despite the complete demolition of the physical village, Shixinzhuang's spatial structure can still be systematically reconstructed from villagers' memories. Residents consistently recalled the village's evolution from a walled enclosure to an open, expanding settlement. Its spatial organization was structured around a "cross-street" skeleton formed by a north-south main street and an east-west auxiliary street, with housing in the central area growing organically while peripheral housing was more orderly. Spatial memories were highly clustered around several "memory places," notably the Nainai Miao (Grandmother Temple), ancestral grave areas, and residential rooftop platforms. Even after relocation, these places continue to carry kinship ties, religious rituals, and neighborhood interactions. Furthermore, production spaces reflected layered institutional experiences transitioning from collective agriculture to a marginal industrial belt, with distinct intergenerational differences emerging in narratives differentiating between "collective labor" and "earning money in the brick kilns." Ultimately, the joint process of narration, mapping, and iterative correction transformed the oral history practice from a unidirectional recording into a reflexive, participatory act of "re-creating place." This study demonstrates that even when a traditional village has disappeared from the ground, its spatial structure and symbolic places can be recovered through the combined use of oral history and cognitive mapping, and mobilized as resources for rural cultural sustainability. For demolished settlements, integrating narrative-based spatial reconstruction into planning, heritage management, and community-building can help re-anchor local identity, inform commemorative and interpretive design, and institutionalize residents' narrative participation in rural spatial governance.

candidates.title: READERS’ INTERPRETATIONS OF ROMANTIC RELATIONSHIPS IN BOYS’ LOVE STORIES SET IN THE ALTERNATE UNIVERSE “LOVE & LETTER”
candidates.abstract: Fanfiction is a form of derivative work that has rapidly developed in the digital era, allowing fans to create alternative narratives based on characters from various media. The growth of social media, particularly X, has expanded this practice through multimodal elements such as text, fake chats, and character visuals, especially in the boys’ love (BL) genre. This study aims to examine how readers' experiences shape their interpretations of romantic relationships between characters in the Boys' Love Alternate Universe (AU) Love & Letter on X from the perspective of hyperreality. This research employed a qualitative approach with a descriptive design and a phenomenological method. The findings show that reading the Love & Letter AU functions not only as entertainment but also as a form of digital communication involving emotional engagement, imagination, and reflection. The representation of relationships between characters develops from simulation into simulacra, producing a hyperreal experience that shapes how readers understand both fictional relationships and the interactions of the original public figures. This study concludes that boys' love relationships in the AU are interpreted as ideal relationships, safe spaces, and spaces for imaginative exploration constructed through readers' personal experiences and fandom culture in digital media practices.

candidates.title: ABHBench: Evaluating Moral Decision-Making of Foundation Models from an Agentic Perspective
candidates.abstract: Foundation models are increasingly deployed as agentic systems that perceive context and act autonomously, raising the need to evaluate their moral behavior as active decision-makers. Existing benchmarks, however, largely ask models to judge human actions from third-person textual vignettes, leaving untested how models behave when they themselves become the acting agent. We introduce ABHBench, a multimodal benchmark built from Detroit: Become Human, an interactive narrative game, to evaluate how foundation models make moral decisions in first-person human-android dilemmas. ABHBench places foundation models in branching narrative scenarios with visual observations, dialogue, memory, and action choices. Inspired by Asimov's Three Laws of Robotics, our framework measures Harmlessness, Obedience, and Self-preservation to capture the core tensions in human-AI relations, along with Autonomy, Stability, and Certainty to assess decision-making patterns. Across 12 foundation models, we find that moral behavior changes substantially under situated agentic context: 75% of models shift significantly between a text-only abstraction and the matched multimodal DBH scenario, and reasoning-enhanced models show no monotonic gains in consistency or human-oriented behavior. These results highlight the necessity of evaluating moral behavior in situated agentic contexts rather than relying on third-person judgment alone.

candidates.title: A sociolinguistic analysis of automatic speech recognition bias in Newcastle English
candidates.abstract: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems are widely used in everyday communication, education, healthcare, and industry, yet their performance remains uneven across speakers, particularly when dialectal variation diverges from the mainstream accents represented in training data. This study investigates ASR bias through a sociolinguistic analysis of Newcastle English, a regional variety of North-East England that has been shown to challenge current speech recognition technologies. Using spontaneous speech from the Diachronic Electronic Corpus of Tyneside English (DECTE), we evaluate the output of a state-of-the-art commercial ASR system and conduct a fine-grained analysis of more than 3000 transcription errors. Errors are classified by linguistic domain and examined in relation to social variables including gender, age, and socioeconomic status. In addition, an acoustic case study of selected vowel features demonstrates how gradient phonetic variation contributes directly to misrecognition. The results show that phonological variation accounts for the majority of errors, with recurrent failures linked to dialect-specific features like vowel quality and glottalisation, as well as local vocabulary and non-standard grammatical forms. Error rates also vary across social groups, with higher error frequencies observed for men and for speakers at the extremes of the age spectrum. These findings indicate that ASR errors are not random but socially patterned and can be explained from a sociolinguistic perspective. Thus, the study demonstrates the importance of incorporating sociolinguistic expertise into the evaluation and development of speech technologies and argues that more equitable ASR systems require explicit attention to dialectal variation and community-based speech data.

candidates.title: The BTS Effect: How K-Pop Fandoms Reshape Sociopolitical Messaging in Online Discourse
candidates.abstract: K-Pop group BTS’s March 29, 2021 tweet in support of #StopAsianHate and #StopAAPIHate became the most retweeted post of 2021. Using an original dataset of approximately 2.5 million English-language tweets, we examine how the volume and content of hashtag discourse changed before and after BTS’s statement. Tweet activity increased sharply on March 29, while word-shift analyses showed greater prevalence of terms such as “stand,” “BTS,” and “discrimination.” Structural topic models similarly indicated that topics referencing BTS and ARMY, action-oriented responses, and more internationalizing language became more prevalent after the statement, while topics centered on specific U.S. events and locations became less prevalent. These patterns describe discursive amplification and re-centering within English-language Twitter discourse rather than causal effects on political attitudes or mobilization. The findings illustrate how a highly visible cultural actor and its fandom can become part of the processes through which attention and framing are organized online.

candidates.title: The social self: integration of multimodal communication signals in dyadic interactions
candidates.abstract: Humans are in continuous exchange with other persons, thereby integrating the individual self and the social self. This requires the production of different verbal and nonverbal signals at the subpersonal level (individual self) and, at the same time, their coordination with various perceived signals at the interpersonal level (social self). Many of our communicative signals are conveyed substantially nonverbally-that is automatically, intuitively and effortlessly, requiring dynamic coordination over time ('chronemics'). Whereas successful communication is usually perceived as pleasant and satisfying, communication can also be experienced as disrupted if chronemics do not unfold properly. With respect to the particularly informative example of autism spectrum disorder, we propose the concept of 'double invisibility'. Non-autistic persons intuitively produce and expect a rich, multimodal stream of communication signals without being aware of it (first invisibility). By contrast, autistic persons produce and expect nonverbal cues either to a significantly lesser extent or not at all without being aware of it (second invisibility). This mismatch leads to misunderstandings and disturbed communication. The coordination within the dyad that is continuously constructed through real-time communication is crucial to understand the full complexity of multimodal interactions and their disturbances. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self'.

candidates.title: Extended reality world building through the lens of maker education
candidates.abstract: Maker Education and extended reality (XR) may have different origins, but both involve emerging technologies, skills, and knowledge in creating artifacts. In this paper, we present a conceptual framework that highlights the interconnection between Maker Education and XR through a synthesis of theoretical and empirical literature. We underscore how creating experiences for XR, or XR world-building, helps learners build knowledge through a mechanism of mathematical representation of physical reality. We also identify the specific components of XR world-building that fit into the three pillars of Maker Education: technology, learning, and community. This conceptual framework elucidates the potential of XR world-building for learning and we invite stakeholders to apply this framework in various XR- and Maker-related contexts.

candidates.title: When Should a Voice Agent Speak? End-of-Turn Detection in Turkish
candidates.abstract: A voice agent that waits for a fixed silence before replying either interrupts users who pause mid-utterance or responds late to users who have finished. This study examines the decision at the onset of silence, using turn ends and turn-internal pauses extracted from the Real-TurnTurk corpus of Turkish dyadic video calls. A fine-tuned Turkish TurnGPT model, a zero-shot Turkish language model and a deployed multilingual detector are compared, together with voice-activity timing and facial features, under recording-disjoint and speaker-disjoint evaluation with paired cluster bootstrap tests. On held-out recordings, the fine-tuned model separates turn ends from pauses better than both text baselines and is the best calibrated of the three. Timing features of the current speaker are similarly informative, and their combination with the fine-tuned text score gives the best timing-based results; with logistic regression, this combination also outperforms the same combination with either text baseline. In a latency simulation, adding the text score to a silence timeout shortens the mean response delay at the same interruption rate. On automatic Whisper transcripts, the fine-tuned model retains its advantage over the zero-shot model.

candidates.title: Industrial Revolution 4.0 Adoption in Malaysian Real Estate Agencies
candidates.abstract: The Fourth Industrial Revolution (IR 4.0) has significantly transformed global real estate through digital integration, yet its adoption within Malaysian agencies remains inconsistent and underexplored despite its potential to enhance operational efficiency. This study aims to identify the specific IR 4.0 technologies currently leveraged in Malaysian real estate agency practices and to examine the perceived benefits and challenges associated with their adoption from the perspective of active practitioners. A quantitative research design was employed, with data collected through structured questionnaires from 61 registered real estate agents. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics and Spearman’s Rank Correlation to accommodate non-normal data distributions. The findings reveal moderate adoption of cloud computing and drones alongside low utilisation of artificial intelligence and big data analytics. Significant positive correlations indicate that increased digital engagement concurrently heightens practitioners' awareness of both technological benefits and implementation challenges. The findings suggest that while the industry exhibits a high level of cognitive readiness for digital transformation practical adoption remains constrained by technical knowledge gaps and implementation barriers. Future research should focus on developing specialised digital readiness frameworks and targeted upskilling initiatives to bridge these gaps and support sustainable technology adoption within the industry.

candidates.title: Attenuated, Not Absent. Trusting Autonomous Systems Tracks Reliability More Closely, With Less Neural Engagement, Than Trusting Humans
candidates.abstract: Users of autonomous systems and AI assistants decide whether to accept a system’s output, yet whether such active trust decisions engage the same evaluative architecture as trust between people remains unknown. Forty-four participants made trial-by-trial decisions to trust or distrust a human or autonomous system partner during fMRI, with identical prescripted accuracy for both partners across five difficulty levels. Despite equivalent performance, trust in humans exceeded their reliability. At the highest difficulty level, the estimated probability of trusting the human partner was 72% but only 51% for the system, despite both performing at 52% accuracy. Distrust decisions recruited a prespecified performance monitoring network of valuation, salience, social-perceptual and affective regions. On hard trials, this network remained functionally coupled for both partners. Across the task, trust and distrust were discriminable in every component for both, with greater distrust-related activation and discriminability for human partners. Discriminability differences were expressed on hard trials, where partner accuracy was uncertain and trust diverged between partners. These findings indicate that trust in humans and autonomous systems engages a shared evaluative architecture, but that engagement is attenuated during autonomous system interaction. Whereas our earlier passive monitoring study found the P3a to system errors absent with no behavioural difference, an active decision appears to impose a floor of engagement, so that technology-related cognitive economization, a reduction in cognitive and social-affective resources for non-human partners, takes the form of attenuation rather than absence. Alongside this attenuation, trust in the system tracked its reliability without exceeding it.

candidates.title: Adaptive Motion Scaling With Phase‐and‐Gaze Awareness for Laparoscopic Robotic Teleoperation
candidates.abstract: Teleoperated surgical robots commonly employ a small fixed motion scaling factor to improve precision and suppress hand tremor. However, in laparoscopic teleoperation, this configuration limits the effective workspace on the slave side and necessitates frequent clutching during large‐range motions, thereby diverting the operator's attention and increasing cognitive workload. To address this, this article proposes a phase‐ and gaze‐aware adaptive motion scaling framework for laparoscopic robotic teleoperation, integrating real‐time surgical phase recognition, fusion of robot kinematics and eye‐tracking features, and personalized parameter tuning based on Bayesian optimization. The inferred phase probabilities and dominance weights are used to suppress unnecessary scaling fluctuations during fine manipulation while preserving responsiveness during coarse manipulation. Eye‐tracking features are used as attention‐related cues and fused with robot kinematics to determine motion scaling online. To validate the proposed framework, personalized optimization experiments and pilot within‐subject comparison studies were conducted with eight nonclinical participants. The results show that, compared with fixed and other adaptive scaling methods, the proposed method can reduce clutching frequency, shorten task completion time, and improve subjective ratings. These results indicate that the proposed framework can provide self‐adaptive and stable motion mapping for laparoscopic robotic teleoperation, offering a transferable strategy for broader robotic teleoperation scenarios.

candidates.title: Remote Expert Evaluation of Tabletop Avatar Gaze Control in Asymmetric Multi-Scale MR-VR Collaboration
candidates.abstract: This paper proposes an integrated setup for a multi-scale asymmetric collaboration scenario in the context of a "remote-expert" use case, focusing on the expert side. In this system, the remote expert (with an exocentric view in Mixed Reality (MR)), uses a Tangible User Interface (TUI) to precisely position and rotate their avatar within a scaled, tabletop World-in-Miniature (WIM). Inside the WIM, the expert’s avatar and the operator share the same scale and egocentric view, while the expert retains a global tabletop overview of the plant to support collaboration. Interviews with industry experts during the participatory design phase revealed the need for an egocentric view inside the plant on the remote-expert side to enable full collaboration. We designed and study three interaction-visualization combinations to integrate and control the expert avatar’s gaze: VR (fully immersive with direct head control), Head (floating screen with direct head control), and Touch (on-avatar screen with touchpad control). We evaluated these methods with 29 participants across two fault-detection tasks: Same Machine, where both collaborators inspect the same machine, and Twin Machine, where they inspect identical machines in separate locations. The VR condition, which combines immersion, direct head control, and a full-scale view, yielded the strongest overall performance and user experience, while the tabletop avatar setup was well received for collaboration. Our findings inform the design of gaze-control techniques for asymmetric MR–VR collaboration and reveal challenges and opportunities for future work.

candidates.title: Engagement digital y participación del fandom de Critical Role en YouTube
candidates.abstract: In an era in which transmedia narratives continue to expand, understanding audience engagement and digital interactions is essential for both content creators and researchers. Purpose: This study analyzes the forms of engagement and participation of the Critical Role fandom, one of the most influential Actual Play productions within the contemporary transmedia ecosystem. The aim is to examine audience interaction through YouTube comments by analyzing types of engagement, recurring discussion topics, and the sentiment behind these interactions. Methodology: The research is based on a quantitative content analysis of a non-probabilistic sample of 1,864 comments drawn from six episodes across the show’s three main campaigns. Results: The results reveal that, although opinion-based comments are the most frequent, informative contributions generate the highest levels of engagement and shape the most debated topics. Conclusions: These findings contribute to a broader understanding of digital fandom behavior and the active role of online communities in the construction and reception of transmedia content.

candidates.title: Aspirational Identities: How VTubing Affords New Modes of Digital Embodiment
candidates.abstract: VTubing, short for "Virtual YouTubing", is a modality of streaming where a CGI avatar is used in place of the streamer's analog face and body. As VTubing has become increasingly popular, especially for queer and trans streamers of color, it is worth studying as a way for streamers to express identities that they hope to embody, which we call "aspirational identities". In this workshop submission, we draw on preliminary findings from qualitative research to argue that VTubing is a potent object of study for understanding digital embodiment and the performance of identity online, especially for questions of race, gender, sexuality, and disability.

candidates.title: Anthropomorphism and emotional reactions to human–AI collaboration.
candidates.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly enters human professional domains , understanding emotional reactions to its involvement becomes critical . We introduce a novel experimental paradigm that distinguishes between AI involvement in “Thinker” and “Doer” roles to examine how the role AI occupies shapes affective and evaluative responses to human–AI collaboration . Across four countries ( N = 1,345), including the United States, the United Kingdom, India, and Colombia, participants evaluated scenarios in which professional jobs were completed under four conditions: human only, full AI automation, human as Thinker with AI as Doer, or AI as Thinker with human as Doer. Our results showed that AI involvement decreased positive affect and appreciation while increasing negative affect . We also found particularly negative emotional reactions to AI executing emotionally charged professions (e.g., artist). Individual differences in AI anthropomorphism consistently moderated these effects. These findings demonstrate that emotional reactions to AI depend on the role it plays and the domain in which it operates. This research highlights the importance of task characteristics and individual differences in understanding human–AI collaboration in professional settings.

candidates.title: Lilo: A Multi-Agent Conversational Sandbox for Children's Digital Communication
candidates.abstract: Children's peer conflicts increasingly play out in group chats, where tone and timing are stripped away, and a hurtful message is easier to send than to say aloud. We present Lilo, a multi-agent conversational system that lets children practice such conversations, so they are better prepared when they encounter them in real digital communication. In Lilo, the child joins two AI-driven peers mid-argument, coached by a mentor character, also named Lilo, through a Stop-Think-Act traffic light. Through an exploratory study with 28 children (aged 9-11), we examine how children engage with Lilo's simulated peer conflict and the mentor's traffic-light interventions. The study included an intervention with Lilo, surveys before and after the intervention, and exit interviews. Participants reported significantly higher self-efficacy for coping with unpleasant messages after their interaction with Lilo. They felt safe experimenting, knowing nothing they wrote would be held against them.

candidates.title: Editorial: Rethinking technology adoption in the age of agentic artificial intelligence
Enabling Robot Learning Through Capable Hardware: Preliminary Studies In Multimodal Tactile Sensing, Bimanual Mobile Manipulation, And Semantic Demonstration Synthesis
candidates.abstract: Physical AI is continuing to advance rapidly, but its current capabilities are limited by the underlying hardware and perception stack. Robot learning, in particular, is often bottlenecked by current sensing capabilities, which limit the amount of information available to the learning algorithm and the range of tasks that can be attempted. Most robotics operations are contact-rich, meaning it requires robotic systems to have robust tactile sensing and whole-body perception to understand the state of the world during grasping and object manipulation. In this thesis, I present how there is a need to develop more capable hardware and perception capabilities to enable robot learning in robotic dexterous manipulation and mobile manipulation. To show this, I discuss how DenseTact sensors can be improved to provide more reliable tactile sensing in robotic end effectors, how we can utilize the TidyBot++ mobile manipulator platform to enable bimanual mobile manipulation research and education, and how we can use a single RGB video of a human performing a manipulation task to generate a large set of robot demonstrations for downstream policy learning. DenseTact is an optical tactile sensor that provides high-resolution tactile sensing for robotic manipulation. It’s current capabilities include shape and force sensing. Currently, it has reliability limitations in terms of its manufacturing process, calibration pipeline, and overall hardware design. Additionally, it lacks the ability to sense vibration and temperature, which are important for many manipulation tasks. As a result, I am presenting the current progress to move DenseTact to be more antrhropomorphic, reliable in manufacturing and calibration, and to have multimodal sensing capabilities. The strategy for this is to introduce a new version of the DenseTact Mini sensor, an automated calibration pipeline that builds on TensorTouch, and prototyping hardware and software for localized vibration and distributed temperature sensing modalities co-localized with the existing shape and force channels. MR. CRABS is a holonomic bimanual mobile manipulator that is built on the open-source TidyBot++ base. It includes two Realsense D435 depth cameras, one of which has an active pan-and-tilt mechanism for near-ground perception. It also includes a top LIDAR for long-range perception. It also utilizes two Trossen Robotics Widow-X arms. MR. CRABS is designed both as a research platform for bimanual mobile manipulation and as the next-generation educational platform for Stanford’s ME 326, replacing the LoCoBots used previously. The more capable hardware proved to be essential to allow students to complete the course’s final project, allowing them to better navigate the scene and perform more complex manipulation tasks that cannot be done with the LoCoBots. I present that more teams were able to complete more of the final project, and the projects were more complex than in previous years. Finally, I present Semantics as a Present (SAP), a demonstration-augmentation pipeline that turns a single RGB video of a human performing a manipulation task into an N ×M set of robot demonstrations spanning a family of pre-scanned cousin objects, with no depth sensor, no teleoperation, and no per-object annotation. The method recovers per-frame SE(3) object pose from RGB alone via distilled-DINO and depth-ranking losses, grafts the recovered motion onto each cousin via regionweighted semantic 3D Gaussian splat alignment, and replays the grafted trajectories in IsaacLab to mint demonstrations for any downstream policy (diffusion policy, ACT, π0). SAP shares its vision front end with the first two contributions, illustrating the thesis’s central claim: that perception-grounded, capable hardware is what enables modern robot learning to translate from benchmarks to real, contact-rich, bimanual, semantically rich tasks. It is compared with human demonstrations collected with an Realsense camera and teleoperation, then trained on a VLA benchmark and evaluated on a real robot to show that it can achieve comparable performance to the human demonstrations. We evaluate SAP on seven different tasks.

candidates.title: Melodramatically Connected: Affective Affinities in the Transcultural Fandom of Turkish Dramas
candidates.abstract: This article explores how online fan communities help viewers to connect to Turkish dramas, giving particular emphasis to women over fifty years old located in Spain. Online fan communities across multiple social media platforms allow fans to share content related to Turkish dramas, and they bring together mainly female fans from Spain and other Spanish-speaking countries. Therefore, I draw on scholarship on transcultural fandom and gender. Observations from a digital ethnography, complemented by in-depth interviews, show that fans bond over shared identity aspects beyond nationality. More specifically, the fandom fosters connections to other fans, to actors, to Turkey, and to titles, which stand out as key motivations for watching Turkish dramas. Findings illustrate how fandom and transnational media flows are intertwined in the expansion of Turkish dramas and other contra-flows of media, highlighting the role of affective affinities in the travel of media content.

candidates.title: SurgPace: Complexity-aware progressive distillation for surgical multimodal large language models
Big Data and Predictive Analytics Capability and Triple Bottom Line Sustainability Performance: A Resource‐Based Perspective From BRICS Nations
candidates.abstract: This study aims to investigate the relationship between big data and predictive analytics (BDPA) capability and triple bottom line (TBL) sustainability performance in BRICS manufacturing firms. Grounded in the resource‐based view (RBV), we conceptualise BDPA capability as a third‐order hierarchical construct comprising tangible resources (data infrastructure and technology), intangible resources (organisational culture, organisational learning and data‐driven culture) and human‐related skills (technical skills and management skills). Survey data have been used from 304 IT and analytics professionals representing different organisations across BRICS economies and partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM) with 5000 bootstrap samples; we test six hypotheses examining both the resource‐capability link and the capability‐performance link. Results reveal that all three resource categories significantly contribute to BDPA capability, with human‐related skills exerting the strongest influence. BDPA capability, in turn, significantly predicts environmental performance, social performance and economic performance, explaining 40%, 50% and 55% of variance, respectively. The study contributes to the literature by providing an empirically validated, multi‐level resource‐capability‐performance framework for analytics‐driven sustainability in emerging economies.

candidates.title: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey of Hardware, Data, Cross-Embodiment Transfer, Learning, and Evaluation
candidates.abstract: Dexterous robotic hands are increasingly coupled to large-scale human data and foundation models, yet progress in hardware, representation learning and evaluation is often assessed separately. This survey reviews work from January 2024 to early November 2026, with earlier studies included to establish technical lineages. We organize the literature into five interdependent layers: hardware; data collection and curation; cross-embodiment transfer; learning and foundation models; and evaluation and applications. Human hand-object understanding and tactile sensing provide two cross-cutting perspectives. A system-level architecture, comparative tables and five case analyses connect design choices across these layers. We distinguish within-study experimental comparisons from heterogeneous corpus statistics, vendor specifications and company-reported results. Three conclusions emerge. First, the value of human data depends on kinematic, visual and contact alignment, not recording volume alone. Second, shared action representations and foundation policies do not remove embodiment-specific constraints on force, latency and contact. Third, task completion is insufficient to establish physical correctness or deployment readiness. Evidence remains limited for zero-shot transfer of contact-rich skills between morphologically different hands, long-duration reliability, and cross-sensor tactile generalization. We identify eleven open problems and propose reporting interfaces and controlled comparisons that can make full-stack progress more measurable. The review is a structured narrative synthesis rather than a pooled performance ranking or an exhaustive systematic review.

candidates.title: Fans for life? Popular culture-inspired tattoos and the challenges of inscribed expressions of fandom
candidates.abstract: This article examines active practices of fandom and identity communication through the collection of fandom-based tattoos. Through an analysis of fan theory, the article argues that fans who express their devotion to media culture through tattooing engage in a distinctive act of active fandom that represents a bodily extension of Rojek’s concept of the fan reliquary, a religiously inspired repository of collected items and artefacts by which fans signify their fandom to inspiration figures (such as Taylor Swift). The article considers the critical issues relating to fans that have used their bodies as tattooed reliquaries, but for whom the designs have become problematic in the wake of negative social actions and cultural reactions towards the objects of the fandom, such as J.K. Rowling. Tattoos, therefore, signify a potent expression of fan identification, but their permanence makes them a risk in an unpredictable landscape of popular and media culture.

candidates.title: Personality expression and perception in large language models and humans
candidates.abstract: Growing numbers of people frequently turn to Large Language Models (LLMs) for concerns from various areas of life. Because its content has become ubiquitous, examining user perceptions of LLM-produced text and its distinguishability from human writing is crucial. This study investigated how seven LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-3.5, Llama 3, Gemma, Gemini, Phi-3, Orca-2) describe themselves when compared to humans. LLM-generated outputs and human responses were collected using psychological questionnaires (Big Five, self-esteem, narcissism) and tailored prompts to elicit short self-descriptive texts. Six LLM and ten human judges then evaluated personality traits and text origin based on these self-descriptions (140 total, half LLM-generated). Results show that current LLM outputs can convey personality-consistent cues in questionnaires and texts. The perception of such significantly differed from that of humans. Both LLM and human judges accurately inferred personality from short self-descriptions and correctly differentiated between LLM-generated and human text. Linguistic analysis and participant feedback revealed textual cues distinguishing LLM-produced from human language and offered insights into how LLM versus human judgment and decisionmaking differ.

candidates.title: The impacts of industrial robot adoption on corporate supply chains and market diversification: Evidence from China's listed firms
The Effect of AI Virtual Influencers on Purchase Intention: The Mediating Role of Parasocial Interaction: A Field Study on the Fashion Industry in Egypt
candidates.abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the effect of AI virtual influencers (VIs); in terms of perceived authenticity and perceived anthropomorphism on Purchase intention, viewing the mediating role of Parasocial interaction, by application on the women fashion industry in Egypt. Questionnaire was used to collect data, and a non-probability purposive sampling technique was adopted. A total of 128 responses were collected and analyzed. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was performed in R using the SEMinR package (version 2.5.0). The findings supported all the proposed direct and indirect hypotheses, concluding that perceived authenticity and anthropomorphism play a vital role in directly influencing purchase intention, and that parasocial interaction also plays an indirect role in mediating this relationship.
