candidates.title: Crafting Persuasive Environmental Messages for Virtual Influencers: The Role of Anthropomorphic Conversational Style, Persuasion Appeal, and Behavioral Context
candidates.abstract: The use of virtual influencers (VIs) has emerged as an alternative to human influencers for marketing initiatives. Prior studies have focused primarily on the visual characteristics of VIs and their use in advertising settings, with limited attention given to their capacity to drive pro-environmental behaviors (PEBs). We have developed an integrated persuasive framework, grounded in the Elaboration Likelihood Model and Congruity Theory, that links VI characteristics, message appeals, and behavioral context to persuasion outcomes. Study 1 examined VI message strategies and found that competence (vs. warmth) anthropomorphic conversational style and influencing (vs. de-influencing) appeal enhanced message persuasiveness. Study 2 explored the effectiveness of VIs in promoting plastic waste reduction behaviors across different behavioral contexts and found that messages pertaining to difficult (vs. easy) and private (vs. public) behaviors significantly enhanced message persuasiveness, but that messages promoting easy and private behaviors generated stronger behavioral intentions. The insights from these studies can provide valuable guidance to businesses, marketers, and environmental advocates on effective VI message strategies for addressing challenges related to climate change.

candidates.title: Sensorium: An Open-Source Multimodal Data Collection and Curation Library for Embodied Surgical AI
candidates.abstract: Embodied surgical AI requires reliable multimodal data, yet surgical data collection remains costly, difficult to repeat, and strongly dependent on the hardware setup. We present Sensorium, an open-source Python library for recording, processing, annotating, and curating multimodal surgical data from configurable robot and sensor streams using the Robot Operating System (ROS) and ROS2 middleware. The library combines operator-facing data acquisition, configurable processing, semantic annotation, and episodic dataset generation. We evaluate Sensorium across 1516 recordings of phantom, ex vivo, and in vivo porcine experiments involving multiple surgical tasks and sensing configurations, and report preliminary usability feedback.

candidates.title: Gaze-Assisted Supervisory Control for Lunar Robotic Arm Teleoperation Under Concurrent Monitoring
candidates.abstract: Rover-mounted robotic arms can extend human reach during lunar sample handling, but continuous joystick teleoperation requires repeated visual-motor alignment while operators may also need to monitor system states. This paper presents a gaze-assisted supervisory control framework in which gaze nominates a rock or placement target, explicit confirmation authorizes the action, and the robot performs bounded autonomous grasp-and-place execution. The framework was evaluated against manual joystick teleoperation in a mission-analog virtual reality study with 16 participants. The study used a 2 x 2 x 3 within-subject design varying control mode, placement difficulty, and concurrent monitoring load. Mean recorded task completion time decreased from 47.65 to 18.43 s per rock, with 72.5% of this difference arising during grasping. Under the tested auditory monitoring conditions, gaze-assisted supervisory control showed less average proportional slowing, with no detected control-mode difference in monitoring-response accuracy or speed. The rate of gaze shifts between core areas of interest decreased from 49.98 to 27.73 shifts/min, while the raw NASA Task Load Index score decreased from 32.54 to 18.26. However, the benefit was task dependent. In precision placement, manual control yielded lower mean placement error and a higher placement success rate. These findings support a mixed-initiative allocation in which gaze enables rapid task-level intention specification and autonomous execution, while precision-critical stages retain manual refinement.

candidates.title: Making Meets Informal Innovation: Formalisation, Access and Openness in Indian Makerspaces
candidates.abstract: Makerspaces and fabrication labs (fablabs) are inclusive and open infrastructures. They democratise access to tools and technologies and facilitate bottom‐up innovation. Research on these spaces thus highlights the importance of openness, community orientation and the ability to foster informal experimentation that these spaces enable. In this paper, I examine how these features have been operationalised in contexts characterised by a high degree of economic and institutional informality by focusing specifically on Indian makerspaces and fablabs. I ask how these spaces relate to need‐driven local innovation practices and how they are sustained. The paper uses qualitative data collected through semi‐structured interviews and analyses the organisation of access, learning and innovation in these spaces. The analysis indicates that makerspaces and fablabs in India do not work as open infrastructures in their entirety. Instead, they serve as mediators between informal innovation practices and institutionalised pathways shaped by an entrepreneurial discourse. The analysis further indicates that they create new limits of participation, expertise and knowledge exchange. The paper contributes to the body of literature on open infrastructures and informal innovations by reconceptualising the notion of openness as a result of governance rather than as a characteristic of such spaces.

candidates.title: Emotional and behavioral asymmetries in user responses to virtual versus human influencers
candidates.abstract: As AI virtual influencers (AIVIs) proliferate, understanding human-AI emotional engagement is vital for advancing affective computing. To examine whether AIVIs evoke comparable affective responses to human influencers (HIs), we analyzed 156,918 Instagram comments that received 12+ million likes, integratinglarge language model (LLM)-derived knowledge graphs, emotion analysis, and machine learning. HI-directed discourse shows more differentiated emotional expression and a pattern consistent with more cohesive semantic networks than AIVI-directed discourse. AIVI-directed comments are less likely to express positive affect (24.8% vs. 41.5%) and also less likely to express negative affect (5.8% vs. 9.3%), indicating reduced affective expression of either valence rather than heightened negativity. This group-level tendency is not uniform: affective engagement varies substantially across AIVIs, and that variation is more closely associated with positive than with negative expression. Our Multi-Signal Embedding Network (MSEN), incorporating behavioral metrics and OpenAI semantic embeddings, classified influencer types from behavioral, affective and semantic features (F1 = 0.89), outperforming baselines including a state-of-the-art zero-shot LLM. These findings identify a boundary condition for the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) paradigm: human-like appearance can elicit social responses without producing affective and semantic response patterns as rich as those elicited by HIs.

candidates.title: ProAct: Harnessing Streaming Motion Generation and Agentic Reasoning for Realtime Embodied Social Interaction
candidates.abstract: Real-time embodied social interaction places two equally demanding requirements on an agent: continuously generating fluent multimodal interaction behavior, and proactively reasoning over accumulated dialogue and visual context to decide when to take initiative. These requirements must both be satisfied under a strict latency budget, making them difficult to meet simultaneously. We present ProAct, a dual-system framework that manages these time-critical requirements by integrating a low-latency Behavioral System for streaming multimodal interaction with a slower Cognitive System that performs long-horizon social reasoning and produces high-level proactive intentions. The Cognitive System incorporates an efficient memory mechanism and a user-motivation prediction module to reason over accumulated dialogue and visual context and determine when proactive intervention is appropriate. The Behavioral System further includes an intention-conditioned streaming flow-matching motion generator with a disentangled Control-Net branch, which translates deliberative intentions into continuous nonverbal behavior without disrupting interaction fluency. We deploy ProAct on a physical humanoid robot and validate the framework through comprehensive experiments, including real-world user studies, motion-generation benchmarks, and evaluation on ProActBench, a new, targeted benchmark for evaluating proactive trigger detection and restraint in embodied interaction. Code and ProActBench will be released at https://proactrobot.github.io/.

candidates.title: Trail: Accurate Local Smart Home Control Using Decision Models
candidates.abstract: Natural-language driven smart home control remains challenging: cloud-hosted Large Language Models (LLMs) raise privacy concerns, while local Small Language Models (SLMs) can generate invalid actions or misinterpret requests. We introduce Trail (Typed Registry-Anchored Inference for Language commands in Smart Homes), a fully local framework that replaces open-ended command generation with hierarchical typed decisions. Trail exploits the natural structure of a home's action space, selecting a room, device, and operation from candidates derived from the runtime device registry. This ensures valid actions while enabling confidence-based abstention when requests cannot be reliably resolved. We also design a structured memory module that uses typed decisions to support user preferences, device references, and multi-turn interactions. To evaluate Trail, we extend HomeBench and generate three datasets: Trek-Base, which tests natural-language variation; Trek-Robust, which evaluates robustness to changes in the home and its description; and Trek-Memory, which assesses conversational memory across multi-turn interactions. Trail achieves 85.3% accuracy on Trek-Robust versus 69.8% for a finetuned Qwen3.5-4B baseline, while remaining competitive on Trek-Base requests. With memory, Trail resolves 75.6% of the requests that depend on earlier turns, compared with 42.5% for the finetuned baseline given conversation history.

candidates.title: The Art of Resourcefulness: Decoding Jugaad in Bottom of the Pyramid Consumer Behavior
candidates.abstract: This pioneering study investigates what drives Bottom of the Pyramid (BOP) consumers to adopt jugaad, a resource‐constrained workaround practice conceptualized here as a form of adaptive consumption that sustains the circular economy, through the lenses of the value‐based adoption model (VAM) and expectancy theory (ET). Across two studies, we uncover the value calculus underlying this behavior. Study 1, a phenomenological analysis of 29 in‐depth interviews with subsistence consumers in eastern India, reveals that adoption decisions hinge on a dynamic trade‐off between two perceived benefits (utilitarian and psychological) and three BOP‐specific perceived sacrifices (opportunity costs, skill constraints, resource limitations). Building on these insights, Study 2 employs the Decision‐Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory method with 10 experts to model causal interrelationships among observed factors. Results identify repair and scarcity as primary drivers, while physical mental strain and time intensity emerge as key barriers. Crucially, jugaad operates paradoxically, as both a coping mechanism and a source of burden, creating a dynamic that facilitates adoption despite its costs. Overall, the findings pioneer value‐based decision‐making in the context of scarcity. Building on these theoretical insights, the study also offers a clear direction for practitioners. Managerially, firms can transform informal resourcefulness into market opportunities by developing repairable, adaptable products that align with BOP consumers' everyday realities and aspirations. For policymakers, the findings illuminate pathways for fostering inclusive circular systems that strengthen consumer capabilities, reduce waste, and enhance community resilience.

candidates.title: Embodied multisensory immersive experiences: a perspective into emerging threats and possible solutions
candidates.abstract: Multisensory immersive virtual reality experiences, encompassing audio, visual, haptic, and/or digital smells and tastes, have been shown to enhance a user’s sense of immersion and embodiment, leading to improved experiences, task performances, and even clinical outcomes. While the great majority of published works tend to highlight the benefits of such embodied experiences, in this perspective-style paper, we shed light on emerging threats that are often overlooked in the literature. Here, we group these threats into four categories: discomfort, safety, privacy and security, and societal issues. We give examples of such threat vectors and discuss potential solutions. Overall, it is hoped that this perspective will help raise awareness of these emerging threats, such that solutions can be developed from the ground up for future embodied experiences.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence Technologies In Digital Radio Broadcasting: Content Creation, Audience Analysis, And Automation Of Broadcasting Processes
candidates.abstract: The rapid advancement of digital technologies has produced fundamental transformations in the media system, and radio broadcasting in particular. The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies into broadcasting practice is redefining how content is prepared, edited, distributed, and used to engage audiences. Employing a qualitative literature review and conceptual-theoretical analysis, this study systematically examines the principal domains in which AI is applied to radio broadcasting: automated news-text generation, speech synthesis, music and content personalization, audience-behavior analytics, and broadcast-process automation. The research situates these developments within an interdisciplinary theoretical framework informed by McLuhan’s medium theory, Rogers’s diffusion of innovations, Diakopoulos’s concept of algorithmic hybridization, Katz and Blumler’s uses-and-gratifications approach, and Habermas’s notion of the public sphere. Comparative case material is drawn from RadioGPT in the United States, the bigGPT project on Germany’s bigFM, will.i.am’s RAiDiO.FYI platform, and the Australian station CADA’s AI host “Thy,” alongside a localized assessment of Azerbaijan’s media landscape through ASAN TV’s virtual presenter Asaniyya. The findings indicate that AI enhances production efficiency, optimizes resource allocation, and enables personalized content delivery, while simultaneously raising unresolved ethical and legal questions concerning transparency, copyright, data privacy, algorithmic bias, and the future of the journalistic profession. The study concludes that a hybrid broadcasting model, grounded in the complementarity of human creativity and machine capability, represents the most sustainable trajectory for the future of radio.

candidates.title: A Generative AI-Driven Architecture for Whole-Home Intelligent Services: Edge Models, Memory Management, and Household Applications
candidates.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is entering the home. Cloud-based assistants face governance limitations in data transmission, continuous availability, and the reliability of physical actions, which are especially salient in households where devices remain online, data accumulate over time, and commands trigger real-world actions. Using the home local server as a unifying organizing axis, this article develops a design-oriented review framework. Sources from arXiv, CNKI, ACL Anthology, and official documentation were searched through November 2026 and coded into five evidence categories: reviews, system prototypes, benchmarks, HCI and eldercare studies, and official documentation. System designs were mapped onto shared architectural modules, identifying nine recurrent responsibilities of the home local server. Generative models support perceptual interpretation, intent understanding, and candidate planning, while deterministic validation, knowledge-graph constraints, and authorization leases confine candidate actions to an inspectable space. Home control, emotional companionship, and intelligent guarding can be compared within a common framework: they share state and memory but differ in latency, false positive and negative rates, proactivity, and permissions. Existing benchmarks rely on virtual environments and cannot substitute for real-deployment evaluation. Local deployment is not inherently safer, and technical continuity alone does not establish the social or medical effects of companionship and guarding. The article proposes a five-dimensional evaluation framework covering architectural capability, system resources, privacy, safety and reliability, and human experience, together with six design principles and a future research agenda for local-first intelligent home systems.

candidates.title: A Teacher–Agent–Robot Collaborative Model for Bilingual Hands-on STEAM Learning: Integrating an LLM-based Pedagogical Agent with Educational Robots
candidates.abstract: In recent years, Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown potential in providing dialog-based guidance and learning prompts in educational contexts. However, systematic empirical research remains limited on approaches that position educational robots as the interaction medium and LLMs as the instructional support engine to orchestrate classroom guidance using prompts and instructional workflow scripts. In response, this study adopted a bilingual STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, the Arts, and Mathematics) summer camp for lower elementary students as the research context, and developed and implemented an R&T (Robots & Tangible Objects) learning system that integrated educational robots with an LLM-based pedagogical agent to foster embodied interaction and bilingual learning. The system used predesigned prompts and procedural rules to organize instructional steps, question prompts, operational checks, and feedback statements, enabling the students to receive consistent and repeatable support at key task-progression checkpoints. A total of 34 elementary students participated in a five-day program (120 minutes per day). Data sources included STEAM knowledge tests, English vocabulary assessments, a curiosity scale, hands-on performance ratings, and system interaction logs. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests indicated significant improvements in the students’ STEAM knowledge, curiosity, and English vocabulary, while group-level analyses showed significant differences in hands-on performance. Process log analyses further suggested that the prompt-guided workflow scripts helped to maintain consistency in classroom guidance and supported task completion through an action–feedback–revision cycle. Nevertheless, classroom implementation was constrained by factors such as token limits, speech-recognition latency, and network/API stability, which indicated the need to incorporate exception handling and timely teacher support mechanisms to ensure instructional continuity. Overall, this study provided initial empirical support for a feasible design framework for integrating educational robots × an LLM-based pedagogical agent into bilingual hands-on STEAM activities, and its findings offer practical recommendations for curriculum adoption and system deployment.

candidates.title: Influence of Chatbots on Consumer Purchase Decision-Making in Luxury Products
candidates.abstract: The rapid introduction of artificial intelligence into digital commerce has altered the way brands interact with their customers, particularly in the luxury sector, where personal contact and exclusivity are essential for adding value. Among the different technologies, chatbots have emerged as important tools since they allow for immediate communication, recommend products, and offer personalized help. This study examines how consumers view chatbots in the context of luxury products and develops a conceptual framework that links the features of chatbots – specifically responsiveness, personalization, anthropomorphism, and interactivity – with customers' intention to make a purchase through the intermediary effects of trust, perceived value, and emotional engagement. Unlike in the case of mass-market buying, luxury consumption is rooted in symbolic value, in the demonstration of status, and in the satisfaction obtained from the experience rather than simply in functionality, so the character of the digital interaction becomes particularly significant. An exploratory quantitative approach is used in the study, with a survey carried out of people who have used chatbot services on luxury websites. A Chi-square test of independence reveals a statistically significant relationship between the perception of chatbot design (to the extent that it appeared robotic) and the perception of ease of navigation, indicating that opinions about design and usability are related rather than independent. Since the sample size is small, this result is regarded as exploratory and indicative rather than conclusive, and the proposed connections between personalization, responsiveness, trust, perceived value, and purchase intention are given as a conceptual framework for future empirical research. The study makes a contribution by connecting research on artificial intelligence in marketing with theories of luxury consumption, thereby offering insights into how technology-based communication can be combined with prestige, craftsmanship, and exclusivity.

candidates.title: From Technological Innovation to Commercialization Building Competitive Advantage in a Robotics Firm: A Case Study of Unitree Robotics
candidates.abstract: This study examines how a robotics manufacturer converts technological resources into commercialization and competitive positioning. Using a longitudinal, embedded single-case design based on public documentary evidence, it analyzes Unitree Robotics’ quadruped and humanoid robot businesses from August 26th, 2016 - the company’s incorporation date, to September 30th, 2026. The analysis combines the resource-based view, dynamic capabilities theory and innovation-commercialization research to examine technological resources, product diversification, manufacturing organization, sales channels and financial outcomes. The evidence indicates substantial revenue growth, a marked shift toward humanoid robots and hybrid production and channel configuration. However, 2026 interim results show that revenue growth coexisted with declines in adjusted net profit and operating cash flow. Public information remains insufficient to establish repeat customer demand, routine industrial deployment or superior unit economics. The study argues that Unitree has developed a significantly emerging commercial position, while the sustainability of its competitive advantage remains conditional on reliable applications, recurring customer value, profitability and cash generation.

candidates.title: Beyond Technocratic Optimism: A Systematic Review of Repair in the Circular Economy
candidates.abstract: Repair is increasingly promoted as a key strategy within the circular economy, yet research on repair remains fragmented. This article provides a systematic review of management and social science research on repair, combining a critical thematic review with bibliometric analysis. We map key features of the field and integrate research streams related to governance, consumer behaviour, repairability, business models and outcomes. Our study shows that the literature is structured around four assumptions related to policy effectiveness, repairability, sustainability outcomes and scalability. By critically examining these assumptions, we challenge the technocratic optimism that dominates the field and reconceptualise repair as a context‐dependent socio‐technical and political‐economic phenomenon shaped by institutional constraints and competing value logics, rather than an inherently beneficial circular economy strategy. We conclude by deriving implications for managers and policymakers and by outlining a research agenda to better understand when and under what conditions repair contributes to circular economy objectives.

candidates.title: From digital companionship to real-world withdrawal: the deep impact of anthropomorphic AI on college students' social interaction and educational responses
candidates.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping mental health services in higher education, and the widespread adoption of anthropomorphic AI is noteworthy. This article employs a literature-based theoretical reasoning approach, integrating parasocial interaction theory, self-determination theory, and uses and gratifications theory to construct a Triggering–Satisfying–Differentiating framework, systematically examining the mechanisms through which anthropomorphic AI affects college students' social psychology. The study finds that AI effectively alleviates loneliness and social anxiety in the short term by enhancing social presence, providing unconditional acceptance, and offering immediate accessibility. However, its "frictionless socializing" experience simultaneously carries three latent risks: substitute gratification weakens motivation for real-world social interaction; idealized interaction raises interpersonal expectation thresholds; and emotional dependence reinforces social avoidance behavior. For students with social anxiety tendencies, the digital haven may evolve from relief to chronic avoidance, hindering essential social skills and resilience. Accordingly, this paper proposes that universities establish "human–AI boundary" awareness, adopt a "reality-first" principle for behavioral guidance, develop connection-promoting AI tools, and build a multi-tiered digital literacy education system. The article aims to provide theoretical and practical pathways for interventions in college students' social development.

candidates.title: Artificial Narrow Intelligence and Organizational Effectiveness in Higher Education: The Parallel Mediating Roles of Technology Acceptance and Organizational Culture
candidates.abstract: Artificial narrow intelligence (ANI) is being embedded into teaching, research administration, and governance faster than management theory can evaluate it, yet empirical evidence on how ANI shapes organizational effectiveness in higher education remains fragmented. This study proposes and tests the ANI Dual-Pathway Framework, in which technology acceptance (TA) and organizational culture (OC) act as parallel mediators linking ANI to the organizational effectiveness (OE) of academic staff. A sequential quantitative-qualitative design combined a structured questionnaire (511 valid responses from 550 distributed; 97.5% effective recovery rate) with 20 semi-structured interviews and focus-group discussions across public, private, and vocational higher education institutions in Beijing. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling, estimated with maximum likelihood and 5000-resample bias-corrected bootstrap for specific indirect effects, were applied. The measurement model was reliable and valid (Cronbach's alpha = 0.914-0.952; KMO = 0.931; CFI = 0.994; RMSEA = 0.015), and the respecified structural model fit well (χ²/df = 1.691; CFI = 0.991; RMSEA = 0.037). ANI had a significant direct effect on OE (β= 0.290). The bootstrap specific indirect effects showed significant indirect effects through TA (β= 0.061) and through OC (β= 0.097). The organizational-culture indirect pathway exhibited a larger effect magnitude relative to the technology-acceptance pathway. Two exploratory propositions regarding socio-technical strain and AI anxiety were examined exclusively using qualitative interview data and were not subjected to quantitative hypothesis testing. Findings indicate that organizational culture constitutes the stronger mediating channel and that investments in trust building and benevolent leadership should accompany technical deployment. Given the cross-sectional nature and geographically bounded sample, causal inferences cannot be definitively established. This work provides evidence-based guidance for higher education managers and policy makers in emerging-economy contexts.

candidates.title: WARMTH, COMPETENCE, OR BOTH? DUAL-PATHWAY CONCEPTUALISATION OF ROBOTIC RESTAURANT ENCOUNTER AND CUSTOMER REVISIT INTENTION
candidates.abstract: Service robots have become a routine presence in restaurants across Asia, yet customer responses to them remain ambivalent. Studies of service robots in hospitality typically bundle the attributes of the machine into a single quality score and regress satisfaction on it. Social cognition research suggests a different structure. People judge any agent, human or artificial, along two largely independent dimensions, competence and warmth, and these dimensions carry different emotional and behavioural consequences. This paper applies that logic to the robotic restaurant encounter and proposes a dual-pathway conceptual model. Robotic service quality and robotic efficiency are specified as competence cues, robotic anthropomorphism and robotic empathy as warmth cues; the two sets of cues form separate appraisals that jointly determine customer satisfaction and, through it, revisit intention. Eight propositions are advanced, including a non-monotonic relationship between anthropomorphism and perceived warmth, and two boundary conditions: cultural service expectations and the utilitarian or hedonic character of the dining occasion. The model offers a way of explaining why robots that perform flawlessly can still disappoint, and it treats the mixed case of a competent but cold robot as the commercially common outcome rather than a measurement anomaly. It also predicts that a service failure met with a warm response will damage satisfaction less than one met with correct but impassive handling. For operators, the framework gives a basis for allocating investment between the two pathways, separating competence attributes fixed at procurement from warmth attributes that can be staged after deployment. For researchers, it specifies a validation strategy combining experimental manipulation with survey-based estimation.

candidates.title: IDEOLOGICAL LUDONARRATIVE AND THE IMAGE OF THE “ENEMY” IN FPS VIDEO GAMES ANALYSIS OF CALL OF DUTY, MODERN WARFARE, ATOMIC HEART, AND ESCAPE FROM TARKOV
candidates.abstract: First-person shooter (FPS) games have evolved from military simulations into popular entertainment, making them powerful tools for cultural and political messaging. When set against the backdrop of contemporary armed conflicts, these games often reinforce national viewpoints by presenting specific, biased interpretations of history. Given the ongoing tensions between Russia and the West—intensified by the 2022 Russian-Ukrainian conflict—this article investigates video games as active participants in “hybrid warfare” and as key objects for critical media literacy. The study evaluates two distinct approaches to narrative: the pro-Western storylines in the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare series and the pro-Russian, self-referential perspectives found in Atomic Heart and Escape from Tarkov. By examining how the “enemy” is constructed and how conflict is framed, this article evaluates whether these ludic elements function as ideological artifacts that reinforce stereotypes and facilitate the dissemination of propaganda. Data for this study was collected through a multi-staged approach. First, primary ludonarrative content was extracted from official gameplay and cinematic sequences. To ensure comprehensiveness, this was supplemented by data from community-maintained databases (Fandom wikis). These databases serve as repositories of verified game documentation, including dialogue transcripts, character archetypes, and quest structures. The study aims to show that FPS games are not neutral; they are active platforms for political construction that shape players perception. Consequently, media literacy must prioritize the study of these games to better understand how digital entertainment functions as a modern tool for influence and reeducation.

candidates.title: HomeLoop: A Simulation Framework and Benchmark for Robot-IoT Coordination in Everyday Domestic Assistance and Safety
candidates.abstract: Recent progress in embodied robotics is bringing robots closer to deployment in homes, as vision-language models (VLMs) are demonstrating significant advances in reasoning, making VLM-driven robots promising home assistant agents. These agents will often be introduced into homes that already have cameras, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, and residents with wearables. To fulfill their potential, they need to integrate with existing smart infrastructure and reason through ambiguous scenarios: a smoke alarm may come from a pan about to ignite, a pan already on fire, a resident cooking or a faulty sensor, and each calls for a different response. To that end, we introduce HomeLoop, a simulation framework and benchmark built on Isaac Sim that combines robot bodies, networked devices and wearables, simulated residents and visitors, faulty sensors, and hazards that evolve over time. Our benchmark is composed of 20 tasks across five families grounded in real-world household hazards and needs, and designed so that the same alert can have different causes. A runtime monitor scores each episode with temporal-logic checks on the final outcome and the actions along the way, and every action carries a predefined cost. We evaluate six open-weight and proprietary VLMs. The best achieves a family-balanced score of 61.9%, and across models we see a pattern of over-reaction: failed episodes involving prohibited interventions outnumber those involving missed required interventions by more than two to one, with models often shutting off the stove before investigating the alarm's cause. HomeLoop is an extensible foundation intended for use in research on robot-IoT coordination, long-term memory, proactive assistance, and privacy-safety trade-offs. HomeLoop will be released with 2,100 home layouts that can be automatically furnished in diverse configurations, five robot bodies and 20 networked device types.

candidates.title: AffectiveVLA: Safe and Intent-Aware VLA Control for Human-Humanoid Social Interaction
candidates.abstract: Social touch interactions, such as handshakes, fist bumps, and hugs, require humanoid robots to infer human intent, generate contact-rich motions, and maintain safe physical contact. We present AffectiveVLA, an intent-gated Vision-Language-Action (VLA) pipeline deployed on a Unitree G1 humanoid with dexterous hands. A lightweight RGB-based model recognizes interaction intent from two onboard cameras and converts it into a language prompt for the VLA policy. Low-confidence predictions suppress motion execution, reducing unintended activations. During physical contact, interaction-specific compliance profiles adjust arm impedance, while an independent voice-triggered mechanism initiates a latched safe-stop procedure. Using VR teleoperation, we collected approximately 1,300 multimodal interaction episodes and fine-tuned four VLA models: GR00T, RLDX-1, Being-H0.5, and UnifoLM-VLA-0. On-robot evaluation identifies GR00T as the best-performing standalone model. Integrating intent recognition increases its macro-F1 score from 0.75 to 0.90, while the intent model achieves a p95 inference latency of 6.27 ms. These results demonstrate that explicit intent gating improves the reliability of VLA-based social interaction without compromising real-time operation.

candidates.title: LIVING ENGLISH THROUGH K-POP: AN IPA STUDY OF INDONESIAN EFL LEARNERS' ACQUISITION EXPERIENCES
candidates.abstract: The growth of digital media and online fan communities has opened informal spaces in which Indonesian EFL learners encounter and use English outside formal classroom instruction. K-Pop fandom is one such space, where fans of diverse linguistic backgrounds communicate largely in English through platforms such as TikTok, Instagram, X, and Weverse. However, little is known about the specific kind of English input this communicative interaction provides, or about how Indonesian EFL learners themselves make sense of their acquisition experiences within this informal context. This study addressed two research questions: (1) what kind of language input is found in K-Pop fandom communicative interaction, and (2) how do Indonesian EFL learners perceive their English acquisition experiences through K-Pop fandom practices. Sixteen Indonesian K-Pop fans with five to ten years of fandom involvement and varying levels of communicative activity participated. Data were drawn from documentation of fandom social media interaction across multiple platforms and from semi-structured interviews analyzed through Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA). Results show that fandom input is layered and multimodal, combining lexical, pragmatic, discourse-level, and multimodal features that typically co-occur. Learners' lived experiences were represented by five group experiential themes: a non-linear shift from anxiety toward confidence, differentiated parasocial motivation, varying degrees of social participation, a perceived functional contrast between fandom-based and classroom-based language use, and a partial, domain-specific reconstruction of self-identity as an English user. These findings suggest that K-Pop fandom functions as a rich but internally differentiated informal English acquisition space, with practical implications for educators who may integrate authentic fan-generated texts as supplementary material while continuing to provide structured speaking practice that fandom-based exposure does not reliably supply. ABSTRAK Perkembangan media digital dan komunitas fandom daring telah menciptakan ruang informal baru bagi pembelajar EFL Indonesia untuk menemukan dan menggunakan bahasa Inggris di luar pembelajaran kelas formal. K-Pop fandom merupakan salah satu ruang tersebut, tempat penggemar dari berbagai latar belakang bahasa berkomunikasi terutama dalam bahasa Inggris melalui platform seperti TikTok, Instagram, X, dan Weverse. Namun, masih sedikit yang diketahui mengenai jenis input bahasa Inggris yang tersedia melalui interaksi komunikatif tersebut, maupun bagaimana pembelajar EFL Indonesia memaknai pengalaman pemerolehan bahasa mereka dalam konteks informal ini. Penelitian ini menjawab dua pertanyaan: (1) jenis input bahasa apa yang ditemukan dalam interaksi komunikatif K-Pop fandom, dan (2) bagaimana pembelajar EFL Indonesia mempersepsikan pengalaman pemerolehan bahasa Inggris mereka melalui praktik K-Pop fandom. Enam belas penggemar K-Pop Indonesia dengan pengalaman fandom lima hingga sepuluh tahun dan variasi tingkat keterlibatan komunikatif menjadi partisipan. Data diperoleh dari dokumentasi interaksi media sosial fandom dan wawancara semi-terstruktur yang dianalisis menggunakan Interpretative Phenomenological Analysis (IPA). Hasil menunjukkan bahwa input fandom bersifat berlapis dan multimodal, mencakup fitur leksikal, pragmatik, wacana, dan multimodal yang umumnya muncul bersamaan. Pengalaman hidup pembelajar direpresentasikan melalui lima tema pengalaman kelompok: pergeseran non-linear dari kecemasan menuju kepercayaan diri, motivasi parasosial yang terdiferensiasi, variasi tingkat partisipasi sosial, kontras fungsional antara penggunaan bahasa berbasis fandom dan kelas formal, serta rekonstruksi identitas diri sebagai pengguna bahasa Inggris yang bersifat parsial dan spesifik ranah. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa K-Pop fandom berfungsi sebagai ruang pemerolehan bahasa Inggris informal yang kaya namun terdiferensiasi, dan implikasinya bagi pendidik adalah bahwa teks autentik berbasis fandom dapat diintegrasikan sebagai bahan ajar pelengkap sambil tetap menyediakan latihan berbicara terstruktur yang tidak dapat dipenuhi oleh keterlibatan fandom semata.

candidates.title: Older adults’ social responses to AI virtual humans in digital kinship contexts: associations of loneliness, perceived cues and appraisals with purchase intention
candidates.abstract: As AI virtual humans become increasingly prominent communicative actors on short-video platforms, digital kinship content characterized by kinship-based forms of address, family narratives, caring expressions, and companionship-oriented interaction has begun to enter older adults' everyday media use and become intertwined with commercial recommendation. Selectively drawing on the three-factor theory of anthropomorphism and integrating it with the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) paradigm, this study conceptualizes loneliness as a manifestation of sociality motivation; emotional appeal, human likeness, and homophily as perceived cues and appraisals associated with elicited agent knowledge; and social presence and empathy as proximal social responses within the CASA framework. It examines older adults' social perceptions of and emotional responses to kinship-oriented AI virtual humans and their associations with purchase intention. Using a standardized set of AI virtual human short videos representing key features of digital kinship content as stimuli, we collected valid data from 372 Chinese adults aged 65 years and older and employed partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) as parallel and complementary analytical approaches. The PLS-SEM results revealed distinct antecedent patterns for the two proximal responses. Emotional appeal showed the strongest association with social presence, whereas homophily was more strongly associated with empathy than with social presence. Human likeness was significantly associated only with social presence, while loneliness was positively associated with both responses. Empathy showed a stronger association with purchase intention than social presence, and all indirect associations were significant except the pathway from human likeness through empathy. The fsQCA results further showed that the combination of emotional appeal and empathy constituted the most stable configuration associated with high purchase intention, whereas loneliness emerged as a core condition only when homophily was also present. This study provides empirical evidence for understanding perceptions of social presence and empathy in later-life human-AI relational perception and offers practical implications for the governance of kinship-oriented AI commercial content and the protection of older consumers.

candidates.title: Reality and Perceptual Gaps in Expressive Swarm Robotics
candidates.abstract: Moving robot swarms from simulation into the physical world can be difficult because small discrepancies in hardware, timing and communication can cascade across interacting robots and alter group behaviour. This challenge is known as the reality gap. When swarms operate in human environments, a second challenge emerges: a perceptual gap between what the swarm physically does and what human onlookers actually perceive. This study examines the same decentralised coordination code deployed across three robotic swarms-tabletop, aerial and human-scale mobile manipulators-during live artistic performances. We find that while the underlying algorithms executed reliably on all three platforms, physical embodiment drastically altered visible motion-distorting execution timescales by more than a factor of three and reshaping trajectory geometry. More importantly, audience surveys revealed that human interpretation does not mirror technical success: how observers attribute meaning (perceived purpose) and how they react emotionally (comfort versus threat) depend heavily on physical form. Meaning attribution and emotional responses did not vary together. Our results demonstrate that successfully transferring swarm software to physical hardware is insufficient for real-world deployment. Addressing the reality gap does not guarantee that the resulting collective motion will be readily interpreted by human observers. Swarms destined for human environments must be engineered not only for decentralised stability but also for the expressive physical dynamics through which humans interpret collective motion.

candidates.title: A preliminary design framework for human-friendly AI interaction: grounded in anthropomorphism
candidates.abstract: People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversation, grounded in an understanding of human cognitive functioning. The proposed framework provides both AI providers and designers with an initial structure for shaping and improving the quality of human-friendly interaction.

candidates.title: Path Dependence in the Development of Surgery in China: From Neolithic Trepanation to Minimally Invasive and Robotic Surgery
candidates.abstract: Background The history of surgery in China has often been interpreted through two partial narratives: modern surgery as a nineteenth-century Western import, and ancient Chinese surgery as originating from Hua Tuo and mafeisan. Both perspectives identify important milestones, but neither fully explains why early operative practices existed in China while safe, reproducible, and scalable major surgery emerged only much later through hospitals, anesthesia, asepsis, professional teams, and health-system infrastructure. Objective This study aims to reinterpret the development of surgery in China through path dependence theory, explaining how empirical intervention, textual external medicine, hospital-based surgery, minimally invasive techniques, and robotic innovation formed historically layered surgical pathways. Methods This study applies path dependence theory and historical institutionalism. It synthesizes archaeological evidence, early Chinese medical manuscripts, classical external-medicine texts, hospital and anesthesia history, surgical literature, health-system studies, workforce and hospital-operations research, and contemporary regulatory materials. The analysis focuses on initial path formation, self-reinforcement, institutional layering, lock-in, critical junctures, and path creation. Results Chinese surgery developed through seven interconnected phases: prehistoric empirical intervention from approximately 3000 to 168 BCE; Han-period textualization of external and invasive therapies between 168 BCE and 145 CE; the symbolic but discontinuous breakthrough of Hua Tuo and mafeisan; imperial stabilization of traditional external medicine from 652 to 1835 CE; modern hospital-based surgery from 1835 to 1949 CE; post-1949 state-building and specialist expansion from 1949 to 1978 CE; and reform-era minimally invasive surgery, robotics, and domestic device innovation from 1978 to the present. These phases show that Chinese surgery did not evolve as a simple linear progression, but through layered institutional pathways shaped by texts, risk, hospitals, state capacity, professional training, technology, regulation, and industrial systems. Conclusions Surgery in China was neither merely a late Western import nor a continuous extension of ancient anesthesia-associated surgery. It was a path-dependent process in which operative capacity became safe, teachable, governable, and scalable only when technical practices were embedded in institutions, teams, infrastructures, financing, regulation, and public trust. This historical perspective highlights the need to evaluate contemporary minimally invasive and robotic surgery not only as technological progress, but also as a governance challenge involving safety, equity, workforce sustainability, and regional surgical capacity.

candidates.title: The 2026 State of Open Source in Financial Services: Fintech Open Source Foundation (FINOS)
candidates.abstract: The financial services sector is managing a balancing act between rapid AI adoption with enterprise risk. Now in its sixth year, this annual industry report produced by FINOS and LF Research and in partnership with GitHub, Scott Logic, and sponsor BrightQuery, delivers definitive data on industry adoption and risk management in the era of modern AI. Key findings from the survey include: financial sector GitHub commits jumped 63% year-over-year 58% of institutions now operate an OSPO While 88% credit open source with faster delivery, 52% cite security and privacy as the primary barrier to production AI. To overcome adoption hurdles, leaders must treat open source as a governed discipline and pool resources around shared standards. Read the full report now to benchmark your strategy!

candidates.title: Fan Fiction as Literary Resistance: Rewriting Orwell’s 1984 in Katherine Bradley’s The Sisterhood
candidates.abstract: This article examines how Katherine Bradley’s The Sisterhood works as a fan fictional rewriting of George Orwell’s 1984 and challenges the established canonical narrative while also introduces new alternative possibilities within the canonical fictional world of Oceania. In the light of Henry Jenkins concepts of participatory culture, and collective intelligence, this article analyzes Bradley’s use of fan fiction practices such as reimagination, rewriting, alternative ending, alternative universe, second lead, and canon divergence. This article further explores how being a fan text, The Sisterhood engages in intertextual dialogue with Orwell’s 1984. The significance of this study lies in its exploration of the relatively under examined feminist dimension of fan fiction. It extends the discussion beyond online fan communities to written literary discourse, demonstrating how fan fiction theory can be applied to literary rewritings beyond its conventional context of online practices. This article thus positions fan fiction as a significant literary practice.

candidates.title: Viral Memes as Generators of a Distinct Gen Z Lexicon
candidates.abstract: Viral internet memes have emerged as a primary engine of lexical innovation, forging a distinct, multimodal vocabulary that defines Generation Z’s communicative identity. Operating at the intersection of visual semiotics, algorithmic amplification, and participatory culture, memes accelerate the lifecycle of neologisms—transforming ephemeral image-text templates into durable lexical items such as Rizz, Skibidi, Delulu, Gyatt, and No Cap. These forms circulate through platforms whose recommendation systems reward repetition and engagement, compressing traditional processes of language change into weeks or months and enabling rapid diffusion from niche online communities into mainstream usage and even dictionary recognition. Drawing on recent corpus-based and discourse-analytic research, this article examines memes as productive linguistic systems that generate hybrid registers, semantic shifts, and in-group codes. It demonstrates how multimodal recombination, inter textual play, and platform affordances produce not merely slang but a generative grammar of digital expression—one that constructs generational identity, enacts social distinction, and resists institutional standardization. By situating meme linguistics within broader theories of cultural transmission and algorithmic mediation, the study reveals that Gen Z’s lexicon is neither ephemeral noise nor linguistic decline, but a sophisticated, high-velocity adaptation to the attention economy. The resulting vocabulary functions as both cultural capital and cognitive shorthand, reshaping how meaning, affect, and belonging are negotiated in contemporary digital life.

candidates.title: Helping Dementia Patients Find Comfort: Tom Stevens, Founder of Tombot
candidates.abstract: Inspired by his experience caring for his mother with Alzheimer's disease, entrepreneur Tom Stevens founded Tombot to create a realistic robotic companion for people with dementia and others who cannot care for a live pet. Developed with input from hundreds of seniors and animatronic expertise from Jim Henson's Creature Shop, Tombot's robotic puppy Jennie combines lifelike movement, touch response, and sound to encourage emotional attachment. In this article, Stevens discusses the engineering challenges behind Jennie, Tombot's path from startup to commercialization, and his goal of using technology to provide comfort, companionship, and improved quality of life.

candidates.title: Mapping the Industry 5.0-Oriented Enablers for Driving Organisational Operational Performance Excellence
candidates.abstract: Although Industry 4.0 promotes organisational efficiency, it has ignored or misunderstood many prevailing concerns to drive operational performance in industrial operations. While the desired operational performance value of Industry 5.0 (I5.0) is well recognised, how the same can be delivered through the lens of its enablers has not been explored. The present study fills this knowledge gap by first identifying I5.0-oriented enablers that drive operational performance, then grouping them into legitimate categories, and then prioritising them, so organisations can focus on the critical enablers for operational performance. The enablers were first identified from the literature and then grouped into legitimate categories using content analysis of the literature. The enablers were then prioritised using grey relational analysis (GRA) and further validated using the best-worst method (BWM). The study also provides the technological, organisational, and environmental (TOE) framework of the identified enablers that facilitate the path to drive organisational sustainability. The study finds that management-related (MR) and finance and knowledge-related (FKR) barriers are key enablers that must be prioritised to realise operational excellence from the perspective of I5.0. The findings of the present study drive implications for practitioners by fostering a deeper understanding of enablers for driving operational performance in routine tasks. Furthermore, the TOE framework facilitates decision-makers by enhancing workforce readiness and fostering stakeholders' collaboration for achieving sustainable resilience and human-centric operations.

candidates.title: Transforming Science with Large Language Models: A Survey on AI-assisted Scientific Discovery, Experimentation, Content Generation, and Evaluation
candidates.abstract: With the advent of large multimodal language models, science is now at a threshold of an AI-based technological transformation. An emerging ecosystem of models and tools aims to support researchers throughout the scientific lifecycle, including (1) searching for relevant literature, (2) generating research ideas and conducting experiments, (3) producing text-based content, (4) creating multimodal artifacts such as figures and diagrams, and (5) evaluating scientific work, as in peer review. In this survey, we provide a curated overview of literature representative of the core techniques, evaluation practices, and emerging trends in AI-assisted scientific discovery. Across the five tasks outlined above, we discuss datasets, methods, results, evaluation strategies, limitations, and ethical concerns, including risks to research integrity through the misuse of generative models. We aim for this survey to serve both as an accessible, structured orientation for newcomers to the field, as well as a catalyst for new AI-based initiatives and their integration into future “AI4Science” systems.

candidates.title: Opening Musical Creativity? Embedded Ideologies in Generative AI Music Systems
candidates.abstract: AI systems for music generation are increasingly common and easy to use, granting people without any musical background the ability to create music. Because of this, generative-AI has been marketed and celebrated as a means of democratizing music making. However, inclusivity often functions as marketable rhetoric rather than a genuine guiding principle in these industry settings. In this paper, we look at four generative-AI music making systems available to the public as of mid-2025 (AIVA, Stable Audio, Suno, and Udio) and track how they are rhetoricized by their developers, and received by users. Our aim is to investigate ideologies that are driving the early-stage development and adoption of generative-AI in music making, with a particular focus on democratization. A combination of autoethnography and digital ethnography is used to examine patterns and incongruities in rhetoric when positioned against product functionality. The results are then collated to develop a nuanced, contextual discussion. The shared ideology we map between producers and consumers is individualist, globalist, techno-liberal, and ethically evasive. It is a 'total ideology' which obfuscates individual responsibility, and through which the nature of music and musical practice is transfigured to suit generative outcomes.

candidates.title: TARMAC as a taxonomy for robot manipulation in chemistry
candidates.abstract: Laboratory automation has benefited substantially from well-defined protocols and machine-readable representations of chemical procedures. Yet a long tail of context-dependent physical tasks, including setup, adjustment, and cleanup, continues to require manual intervention or bespoke robotic implementations tailored to individual workflows and platforms. This study examines whether this apparent diversity can be organized into a structured and reusable action space. TARMAC (TA xonomy for R obot MA nipulation in C hemistry), an empirical taxonomy of laboratory actions, is derived through a bottom-up analysis of instructional chemistry practice. The taxonomy comprises 18 physically meaningful primitives organized by three dimensions: wrench dependence, actuation directness, and motion periodicity. Evaluation through cross-corpus protocol decomposition and robotic instantiation addresses expressive coverage and proof-of-concept executability. Across 23 procedures, 904 of 917 manipulative steps map to the primitive set, while robotic tests instantiate 8 primitives in five tasks across four robotic configurations. Together, these results indicate that laboratory manipulation can be organized as a structured action space across the examined contexts. TARMAC therefore provides a descriptive basis for organizing and comparing manipulation requirements across experimental workflows and robotic embodiments.

candidates.title: MOSAIC: Unveiling the Moral, Social and Individual Dimensions of Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in sensitive applications including psychological support, healthcare, and high-stakes decision-making. Existing evaluation benchmarks rely almost exclusively on Moral Foundation Theory (MFT), neglecting other key dimensions such as social values, personality traits, and individual characteristics that shape human ethical reasoning. We introduce øurbenchmark , the first large-scale benchmark designed to jointly assess the mo ral, s ocial, a nd i ndividual c haracteristics of LLMs. øurbenchmark comprises nine validated questionnaires drawn from moral philosophy, psychology, and social theory, alongside four platform-based games designed to probe morally ambiguous scenarios, totaling over 600 curated items. We validate the benchmark across six models from different families, providing empirical evidence that MFT alone is insufficient for comprehensive ethical evaluation of LLMs. All resources are publicly available.

candidates.title: RoboARCade: Benchmarking Agentic Robot Control
candidates.abstract: Improvements in multi-modal capabilities have enabled agents to act directly as robot policies, a setting we refer to as agentic robot control (ARC). We introduce RoboARCade, a benchmark of long-horizon manipulation tasks across three embodiments designed to test in-context adaptation, memory, and reasoning for precise control. The tasks build on existing open-source benchmarks, which we make harder by widening the range of initial conditions. RoboARCade is easy to use and extend: all tasks run on a single simulation backend, MuJoCo, each task is a self-contained data pack, and agents connect through interchangeable interfaces, so new tasks, agents, and interfaces can be added independently. The benchmark separates leading agents: GPT-6 Astra achieves 49.8% compared with 43.6% for Claude Fable 5.1, leaving substantial room for improvement. Comparing two interfaces, we find that a richer visual interface adds only 1.5 to 6.8 points at 1.7 to 2.3 times the cost. Failures stem mostly from choosing a poor manipulation strategy or executing a good one imprecisely, rarely from misunderstanding the scene, and agents incorrectly claim success on 24% to 39% of attempted subtasks. Agents can also improve without human input: one successful demonstration in context raises Astra's score from 53.5% to 73.0% on a five-task subset, and a prompt the agent writes and revises itself reaches 72.0%. Code, videos and full traces are available at roboarcade.org.

candidates.title: Building a robotic self
candidates.abstract: I wake up in the morning, I see my hand and I know it is me. This seemingly simple skill lies at the foundation of our agentive selves. We assume that the development of the self, in both biological and synthetic agents, is grounded in sensorimotor embodiment and inductive learning biases, as well as in the principle of predictive coding. Here, we explore the core inductive biases and process components for building a robotic minimal self. We propose that the formation of a hierarchical, generative model of the self is driven by active inference processes that interactively infer both an endogenous contextual frame and behaviour within this frame. Accordingly, experimental implementations in humanoid robots show how body ownership and agency can develop as foundational computational components. This work on building a robotic minimal self outlines future research directions in mechanistic modelling of the development of an artificial self. To probe the depth of this development, we sketch out embodied Turing tests that challenge complex problem-solving skills, as well as social intelligence and theory of mind. We suggest that uncertainty resolution and the social domain may be promising avenues for further research in the near future. This article is part of the discussion meeting issue 'From being to identity: analysis and synthesis of the self'.

candidates.title: LLMs as MDP Designers: A Dependency-Aware Agentic Framework for Automated Robot Policy Generation
candidates.abstract: We investigate the automated generation of executable robot reinforcement learning (RL) policies from natural-language task descriptions. Rather than using large language models (LLMs) as execution-time decision makers, we use them as designers that construct RL pipelines before deployment, including Markov decision process (MDP) formulation and simulator implementation. We identify a phase-wise structure in this problem: MDP formulation is dependency-structured and sequential, whereas simulator implementation becomes modular once the formulation is fixed. Based on this structure, we propose ARPG, a dependency-aware agentic framework that performs sequential MDP modeling, localized verification and correction, and simulator-structured implementation while externalizing intermediate artifacts. ARPG targets a key failure mode of automated policy generation: executable code may still yield non-learnable policies when state, action, reward, and termination artifacts are not semantically aligned. Experiments in Isaac Sim show that ARPG improves modeling correctness, environment executability, and policy-generation success compared with monolithic LLM baselines and off-the-shelf agentic systems. Additional demonstrations on custom robotics, standard RL, and engineering-domain MDPs further suggest that the same modeling pipeline can be reused beyond the main benchmark suite.

candidates.title: A Taxonomy of Mental Health and Technology Needs for Alzheimer’s and Dementia Caregivers
candidates.abstract: Family members caring for individuals with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (AD/ADRD) provide the foundation of long-term care worldwide. In 2023, more than 11 million U.S. family and friends contributed 18 billion hours of unpaid care, often at the cost of their own physical and mental health. These informal caregivers-also referred as the "invisible second patients"-experience elevated rates of mental health problems. Yet research commonly reduces their complex psychosocial experiences to a single construct of caregiver burden, obscuring which specific needs are unmet or effectively supported. At the same time, digital and AI-enabled technologies are rapidly expanding, from smartphone apps and videoconferencing to sensor platforms and AI chatbots. However, the absence of shared frameworks across medicine, psychology, and technology research limits cumulative progress. This study introduces a Caregiver Mental Health and Technology Taxonomy that systematically links AD/ADRD caregiver needs with corresponding classes of technology-based interventions. Drawing from an interdisciplinary literature review and two qualitative studies with caregivers, the taxonomy identifies mismatches between caregiver priorities and existing technological support, highlights under-served domains such as relational strain and compassion fatigue, and proposes design directions for adaptive, responsive systems. The framework offers a shared vocabulary to guide clinicians, researchers, and technology designers in developing more person-centered and clinically grounded innovation in dementia care. Supplementary Information: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s12126-026-09686-4.

candidates.title: Arcadian: Open-Source Humanoid Ecosystem for Accessible and Customizable Research and Education
candidates.abstract: Reproducing and modifying a meter-scale humanoid remains challenging for research and teaching groups with limited fabrication resources and engineering support. This paper presents Arcadian, an open-source humanoid ecosystem that offers accessible and customizable humanoid hardware and software with community support. Arcadian aims to strike a balance among cost-effectiveness, structural durability, and full customizability, lowering the barrier to entry for research and education. Specifically, this meter-scale humanoid adopts metal-embedded 3D printing to achieve a high strength-to-cost ratio, eliminating the need for computer numerical control (CNC) machining while retaining design flexibility. Extensive simulation and hardware tests validate the design: a reinforcement-learning (RL) locomotion policy trained in simulation transfers to the hardware, and a virtual reality (VR) teleoperation interface drives both arms for simple manipulation tasks. The robot is around one meter tall and costs approximately $6,800 to build. All computer-aided design (CAD) models, the bill of materials, assembly documentation, and training and deployment code are publicly released, distributed through Tnkr.ai and MakerWorld and supported by a Discord server and a project forum through which community feedback informs design updates. The ecosystem resources are available at https://anonymous-humanoid.gitbook.io/docs.

candidates.title: TECHNO-DRAMATURGY AND DRAMATURGY FOR DEVICES: THINKING TECHNOLOGY THROUGH THE THEATRΕ WITH ULRIKE QUADE
candidates.abstract: This article examines how technology influences the practices of creating theatre and dance, and consequently, impacts dramaturgy. It does so through the lens of the work of theatre maker Ulrike Quade. It discusses the intersection of dramaturgy and technology from two perspectives. Part 1 on techno-dramaturgy looks at how Quade thinks technology through the theatre, how the incorporation of technology in her creative practice opens new possibilities for showing and telling in the theatre, and also places new demands on doing dramaturgy as attending to creative processes and what comes about within them. Part 2 examines how theatrical practices of making, as thinking-through-practice, can inform the development of technology and how this can inform further expansions of dramaturgical practice towards what I have termed dramaturgy for devices.

candidates.title: From Virtual to Valuable: How Influencer Type and Product Type Shape Consumer Value Co‐Creation Intention
candidates.abstract: Virtual and human influencers offer distinct social and experiential cues, but their relative effectiveness may depend on how consumers evaluate the endorsed product. Drawing on the cognitive‐affective‐behavioral framework, this research integrates social information processing theory and cognitive‐affective system theory to examine consumer value co‐creation intention. Across three between‐subjects experiments (N = 994), results reveal a consistent matching effect: virtual influencers have a relative advantage for search products, whereas human influencers have a relative advantage for experience products. This matching effect operates through parasocial interaction and empathy: forming a parasocial representation may make an influencer's perspective and affective cues more accessible, providing a relational basis for subsequent empathy. Consistent with this sequence, both the indirect effect through parasocial interaction and the serial indirect effect through parasocial interaction and empathy follow this product‐dependent pattern across both product categories, whereas the indirect effect through empathy alone favors human influencers only for experience products. Together, these findings identify product type as a boundary condition linking relational and affective processes to consumer value co‐creation intention, offering practical insights for aligning influencer selection with product characteristics.

candidates.title: Sacred Space, Musical Experience and Narrative Performance — A Study of the Arts-Therapy Mechanism of the Tujia "Huan Yuan Nuo" (Votive Nuo) Ritual Drama in Xiangxi
candidates.abstract: The Tujia nuo opera in Xiangxi is a comprehensive ritual art integrating sacrifice, drama, music and dance, and its "Huan Yuan Nuo" (Votive Nuo) ritual contains rich folk healing wisdom. This article takes the Tujia "Huan Yuan Nuo" of Xiangxi as its object of study. Combining fieldwork with documentary research, it examines the operational logic of the ritual's healing mechanism from the interdisciplinary perspective of arts therapy. The study finds that the Tujia "Huan Yuan Nuo" achieves its healing function through a fourfold mechanism. Survival anxiety acts as the generative motive and constitutes the psychological foundation of nuo opera healing. Sacred space provides the field-based foundation, evoking a sense of security and belonging by means of sympathetic magic and the collective unconscious. Musical experience serves as the guiding mechanism, achieving emotional catharsis and transformation through the ISO principle. Narrative performance offers spiritual support, providing encouragement and cultural identity through archetypal narrative and comic performance. The study shows that the healing practice of Tujia nuo opera is a kind of "cultural psychotherapy" rooted in the local belief system. It can provide important ethnic cultural resources for the localized development of modern arts therapy.

candidates.title: Character Design for Ludic Hybrid Environments: New Possibilities for Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion
candidates.abstract: As digital media and interactive technologies continue to grow, hybrid environments—where physical and virtual spaces intersect—are becoming more common. Within these spaces, character design plays an important role in shaping how users interact and how cultures are represented. This study explores how thoughtful character design can support equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) through the lens of convergence culture. When creators intentionally embed EDI principles into their work, hybrid environments can become more inclusive, encourage empathy, and reduce divides between real and digital worlds. The paper concludes by offering socially responsible design guidelines that can inform future developments in character design.

candidates.title: TuringPAI: A Foundation for On-Device Physical AI
candidates.abstract: Physical AI requires models that understand spatial relationships and dynamic environments and translate observations into actions under limited onboard compute. We present TuringPAI, a family of models for on-device Physical AI comprising TuringPAI-VL for shared vision-language understanding, TuringPAI-Drive for autonomous driving, and TuringPAI-Embodied for robotic manipulation. TuringPAI-VL is a 0.65B model built on HybridViT-MLQ, which combines convolutional local aggregation with Transformer-based global modeling. Multi-scale Latent Queries integrate spatial features and observation history within the same visual Transformer, providing a compact, structured interface to the language model. Training combines general vision-language data with geometric, cross-view, and temporal supervision. TuringPAI-VL supports general multimodal understanding and improves quantitative geometric perception over Qwen2-VL-2B, while providing a shared initialization for the two downstream VLA models. For autonomous driving, TuringPAI-Drive maintains all evaluated ADE/FDE metrics within 1.2\% of a full-token HybridViT baseline using the MLQ interface and achieves comparable aggregate scores in an in-house simulation evaluation. Using XPeng Native Runtime (XNRT) on a single NVIDIA Orin-X SoC, TuringPAI-Drive generates trajectories at 12\,Hz in on-vehicle operation. For robotic manipulation, TuringPAI-Embodied achieves a 96.8\% average success rate across the four LIBERO suites. These results demonstrate a shared vision-language foundation for driving and robotic manipulation under practical on-device constraints.

candidates.title: Prompt Engineering for AI: A Communication Skills Approach
candidates.abstract: This book equips readers with critical communication skills for productive, strategic prompting of large language, image, and multimodal AI models and tools. Working with AI tools requires users to define problems, set objectives, ask better questions, and evaluate the outputs they produced based on user requests. These communication skills discussed in this book, and others, offer a strategic framework for using generative AI tools and adapting as they evolve. The first three chapters explain the basics of AI tools, the utility of communication skills, and the importance of ethics. The next three chapters offer pragmatic advice for prompt engineering, with best practices and frameworks that complement the communication skills framework and prepare readers for text and multimodal outputs. The penultimate chapter emphasizes the importance of evaluating generative AI outputs and custom tools users may create. This book ends by showing how communication skills can be adapted as tools evolve and covers prompt-adjacent topics to help build AI literacy. Arguing that prompt engineering is not a technical skill but rather a communication skill, this comprehensive guide will be valuable for students, instructors, and professionals in the fields of communication studies, marketing, journalism, management, leadership, and any context in which generative AI is used. The Open Access version of this book, available at www.taylorfrancis.com , has been made available under a Creative Commons Attribution-Non Commercial-No Derivatives (CC BY-ND) 4.0 International license.

candidates.title: Mind2Act World: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Embodied Mind, Physical Action, and Mind-Action Composition in Robotic Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Embodied intelligence aims to let robots perform complex physical tasks with human-like adaptability and reliability, which requires three complementary capabilities: history-based cognitive reasoning, precise and timely physical execution, and the composition of reasoning and execution through environmental feedback. Yet existing benchmarks either evaluate reasoning and execution within the same tasks or assess them separately without their composition, so they reveal little about whether a failure comes from reasoning, execution, or their composition. We introduce Mind2Act World, a diagnostic benchmark of 30 simulated manipulation tasks from five real-world application domains. Each task has three difficulty levels and two scene settings (Clean and Random), yielding 180 configurations. The tasks form three views: Mind tests decisions based on past observations, Act tests precise and timely execution, and Mind2Act combines both in closed-loop tasks where action outcomes guide later decisions. Comparing the three views shows whether a system lacks a capability or fails to compose capabilities it already has. A diagnosis harness further attributes the failed episodes of three representative systems to Mind, Act, or their composition and summarizes each system in a profile card. Our evaluation of multimodal agents, vision-language-action models (VLAs), and world-action models (WAMs) shows that competence in a single view does not carry over to Mind2Act tasks. Even the strongest agent succeeds in 52.7% of Mind and 39.0% of Act episodes but in only 12.0% of Mind2Act episodes. The strongest agent retains task state but struggles with sustained contact, whereas end-to-end policies execute practiced motions but retain little task state. These findings point to composing reasoning and execution through environmental feedback as the main open problem.
