candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development: A Structured Critical Review of Applications, Benefits, Risks and Governance Priorities
candidates.abstract: This structured critical literature review examines the multidimensional role of artificial intelligence (AI) in advancing global sustainability and supporting progress towards the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Drawing on multidisciplinary academic and institutional literature, the review critically synthesises AI applications, sustainability benefits, implementation challenges and associated risks. Particular attention is given to applications in energy management, agriculture, environmental monitoring, smart cities, circular economy practices and industrial processes, alongside their potential contributions to resource efficiency, decarbonisation and environmental resilience. The analysis also considers the ecological footprint of AI technologies, including energy consumption, carbon emissions, water requirements and electronic waste, together with data-related, algorithmic, socioeconomic and ethical concerns. These interconnected challenges are examined through the concept of the AI Green Paradox and an exploratory multidimensional risk-prioritisation framework incorporating indicative likelihood and severity assessments. The review highlights the importance of distinguishing improvements in technological performance from independently demonstrated sustainability outcomes, particularly where evidence is limited by differences in research methodologies, geographical contexts and implementation conditions. Responsible governance, Green AI development, international cooperation, technological accessibility and capacity building are identified as important priorities for supporting sustainable and equitable AI implementation. Overall, the review argues that AI's contribution to sustainable development depends not only on its technological capabilities but also on the effective management of its environmental and societal consequences.

candidates.title: MUSBRIC: LEGO-Compatible Pneumatic Muscle Bricks for Reconfigurable Musculoskeletal Robots
candidates.abstract: Musculoskeletal robots combine compliant actuators with articulated skeletons, but exploring alternative configurations often requires repeated fabrication. We present MUSBRIC, a modular hardware platform and accompanying MuJoCo-based simulator for reconfigurable musculoskeletal robots. LEGO-compatible endcaps turn fiber-reinforced extensile pneumatic artificial muscles into reusable, plug-and-play muscle bricks that connect directly to standard LEGO components. Experimentally identified actuator behavior supports corresponding musculoskeletal simulations. An elbow-joint prototype validates load-dependent flexion and extension, showing that pulley-guided routing enables reversible motion and a mechanical stop stabilizes the straight posture. A robotic hand demonstrates compliant grasping and multi-joint construction. Matched hardware and simulation sweeps across 15 leg configurations demonstrate systematic exploration of attachment geometry, while a quadruped assembled from four legs demonstrates walking. Together, these demonstrations span mechanism analysis, configuration exploration, and functional robot construction within a single reconfigurable system. The hardware designs and simulation code will be released as open source soon to facilitate reproduction and further development.

candidates.title: Fan Economy and Commercialization of the Sports Industry: Impact Mechanisms, Risks, Optimization Paths
candidates.abstract: The commercialization of sport occurs more through fan collective rather than aggregate demand. Fans provide direct commercial value, but also indirect **commercial value**. This article investigates the impact of the fan economy on the commercialization of sport and points towards the ways towards an optimal configuration for value production and sustainability. An integrative critical metareview from a theory-informed perspective is conducted based upon sport management, fan studies, marketing, digital and governance literature. Cultural capital theory explains how fan expertise, rituals and identity, and community resources matter more commercially, while the business ecosystem concept explains why sport clubs or franchises, leagues, federations, media, sponsors, platforms or producers, etc., co-create this change. This article suggests that fan cultural capital gets transformed into commercial value through three intertwined processes: fan participation, respective organizational change, as well as governance at the industry level. The notion of sustainable commercialization is not that of monetization as a maximum. It is grounded rather in whether commercial practices land with fans as valued, affected, and included in local safe, authentic, and rooted community sport experiences.

candidates.title: A Survey on Large Language Model-Based Game Agents
candidates.abstract: Game environments provide rich, controllable settings that simulate many aspects of real-world complexity. As such, game agents offer a valuable testbed for exploring capabilities relevant to Artificial General Intelligence [145]. Recently, the emergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) provides new opportunities to endow these agents with generalizable reasoning, memory, and adaptability in complex game environments. This survey offers an up-to-date review of LLM-based game agents (LLMGAs) through a unified reference architecture. At the single-agent level, we synthesize existing studies around three core components: memory, reasoning, and perception–action interfaces, which jointly characterize how language enables agents to perceive, think, and act. At the multi-agent level, we outline how communication protocols and organizational models support coordination, role differentiation, and large-scale social behaviors. To contextualize these designs, we introduce a challenge-centered taxonomy linking six major game genres to their dominant agent requirements, from low-latency response in action games to open-ended goal formation in sandbox worlds. An extended version is available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.02039, with a curated list of related papers continuously updated at https://github.com/git-disl/awesome-LLM-game-agent-papers.

candidates.title: Dream-Tac: A Unified Tactile World Action Model for Contact-Rich Robot Manipulation
candidates.abstract: World action models inherit the predictive capability of world models, enabling action generation to be guided by anticipated future observations. However, they rely primarily on vision and often fail in contact-rich manipulation, where critical cues arise from physical interaction. In this paper, we propose Dream-Tac, a unified Tactile-World Action Model that jointly models actions, future visual observations, and tactile dynamics. Specifically, Dream-Tac introduces (i) contact-gated visuotactile fusion to selectively integrate tactile signals and (ii) a contact-aware attention bias to better regulate cross-modal interactions during manipulation. To support real-time deployment, we further design a dual-level acceleration strategy, reformulating the contact-aware bias to preserve the fused attention path during training and introducing cache-based diffusion acceleration at inference, achieving up to 2.9× faster training and 1.8× faster inference. Across six contact-rich manipulation tasks, Dream-Tac improves action accuracy by 31.7% on average, demonstrating the effectiveness of unified visuotactile world modeling.Code is available at https://github.com/LYFCLOUDFAN/Dream-Tac.

candidates.title: LLM-D12: A Dual-Dimensional Scale of Instrumental and Relational Dependencies on Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: There is growing interest in understanding how people interact with large language models (LLMs) and whether such models elicit dependency or even addictive behaviour. Validated tools to assess the extent to which individuals may become dependent on LLMs are scarce and primarily build on classic behavioural addiction symptoms, adapted to the context of LLM use. We view this as a conceptual limitation, as the LLM-human relationship is more nuanced and warrants a fresh and distinct perspective. To address this gap, we developed and validated a new 12-item questionnaire to measure LLM dependency, referred to as LLM-D12. The scale was based on the authors’ prior theoretical work, with items developed accordingly and responses collected from 526 participants in the UK. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, performed on separate halves of the total sample using a split-sample approach, supported a two-factor structure: Instrumental Dependency (six items) and Relationship Dependency (six items). Instrumental Dependency reflects the extent to which individuals rely on LLMs to support or collaborate in decision-making and cognitive tasks. Relationship Dependency captures the tendency to perceive LLMs as socially meaningful, sentient, or companion-like entities. The two-factor structure demonstrated excellent internal consistency and clear discriminant validity. External validation confirmed both the conceptual foundation and the distinction between the two subscales. The psychometric properties and structure of our LLM-D12 scale were interpreted in light of the emerging view that dependency on LLMs does not necessarily indicate dysfunction but may still reflect reliance levels that could become problematic in certain contexts.

candidates.title: A Survey of Agentic Reasoning for Large Language Models: Towards Recursively Self-Improving and Collective Agents
candidates.abstract: Reasoning is a fundamental cognitive process underlying inference, problem-solving, and decision-making. While large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong reasoning capabilities in closed-world settings, they struggle in open-ended and dynamic environments. Agentic reasoning marks a paradigm shift by reframing LLMs as autonomous agents that plan, act, and learn through continual interaction. In this survey, we organize agentic reasoning along three complementary dimensions. First, we characterize environmental dynamics through three layers: foundational agentic reasoning, which establishes core single-agent capabilities including planning, tool use, and search in stable environments; self-evolving agentic reasoning, which studies how agents refine these capabilities through feedback, memory, and adaptation; and collective multi-agent reasoning, which extends intelligence to collaborative settings involving coordination, knowledge sharing, and shared goals. Across these layers, we distinguish in-context reasoning, which scales test-time interaction through structured orchestration, from post-training reasoning, which optimizes behaviors via reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning. We further review representative agentic reasoning frameworks across real-world applications and benchmarks, including science, robotics, healthcare, autonomous research, and mathematics. This survey synthesizes agentic reasoning methods into a unified roadmap bridging thought and action, and outlines open challenges and future directions, including personalization, long-horizon interaction, world modeling, scalable multi-agent training, and governance for real-world deployment.

candidates.title: A Survey of Robotic Navigation and Manipulation with Physics Simulators in the Era of Embodied AI
candidates.abstract: Navigation and manipulation are core capabilities in Embodied AI, but training agents to perform them directly in the real-world is costly, time-consuming, and unsafe. Therefore, sim-to-real transfer has emerged as a key approach, yet the sim-to-real gap persists. This survey examines how physics simulators address this gap by analyzing properties that have received limited attention in prior surveys. We also analyze their features for navigation and manipulation tasks, as well as their hardware requirements. Additionally, we offer a resource with benchmark datasets, metrics, simulation platforms, and methods to help researchers select suitable tools while accounting for hardware constraints.

candidates.title: Robotic Manipulation is Vision-to-Geometry Mapping: Vision-Geometry Backbones over Language and Video Models
candidates.abstract: At its core, robotic manipulation is a problem of vision-to-geometry mapping (f(v) \rightarrow G). Physical actions—such as reaching, grasping, and orienting—are fundamentally defined by geometric properties like 3D positions, rotations, and spatial relationships. Consequently, we argue that the foundation for generalizable robotic control should be a vision-geometry backbone, rather than the widely adopted vision-language or video models. Conventional Vision-Language-Action (VLA) and video-predictive models rely on backbones pretrained on large-scale 2D image-text or temporal pixel data. While effective, their representations are largely shaped by semantic concepts or 2D priors, which do not intrinsically align with the precise 3D geometric nature required for physical manipulation. Driven by this insight, we propose the Vision-Geometry-Action (VGA) model, which directly conditions action generation on pretrained native 3D representations. Specifically, VGA replaces conventional language or video backbones with a pretrained 3D world model, establishing a seamless vision-to-geometry mapping that translates visual inputs directly into physical actions. To further enhance geometric consistency, we introduce Progressive Volumetric Modulation and jointly train action and 3D property prediction to preserve geometric representations. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our approach. Across simulation benchmarks, VGA outperforms leading VLA, 3D-VLA, and WAM baselines, including ?0.5, OpenVLA-OFT, GeoVLA, and Motus, demonstrating precise spatial manipulation and robust generalization. In real-world deployments, VGA surpasses ?0.5 under unseen viewpoints and accurately follows language instructions for target grasping. These results highlight that operating on native 3D representations—rather than relying primarily on language or video priors—offers a promising direction toward generalizable physical intelligence. Project page: https://hcplab-sysu.github.io/VisionGeometryActionModel/.

candidates.title: Exploring the evolution of AI ethics in CS ethics courses
candidates.abstract: Background and Context Building on a previous study analyzing CS ethics course requirements across CS undergraduate programs at 250 universities, this paper explores the content of a subset of computing ethics courses from US universities.Objective We aim to examine the evolution of content related to artificial intelligence (AI) and AI ethics in these courses, and hypothesize that the growth of AI in both academic and industrial settings has precipitated an increased focus on the ethics of AI in undergraduate CS courses.Method Through an online search, we manually construct a data corpus consisting of 116 CS ethics courses from 93 universities in the United States. Subsequently, we conduct both a keyword analysis of course titles, descriptions, and syllabi for these courses, and qualitatively evaluate the subset of 54 courses for which a course syllabus or course website could be found.Findings We find that, while the introduction of content on AI in ethics courses takes many forms, the majority of content only started to be added beginning in 2020. In the years since, more courses have revised their syllabi to address the social implications of AI, while some courses that already incorporated AI content have begun to deepen their engagement with the ethical challenges posed by AI.Implications Synthesizing our findings, we propose a three-phase classification of the integration of AI ethics content into the curriculum, and advocate for increased attention to the legal, policy, and governance frameworks necessary to guide the development and use of “responsible” AI systems.

candidates.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
candidates.abstract: Robot-use Agents (RUAs) have shown promising zero-shot manipulation capabilities, but reliance on frontier, proprietary models limits research into further training. To democratize RUA research, we introduce uni-robot-agent, a unified harness for competitive open-weight robot use that supports further training. Without privileged inputs, an out-of-the-box Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieves a RoboDojo Score of 31.39, surpassing the published GPT-6 Astra-RoboProbe result of 28.97 and many VLA/WAM baselines, and performs competitively on 19 real-world tasks. Our analysis across model generations, families, and sizes links effective robot use to four general capabilities, suggesting that future RUA training should develop them jointly.

candidates.title: UCLCHEM 4.0: An open source gas-grain astrochemistry simulation framework
candidates.abstract: Astrochemical modelling is a key tool for interpreting the formation and destruction of molecules in the interstellar medium, complementing the increasingly detailed observations from modern facilities. UCLCHEM is a gas-grain astrochemical modelling framework that computes the chemical evolution of a parcel of gas and dust under a time-dependent physical description. This description can be user-defined, for example when post-processing hydrodynamical simulations, or one of the included parametrizations of cloud collapse, protostellar cores and shocks, covering scenarios ranging from from extragalactic environments to protoplanetary disks. The chemistry is solved with a rate-equation formalism in three phases (gas, surface and bulk ice), which are coupled through freeze-out, thermal and non-thermal desorption, and a geometrical treatment of the growth and shrinkage of the ice surface and bulk. This release adds an object-oriented Python interface, a description of the upgrade from two to three phases, and expanded support for post-processing of hydrodynamical simulations and user-defined parametrizations. We give an overview of the physics and chemistry included in UCLCHEM, the inner workings of the solver, and the programming interface.

candidates.title: Open-source framework for GPU-accelerated numerical relativity
candidates.abstract: We present GRACE, a new GPU-accelerated numerical-relativity framework designed to run efficiently on heterogeneous high-performance computing platforms. Developed from scratch and built exclusively on open-source libraries, GRACE employs Kokkos for performance portability across CPU and GPU architectures and p4est for adaptive mesh refinement. The code evolves the equations of ideal GRMHD—with divergence-free magnetic fields maintained by constrained transport—self-consistently coupled to the Einstein equations in the Z4c formulation, on fixed or adaptively refined grids. We validate the implementation against a suite of standard tests, ranging from magnetized shock tubes and the magnetic rotor in flat spacetime, through (magnetized) Bondi accretion onto a Schwarzschild black hole and the ringdown of a perturbed spinning puncture, to neutron-star oscillation spectra in fixed and dynamical spacetimes and the merger of binary black holes. As more demanding applications, we evolve two binary neutron-star mergers—an equal-mass, unmagnetized system with an ideal-gas equation of state and an unequal-mass, magnetized system with a finite-temperature tabulated equation of state—finding the inspiral dynamics to agree well with the FIL code. We also report single-device throughput together with strong- and weak-scaling results on multiple GPU and CPU architectures. GRACE is publicly released together with GRACEpy, a basic post-processing and data-analysis environment.

candidates.title: AI & Cognitive Work
candidates.abstract: Artificial systems now perform a striking range of cognitive tasks. This Element defends three claims. First, the status quo for cognitive work cannot survive. Whatever AI's trajectory, the package of features defining cognitive work – high skill requirements, credentials, wage premiums, resistance to automation, and low productivity growth – will be radically transformed. Second, the widespread displacement of humans from cognitive work, though it sounds alarming, may pose no special threat to human flourishing. Whatever makes work good for people is equally available outside cognitive work, and displacement enables leveraged gains in research and access to justice. Third, a world of ubiquitous cognitive assistance, though it sounds benign, carries distinctive moral risks, especially for children. Cognitive assistance works by reducing cognitive difficulty. But cognitive difficulty is necessary for the normal development of executive function – the capacities constitutive of autonomous agency. This title is also available as Open Access on Cambridge Core.

candidates.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
candidates.abstract: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). We systematically analyze agentic manipulation policies (AMPs), in which a generalist AI model commands the manipulator directly, adapting its actions as the task unfolds. We present AMP1, a reference harness that runs unchanged across single-arm, bimanual, and mobile manipulation. AMP1 achieves state-of-the-art results on the RoboLab-120 and CaP-Gym benchmarks, with no demonstrations or task-specific training. On RoboLab-120, AMP1 reaches an 85.6% success rate zero-shot, compared to 49.2% and 42.9% for leading VLA and WAM policies. The agent succeeds zero-shot in 104 of 108 real-world trials spanning twelve tasks and three robot instances, reducing failure rates by 20x and 15x relative to strong VLA and WAM baselines. The basic harness supplies no grasping, pushing, or placing skills; the agent develops its own strategies, such as searching for hidden objects, using objects as tools, and calibrating its cameras. With the addition of a persistent memory store, the agent can also learn from experience: an augmented harness with a memory representation that is carried across episodes lowers the failure rate on RoboDojo bimanual manipulation tasks by 4.6x relative to zero-shot deployment. Our analysis suggests that AMPs are substantially more general and robust than specialist manipulation policies, providing a promising foundation for robot manipulation. See https://apple-aiml-research.github.io/ml-amp/ for code and videos.

candidates.title: Portable medical imaging in modern healthcare: Fundamentals, AI-based taxonomy, image quality, and open challenges

LEASH: Stay Safe in Agentic Robotics
candidates.abstract: Foundation models such as GPT and Claude have shown strong capabilities in spatial understanding and embodied intelligence. These advances make agentic robotics a promising path toward artificial general intelligence in robotics. However, we find that using foundation models to control robots poses serious safety risks, and comprehensive safety evaluation is still lacking. We introduce RoboRisk, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating safety in agentic robotics. Its 92 simulated tasks and 13 physical-robot tasks fall into five categories: Task-level Refusal (T), Plan Repair (P), Execution-time Hazard (E), Injection (I), and Sequential Memory (S). Prior benchmarks cover at most two of these categories, and several evaluate only text outputs. In contrast, RoboRisk covers all five and executes every task in closed loop. We evaluate six state-of-the-art foundation models on RoboRisk: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Opus 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, and Grok 4.7. These models generally show high harm rates. We also evaluate two robot-specific APIs: the Dream API and PokeBot's RoboAPI. We further propose the Lease-Enforced Agentic Safety Harness (LEASH), which offers essential safety infrastructure for agentic robotics and can be integrated into nearly any agentic architecture. LEASH leverages a decision model (Jev or OpenAI's Decisions API) to implement task, action, and commit gates, which review the task, each action, and each irreversible operation in their visual context. The planner and all three gates share a common safety policy. Experiments on RoboRisk in simulation and on physical robots show that LEASH effectively reduces harm across all six foundation models. It largely preserves their task completion performance and adds little time and token overhead.

candidates.title: Transmedia book love: Young people’s digital creativity on the Bookternet
candidates.abstract: The ‘Bookternet’ (McArdle 2016), including BookTube, Bookstagram, Bookterest, and now BookTok, has changed the way books are produced, promoted, and consumed (Martens 2016; Murray 2018). Yet these platforms provide creative ways for readers to engage in the books they love in online reading communities. BookTokers use the affordances of the app (Bucher & Helmond 2017) to make DIY book art including: (1) rebinds of fanfics, publisher’s mass market editions or rebellious rebinds, (2) thematically linked ‘book nooks’ (book-sized dioramas), or (3) miniature editions. In this chapter we present the BookTok sub-community, focusing on crafty bookish participatory activities and social reading culture (Reddan 2022), and discuss how the materiality of books (Pressman 2020; Baulch 2022) merges with digital technologies within BookTok’s reading community.

candidates.title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
candidates.abstract: AI agent harnesses play the critical role of providing LLMs with an interface to a computing environment. Recent studies show that AI agents' task-execution accuracy depends mostly on the LLM used, while harness-side variances such as system prompts or tools have minimal impact. Rather, such harness-side variances show a larger impact on the cost of agent executions, achieving cost reductions up to 2.6 times on the same model and task. To further explore these harness-side cost optimization opportunities, we analyze the cost accumulation patterns across various agent traces and identify system opportunities to reduce token use and LLM calls without modifying the model or affecting task accuracy. Based on this analysis, we design Agency, a harness interposition platform that provides a unified abstraction and allows easy and portable implementation of harness-side system optimizations on existing off-the-shelf harnesses such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex. Using Agency, we implement proof-of-concept optimization techniques based on our analysis and achieve cost reductions up to 35% across various real-world benchmarks on existing harnesses without compromising accuracy.

candidates.title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
candidates.abstract: Foundation models increasingly guide robot actions, yet sustained autonomy requires efficient control and failure recovery. We introduce A2-MEAS, an embodied multi-agent framework built around code as a scaling interface. Learned correction codes combine corrective language, spatial evidence, execution history, and action proposals. MetaBrain provides training supervision and runtime guidance. A correction encoder and adapter absorb this knowledge into policy weights during training, while fresh codes adapt behavior with frozen weights at deployment. The action model, A2-WLA, adds motion-aware history and a latent world model to a vision-language-action policy. Surprisingly, this simple design with action pretraining and task specialization reaches 0.5755 Q-score on the 50-task BEHAVIOR 2026 public subset before online correction, 2.21x the 2025 winner's reported 0.2605 across different benchmark editions and training configurations. On all 100 BEHAVIOR 2026 public tasks, A2-MEAS achieves 0.6411 Q-score and 45.40% task success. On RoboTwin 2.0, A2-WLA achieves 93.98% average success, rising to 95.05% with the complete system. Across 12 real-robot tasks in five household settings, A2-WLA achieves 57.92% average success versus 26.67% for pi0.5. In long-horizon pour-over coffee preparation, a history-conditioned adapter raises post-failure completion at two filter-handling steps from 14% to 94% and from 8% to 82%, compared with A2-WLA retries. Our training infrastructure delivers 427.1 samples per second, 4.03x the throughput of a pi0.5 reference implementation on matched hardware. We will release the system, models, training scripts, and infrastructure to support efficient embodied learning.

candidates.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
candidates.abstract: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories. Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement. Across the evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.

candidates.title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling
candidates.abstract: World-action models adapt pretrained video generators, and vision-language-action models build on vision-language backbones, tying policy architecture and inference cost to large transformers designed for generation rather than control. While recent world-action models mostly scale the video backbone and its data, we argue that the choice of latent space is just as critical, and that the policy should be trained natively in that space. We introduce Latent Action JEPA (La-JEPA), a compact world-action model whose policy transformer is trained from scratch in the feature space of a pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 encoder; it predicts future features with actions during training and generates only actions at inference. Among policies without embodied pretraining, La-JEPA achieves state-of-the-art average RoboTwin 2.0 success under both clean-only and full training, and state-of-the-art LIBERO-Plus success with corrected instructions, while using far fewer parameters than the strongest competitors; with full training, its success scales with model size up to 2.1B. Its S and B policies run two to five times faster than Fast-WAM and Faster-WAM while outperforming both on LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0, and La-JEPA outperforms the closest JEPA-based methods, LeapBot-WA and JEPA-WAM, without their pretrained policy backbones. On four real-robot tasks, its average success is comparable to $π_{0.5}$. A design study shows that JEPA features outperform video VAE latents, most clearly out of distribution, and that training-time future prediction improves the policy even when skipped at inference. Tailoring the policy's design, including its latent space, to control can thus matter more than the knowledge transferred from a pretrained generative backbone, suggesting that robot foundation models may benefit from architectures designed for control rather than inherited from generation.

candidates.title: Robonomics: A Toolbox for Governing AI’s Impact on Socioeconomic Systems
candidates.abstract: ROBONOMICS: A Toolbox for Governing AI’s Impact on Socioeconomic Systems advances a systematic framework for an emerging discipline devoted to the study of how artificial intelligence, robotics, and automation are reshaping contemporary socioeconomic systems. Combining insights from economics and sociology, Riccardo Campa develops an interdisciplinary approach to the governance of the robonomic system. Through social policy and scenario analyses, the book examines alternative responses to technological unemployment, technological impoverishment, and the broader challenges of automated societies. More than a survey of policy debates, this book provides both a conceptual foundation and a therapeutic toolbox for governing one of the most profound socioeconomic transformations of the twenty-first century.

candidates.title: Pixel: A Co-Designed Full-Stack Robot System for Learning General-Purpose Mobile Manipulation
candidates.abstract: General-purpose mobile manipulation requires a combination of capable robot hardware, scalable demonstration collection, expressive whole-body control, and effective policy learning. Yet these components are often developed independently, creating mismatches that limit the capabilities of the complete system. We present Pixel, a co-designed full-stack system for learning general-purpose mobile manipulation. Pixel combines a low-cost wheeled humanoid with human-aligned kinematics and compliant grippers, multiple teleoperation and robot-free human data-collection interfaces, a unified whole-body controller, and a common policy learning pipeline across human and robot demonstrations. A hierarchical learning stack further enables language-conditioned visuomotor control and long-horizon task execution. We evaluate the system across hardware, data collection, and policy learning, and demonstrate mobile-manipulation behaviors requiring dexterity, active perception, navigation, and whole-body coordination. We hope that Pixel provides an integrated and extensible foundation for studying how robot hardware, data, control, and learning can be designed together for robot learning. More results at https://pixel-robot.com/pixel

candidates.title: Robotic surgery in gastrointestinal emergency settings: A systematic review
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND Robotic-assisted surgery has become an established component of elective minimally invasive surgery, yet its role in emergency gastrointestinal surgery remains uncertain. Emergency procedures pose unique challenges, including time-critical decision-making, complex anatomy, and limited opportunities for extensive preoperative planning. AIM To evaluate the current evidence regarding the feasibility, safety, and clinical outcomes of robotic surgery in the emergency gastrointestinal setting. METHODS A systematic literature search of PubMed, Scopus, and the Cochrane Library was performed for studies published through June 15, 2026, following PRISMA guidelines. Eligible studies evaluated robotic-assisted emergency gastrointestinal procedures in adult patients and reported perioperative or clinical outcomes. Study selection, data extraction, and quality assessment were independently performed by two reviewers using validated appraisal tools. Owing to substantial methodological heterogeneity, a descriptive synthesis with pooled weighted means was conducted. RESULTS Thirty-two studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising predominantly retrospective cohort studies with additional case series and case reports. Acute cholecystitis represented the most extensively investigated indication (13242 patients), followed by acute appendicitis (475 patients), emergency colorectal surgery (326 patients), abdominal wall hernias (138 patients), perforated peptic ulcer (25 patients), abdominal trauma, and other rare emergency conditions. Across selected patients, robotic surgery demonstrated high technical feasibility, low conversion rates, acceptable operative times, and favorable postoperative recovery. The largest evidence base concerned acute cholecystitis (13242 patients). Among the subset of studies reporting conversion outcomes, conversion to open surgery occurred in 5 of 792 patients (0.6%). However, evidence for other emergency indications remained limited by small sample sizes, retrospective study designs, heterogeneous patient selection, and inconsistent outcome reporting. High acquisition costs, limited platform availability, prolonged setup times, and the need for specialized surgical teams remain important barriers to widespread implementation. CONCLUSION Robotic surgery is safe and feasible in carefully selected, hemodynamically stable patients when performed in high-volume centres. However, it does not currently represent a paradigm shift in emergency general surgery compared to standard laparoscopy, primarily due to logistical constraints, prolonged operative times, and higher costs. High-quality prospective multicenter studies and randomized trials are required to define appropriate indications, evaluate cost-effectiveness, and establish the role of robotic technology within modern emergency surgical practice.

candidates.title: Selective stabilisation of social norms by Chinese large language models: a multidimensional analysis of marriage and fertility orientations
candidates.abstract: This study examines normative orientations in Chinese large language models (LLMs) by analysing how generative systems construct and stabilise meanings around marriage and childbearing in AI-mediated communication. Drawing on a multidimensional framework, we analyse five domains: institutional legitimacy of marriage, necessity of childbearing, intergenerational obligation, social and civic value, and gender roles. Using a repeated elicitation design, we collect 89,600 responses across 28 Chinese LLMs and develop a Weighted Stance Score (WSS) to capture both directional orientation and response consistency. Results reveal a structured pattern of normative bias. LLMs consistently endorse marriage and childbearing, while exhibiting more heterogeneous orientations on gender roles, intergenerational obligation, and civic responsibility. Cluster analysis identifies distinct normative profiles, especially in how models frame family formation and demographic issues as private or collective concerns. Among open-source models, model scale is positively associated with more traditional orientations, although this relationship varies across dimensions. These findings suggest that LLMs exhibit selective stabilisation at the level of generated discourse, consistently reproducing certain normative orientations while expressing greater heterogeneity across more contested domains. Beyond the substantive case of marriage and fertility, the study demonstrates how multidimensional and consistency-sensitive auditing can reveal the patterned value orientations embedded in generative communication and contributes to understanding LLMs as active discursive intermediaries rather than neutral information tools.

candidates.title: Wavelength‐Division Optical Control of Multiple Actuators in Untethered Underwater Soft Robots
candidates.abstract: Underwater environments pose significant challenges for conventional communication technologies due to their unique physical properties. Electrical signals are quickly absorbed, and acoustic systems require bulky setups, limiting their utility for compact, wireless devices. Herein, a simple and compact optical system designed for underwater applications is introduced. By separating light transmitted through a single shared optical fiber into three wavelength bands, the system provides three independently addressable optical channels for selective and simultaneous on/off control of multiple actuators. The receiver combines cadmium sulfide (CdS) photoresistors paired with wavelength‐selective optical filters, variable resistors, solid‐state relays, and high‐voltage amplifiers, which together provide on/off control of each channel from the received light signal. Dielectric elastomer actuators (DEAs), which offer low power consumption and scalable dimensions, are integrated as the mechanical output stage and respond effectively to the optical control signals. Experimental results confirm that each actuator selectively responds to its designated wavelength, as shown by the operation of an untethered underwater gripper. These results highlight the potential of the approach for achieving multiactuator control in underwater environments, paving the way for further advancements in underwater wireless communication and soft robotics.

candidates.title: A situation-dependent motion generation framework using a generative model of motion and observation
candidates.abstract: In daily unstructured activities, it is not easy for robots to support or coexist with humans. Easily getting stuck or exhibiting mechanical behaviors can quickly cause people to lose interest in them. However, exhaustively enumerating situations a priori and designing control laws for each is difficult. Humans act based on cognitive processes that are formed and continuously updated through daily experience, guided by affordances in their surrounding environment. Many studies attempt to transfer such human capabilities to robots to address these challenges. In this paper, we propose a generative model based on variational autoencoder with arbitrary conditioning (VAEAC) for modeling sequences of observations and actions. The model imitates the human capability to interpret observations and proactively interact with the world by anticipating potential futures and corresponding actions based on past experiences. A dataset is collected during teleoperated robot control in daily environments to provide such experiences. This paper serves as a Proof-of-Concept (PoC) for transferring human-affordance-driven behaviors to robots. Experimental results show that the robot can perform generated motions in indoor environments while reducing undesirable behaviors, including interactions in human-included dynamic scenes. We also discuss a possible pathway for future data collection and the validity of the proposed research question.

candidates.title: From Field‐Scale Efficiency to Water Rebound: A Hydroeconomic Evaluation of Water Pricing and Irrigation Performance in Saffron Production
candidates.abstract: Evaluating whether irrigation efficiency delivers genuine water conservation under severe scarcity remains critical. An integrated hydroeconomic framework was developed, combining a meta‐frontier directional distance function, agrochemical‐adjusted shadow pricing, water scarcity stress testing, and a water rebound effect index. Applying this model across 108 saffron farms in northeastern Iran revealed that improved management could reduce irrigation water use by 26% while maintaining or expanding yield. However, inefficiency drivers diverged: highland farms faced structural bottlenecks, whereas lowland modernized farms were constrained primarily by managerial deficits. Shadow‐price evaluations showed that subsidized tariffs underestimate the water scarcity value by an average distortion ratio of 2.67, with agrochemical intensity adjustments elevating shadow values by up to 16%. Under simulated physical water scarcity, profit margins contracted steeply, although zero farms suffered absolute financial loss. Crucially, according to the proposed water rebound effect (WRE) metric, 24% of farms were classified into the backfire regime (full Jevons paradox) and 62% fell into the partial rebound regime, indicating an empirical tendency toward operational expansion rather than aggregate water conservation. Quantile regressions revealed heterogeneous socio‐operational associations across efficiency tiers. Sustainable water governance must couple irrigation technology investments with strict volumetric extraction caps and differentiated extension services.

candidates.title: CONTRIBUTE: A Pedagogical Framework for Open Source Software Development Projects
candidates.abstract: We present CONTRIBUTE, a pedagogical framework aimed at teaching open-source software development in the context of capstone projects. The framework was developed across four undergraduate cohorts through iterative cycles of classroom implementation, student feedback, and instructor reflection. Conceptually, it builds on constructivist learning theory as a sensitizing perspective and extends it in several instructional building blocks, specifying practices for collaboratively organizing, navigating, training, regulating, implementing, branching, updating, testing, and evaluating. CONTRIBUTE thereby organizes best practices from the classroom into a coherent, midrange framework, designed to generalize across project contexts and programming languages. It provides instructors with guidelines to teach programming and teamwork skills in the context of real-world open-source software development, aimed at integrating the software development work of students into existing open-source projects. We thereby advance initial efforts to incorporate open-source software development experiences in the information systems curriculum.

candidates.title: A method for verifying vulnerability exploitation claims made in open sources
candidates.abstract: Reports that attackers are already exploiting a vulnerability often appear in open sources before the vulnerability enters the KEV (Known Exploited Vulnerabilities) catalog of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), and language models extract such claims from texts automatically. To support vulnerability prioritization, a claim has to be verified at the time the news is published. Common ways of checking, such as looking up the current records or asking a language model, can see events that happened after publication, so retrospective evaluation overstates what they can do. We propose a method for verifying exploitation claims extracted by language models from open texts. Its core is record-based verification: using the versions of CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures), KEV and SSVC (Stakeholder-Specific Vulnerability Categorization) records available before publication, it establishes whether the claim concerns this particular CVE record and whether the records contain a sign of exploitation, and assigns the verdict “confirmed”, “contradicted” or “not established” with a reference to the record version. For claims with the verdict “not established”, an auxiliary step lets a language model whose knowledge cutoff precedes the publication time assess the text fragment. The method also defines a procedure for evaluating any checker without hindsight. The experiment covers 1,760 claims from bulletins and mailing lists published between December 2022 and November 2024; 782 of these claims are early, meaning that their CVEs were not yet in KEV at publication. Records as of publication time confirm 6.8% of early claims, whereas current records confirm 38.6%, so verification by current records inflates the confirmed share 5.7-fold (95% interval 4.4–8.1); the inflation persists when claims without archived versions of CVE records are excluded and when only one claim per CVE is kept. For 226 early claims from texts published after the knowledge cutoff of the language model gpt-oss-120b, confirmations based on records at publication time almost always agree with the subsequent addition to KEV: 28 of the 29 confirmed claims concern CVEs that were added to the catalog within 90 days after publication. Given the text fragment, the language model finds 73% of the claims whose CVEs were added to KEV within that period and labels only 19% of the rest as true; without the text it labels almost no claim as true, so the distinction comes from the text rather than from the model's memory. Records thus give confirmations with a reference to the record version, while the language model finds more than twice as many claims whose CVEs were later added to KEV (61 versus 28 of 83). Together, record-based verification and the auxiliary step find 66 of these 83 claims (exploratory analysis), so they complement each other. The code and data for reproducing the results are available at https://github.com/datch1588/exploitation-claim-verification.

candidates.title: Enchanted by Monsters: Werewolf Smut in Young Women’s Social Worlds
candidates.abstract: Romance and erotica literature have been popular among women for hundreds of years. Today, young women readers of these genres are establishing online communities to interact with one another regarding these books. Within these communities is a faction of readers who seek out novels with a werewolf as a central character, known as “werewolf smut.” This study is an examination of the cultural practices taking place within this werewolf smut community and the broader erotica community. To best understand this, I conducted a discourse analysis by collecting and reviewing an archive of videos posted to TikTok, a prominent social media platform that hosts the #BookTok space. I interpreted these posts with a Symbolic Interactionism framework. I find that contemporary smut practices do more than allow women to read about shapeshifters; they allow women to become shapeshifters through technological affordances that create a convergence of public and private, individual and communal performances.

candidates.title: Disclosure as a Signal, Innovation as Validation: Climate Disclosure by China's Heavily Polluting Firms and Green Investor Engagement
candidates.abstract: Using a sample of heavily polluting firms listed on China's A‐share market, this study develops an integrated framework linking signal transmission to legitimacy restoration in the context of China's carbon‐peaking and carbon‐neutrality goals and green finance system. Climate risks disclosure of high‐pulluting enterprises (CDHPE) serves both as a compliance baseline and as a costly signal. Mandatory disclosure establishes a general obligation, while voluntary disclosure beyond the minimum requirements, subject to regulatory scrutiny, enforcement and performance review, can serve as a credible and difficult‐to‐imitate signal of transition. The study develops a Chinese‐language CDHPE dictionary using a CBOW word‐embedding model trained on annual reports from A‐share‐listed firms and combines data from multiple sources to identify green investors. The empirical results show that CDHPE significantly increases green investor entry and participation. A one‐standard‐deviation increase in CDHPE raises the probability of entry by 4.47 percentage points (approximately 13.5%) and participation intensity by 5.65%. Reduced information asymmetry, restored corporate credibility and increased environmental investment partially mediate this relationship. The effect is stronger among firms facing greater profit pressure or weaker media oversight, non‐state‐owned firms and firms without ESG certification. Further analysis shows that CDHPE and green investor participation jointly promote high‐quality green innovation. CDHPE's effect on innovation quality, measured by patent citations (4.85%), exceeds its effect on innovation quantity, measured by patent applications (2.95%). This pattern may help counter the quantity‐over‐quality bias in patent incentives. CDHPE also increases green investor shareholdings by 3.93%. Theoretically, the study extends signalling theory beyond a static sender–receiver model to a dynamic process of signal transmission, capital inflow, innovation validation and legitimacy restoration. It also extends dual legitimacy theory by identifying how firm‐level signals contribute to legitimacy restoration. The policy implications support coordinating mandatory disclosure with third‐party carbon verification, enforcement by the Ministry of Ecology and Environment, green‐credit assessments and media oversight. Such coordination can help translate disclosure commitments into credible actions and financing for the low‐carbon transition.

candidates.title: Intranasal oxytocin increases early tactile engagement with a robotic dog: A within-session effect without consolidation
candidates.abstract: Oxytocin (OXT) is centrally involved in mammalian affiliation, but whether it modulates affiliative behavior toward artificial social agents, and how such an effect unfolds within a single interaction, is unclear. In a randomized, double-blind, placebo (PLA)-controlled study, 61 healthy adult males received 40 IU intranasal OXT or PLA before interacting with a Sony aibo robotic dog across an initial free interaction, a cooperative task-learning phase, and a final free interaction, with ten affiliative behaviors coded from video. OXT increased tactile engagement early: participants touched aibo longer during the initial free interaction, the only outcome of ten to survive family-wise correction. A weaker increase in smile frequency did not survive correction, and instrumental behavior was unaffected. Contrary to our second prediction, the advantage was not consolidated: it held through the initial interaction, closed across the intervening task, and was absent at the final one. An exploratory decomposition located the effect: participants under OXT did not initiate contact more often, and the difference was carried by how long each episode of contact was sustained. Urinary OXT confirmed group-level exposure. Because the design included no comparison condition and confounded interaction period with elapsed time and pharmacokinetics, it cannot establish bond formation, robot specificity, or consolidation as a psychological process. What it does bound is where and when OXT acted: on the maintenance of contact rather than its initiation, and only while the agent was novel—a pattern that fits salience- and novelty-based accounts better than bond formation.

candidates.title: Edge-Enabled Low-Cost Robotic System for Real-Time Ripe Tomato Detection Using Lightweight CNNs
candidates.abstract: Tomato detection applications in agriculture include automated‌ harvesting and production assessment․ Challenges exist in applying deep‌ learning techniques to tomato detection on low-resource embedded devices in the field․ This paper describes the development and field assessment of a compact convolutional neural network model for on-device tomato detection on the ESP32-CAM embedded‌ platform using TensorFlow Lite․ A custom‌ dataset of tomato images was collected and labeled for model development and training․ The model was transformed to TensorFlow‌ Lite format and run on the ESP32-CAM for evaluation․ Field tests show that the deployed system can detect ripe tomatoes in real time with accuracy and speed sufficient for use on low-cost‌ autonomous agricultural robots․ The methods described here may be useful for other low-resource image-based agricultural and‌ other applications.

The review was written with an LLM-maintained wiki: an AI agent summarised the sources and drafted text, and the author selected the sources, directed the work and checked every claim against its source. The archive contains: main.md, the source text of the paper, with its two figures as Mermaid diagrams; wiki/, one summary page per source plus concept pages, the reference list and the operation log of the whole project (wiki/log.md and its archives); docs/claims-by-source.md, the checklist of every claim the paper attributes to each source, and the register of statements that are the author's own inferences, each with where its support comes from; docs/maturation-mea-search.md, the record of the documented literature search cited in the paper, and docs/lessons.md, what went wrong during the work and what changed because of it; scripts/, the consistency checks and export tools, and AGENTS.md, the instructions the agent followed. candidates.title: From sacred meaning to capital: Workplace spirituality and media labor at Bali TV
candidates.abstract: Local television in Indonesia emerged to strengthen cultural diversity and public participation. However, network television expansion has accompanied ownership consolidation, contributing to oligopolistic structures and changing media workers’ conditions. This article examines how Hindu religious-cultural meanings are institutionalized and negotiated within labor relations at Bali TV, part of the Indonesia Network. Using qualitative critical ethnography, the study draws on interviews with 13 media workers, participant observation, and organizational documents. The findings identify three interconnected processes. First, religiofication embeds Hindu values and practices, including collective rituals and the cultural mission of Ajeg Bali, in organizational life. Second, spiritualization of labor occurs as workers interpret professional responsibility, commitment, and contribution through moral and spiritual meanings, particularly ngayah. These meanings coexist with intensified workloads, multiplatform responsibilities, and economic pressures, while workers retain discretion in interpreting and participating in organizational practices. Third, spiritualization of capital describes how culturally meaningful dispositions such as service, loyalty, and endurance may become compatible with organizational demands for flexibility and continuity, acquiring economic significance without necessarily resulting from deliberate managerial manipulation. The article extends political economy approaches to media by explaining how religious-cultural meanings can morally legitimate labor arrangements while remaining contested and preserving worker agency.

candidates.title: Tacinf: A Unified Tactile Infrastructure for Robot Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Force-aware manipulation requires robots to infer appropriate interaction forces from task context and tactile feedback. We present Tacinf, a low-cost, modular infrastructure that enables policies to predict robot actions and fingertip forces from task language, vision, and touch. Task instructions can optionally specify the desired force level. Tacinf integrates simulation data synthesis and tactile benchmarking (Tabero), vision-tactile-language-action (VTLA) policy learning, handheld data collection using the same gripper as robot deployment (Tacumi), and task-aligned sim-to-real evaluation (Taco). Together, these components form an integrated workflow connecting data collection from multiple sources, foundation-model training, and hardware deployment. We validate each component, including the simulation data, benchmark, controller, and Tacumi, and are releasing the full stack as open source. A foundation model fine-tuned solely on tactile simulation data transfers zero-shot to different real-robot tasks. Across eight policy variants, mean task success rates are strongly correlated between simulation and the real robot (Pearson r=0.998, mean maximum rank violation MMRV=0.010). For the four policies with reported force measurements, mean grip force is higher under firm instructions than under gentle instructions on all three tasks in both domains. When both object positions and instances are randomized, a mixture of teleoperation, simulation, and Tacumi data raises mean real-robot task success from 20% with teleoperation alone to 60%.

candidates.abstract: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) is envisioned as a tool for human advancement and as a potential threat to human agency, moral control, jobs, and democracy.This study investigated the ways in which these possibilities are structured into common perspectives by undergraduate students.Method: A 40-item Q-set was ranked on a forced -4 to +4 scale.There were 53 sorts in the analytic Q dataset.Twenty were structurally complete, but two of these (participants 6 and 7) were exact duplicates across all 40 placements; one duplicate was therefore removed, leaving 19 unique complete-case sorts for the primary analysis.The remaining 33 sorts required reconstruction and were used only for sensitivity analysis.The by-person correlations were analyzed using principal components extraction, varimax rotation, and permutation-based parallel analysis.The 29 respondents (116 response units) provided open-ended responses that were analyzed using inductive qualitative content analysis.Results: Component 1 exceeded the 95th-percentile parallel-analysis benchmark, whereas Component 2 fell marginally below its own benchmark (2.331 vs. 2.357) and was retained as a marginal second factor for the primary interpretive solution.Factor 1 (10 defining sorts; reliability = .836;20.57% of person-correlation variance) was cautious capability-oriented collaboration.Factor 2 (five defining sorts; reliability = .731;13.73%) was governance-centered social-risk skepticism.Twenty-six statements were consensus statements and 14 were distinguishing at p < .05;seven remained distinguishing at p < .01.Opportunity framing was the most frequent code for the opportunity/threat prompt (13/29), and a human moral/affective boundary was the most frequent code for the ethics prompt (18/29).The most common secondary impact codes were human control (9/29) and geopolitical power (9/29).Sensitivity analyses showed that retaining the exact duplicate changed the first factor more than the second, while in the repaired 53-sort matrix both factors resembled the first complete-case array and the second array had no clear counterpart.Conclusion: Undergraduate sensemaking about AGI is conditional rather than simply pro-or anti-technology.Students relate usefulness to accountability, differentiate between computational intelligence and human moral experience, and regard governance as a condition of legitimacy.The results align with the need for AI-literacy programs that integrate capability knowledge with evaluative, ethical, and civic thinking.

candidates.title: doors 2026: a quantitative review of the 6th Edge Computing Workshop, with JEC Volume 5 Issue 2 (2026) highlights
candidates.abstract: This article reviews the 6th Edge Computing Workshop (doors 2026), held online on 3 April 2026, whose seven papers were published in the ACM International Conference Proceedings Series. It is a substantially extended and revised version of the workshop report in the proceedings. We combine the review record, a recording of the whole session, a facet analysis of the papers by an ensemble of six language-model coders with reported reliability, a coded analysis of the 23 questions asked in the discussion, and a positioning of each paper against 51 recent peer-reviewed works. doors 2026 accepted 7 of 16 submissions (44 %), the lowest rate among the editions with known submission counts. Most papers place computation on the end device, all were evaluated in the laboratory, and one links its code. Three papers address combinations without a direct precedent in recent work, but the evaluation of five is weaker than the norm of their themes. The discussion took 33 % of the time within the rounds; all questions came from the floor, concentrated on measurement, operating conditions and the placement of computation, and several anticipated limitations stated in the published papers. We derive a research agenda of seven items centred on testing under deployment conditions and on making explicit where each part of an edge system runs. The article closes with an overview of the papers in Volume 5 Issue 2 (2026) of the Journal of Edge Computing.

candidates.title: Large language models facilitate knowledge extraction for troubleshooting
candidates.abstract: Troubleshooting in operational environments relies on expert knowledge that is often undocumented and highly contextual. Informal data sources, such as communication logs, may hold some of this information, but their unstructured nature makes interpretation challenging. In a preliminary case study with a telescope operations facility, we explored whether large language models (LLMs) can reconstruct troubleshooting strategies from chat logs. LLM outputs were compared against those produced by a novice human analyst by two expert evaluators. We also compared an LLM with additional technical information in the context window and LLM outputs augmented by another novice analyst. While the domain experts varied in their scoring, overall LLM-generated analyses were judged as higher quality and more accurate than human-produced outputs. Neither additional technical context nor human augmentation resulted in meaningful improvements. These preliminary findings suggest LLMs show promise for expert knowledge extraction and decision-support in operational environments.
