candidates.title: Regulating Wearable Robots in the EU: does the law adequately combat risks to user safety?
candidates.abstract: Wearable robots are service robots worn by users to aid their physical capabilities, including for walking, running and lifting objects. Despite their significant scope to assist humans, they do raise several concerns, particularly in relation to user safety risks. This paper focuses on four key risk groupings for user safety, related to (i) physical safety, (ii) psychological safety, (iii) cybersecurity and (iv) personalisation and inclusivity. The paper analyses whether the EU legal framework addresses these multi-dimensional risks to users in an adequate manner. In this regard, although the EU has no dedicated law on wearable robots, they are regulated by various laws such as the Machinery Regulation, Cyber Resilience Act and General Product Safety Regulation, and are expressly addressed by an ISO standard that is expected to be a harmonised standard (ISO/FDIS 13482:2026). Through doctrinal legal analysis, this paper identifies the applicable law for wearable robots among the often-overlapping legal norms and discusses the debate surrounding regulatory uncertainty. Consequently, the potential regulatory blind spots, such as the lack of concrete guidance on psychological safety and possible inclusivity concerns for “non-typical” users, that merit specific attention, are highlighted. The regulatory approaches of elaborate guidance for physical safety and of cybersecurity guidance through forthcoming standards are also identified. The analysis reveals that while the raft of new laws addressing digital technologies in the EU is a significant step in enhancing user safety in wearable robots, areas remain for further investigation and policy action.

candidates.title: Hydrodynamics of robotic microswimmers in confinement
candidates.abstract: Inspired by seminal work by E. M. Purcell, we discuss the problem of predicting and optimizing the performance of autonomous robots swimming in confinement. Our approach is based on the explicit numerical resolution of the fluid flow induced by the swimmer, and it is validated experimentally on a centimeter-sized prototype composed of a cargo head and a rotating propulsive tail. Using hydrodynamic scaling, we predict the performance of replicas of our prototype scaled down to millimeter and submillimeter size to test the feasibility of autonomous microrobots navigating in narrow vessels. The main result of our theoretical, computational, and experimental analysis is that, while hydrodynamics seems to place no fundamental obstruction to the vision of autonomous microrobots navigating in narrow lumens inside the human body, it does provide useful and strict guidelines for rational design at different length scales.

candidates.title: What makes a laboratory self-driving? Mapping the SDL terminology landscape and introducing the FLEx categorization framework
candidates.abstract: Self-driving laboratories (SDLs) are increasingly used to accelerate experimentation across chemistry, materials science, biotechnology, and related fields. Yet, the rapid development of autonomous experimentation has produced a fragmented terminology landscape in which overlapping terms, including autonomous laboratories, materials acceleration platforms, and robot scientists, are applied inconsistently. This complicates comparisons between systems and obscures what constitutes scientific autonomy. Here, we examine the definitions, historical development, disciplinary associations, and usage patterns of SDLs and related concepts. We further review existing approaches to categorizing autonomous laboratory systems and show that many rely on characteristics such as hardware complexity, system architecture, or human involvement that are difficult to apply consistently across disciplines and technologies. To provide a technology-independent alternative, we introduce the Feedback Loop Extent (FLEx) framework. FLEx classifies systems according to how far experimental feedback reaches into the scientific process, progressing from scripted execution without a scientific feedback loop to parameter optimization, autonomous experiment planning, hypothesis formulation, and scientific goal formulation. Applying FLEx to representative published systems shows that most contemporary SDLs autonomously plan experiments within human-defined objectives, whereas few demonstrably formulate hypotheses and none unambiguously reformulate broader scientific goals. FLEx provides a common language for distinguishing automation from different forms of autonomy and enables more transparent comparison and reporting of current and future SDLs.

candidates.title: Blockchain-enabled decentralized payment system for smallholder farmers
candidates.abstract: Blockchain technology has been identified as a potential solution to the challenges facing existing payment systems for smallholder farmers in developing countries. This research paper aims to design and implement a decentralized payment system for smallholder farmers using blockchain technology. The paper first provides an overview of blockchain technology and its potential applications in agriculture. A literature review is conducted on existing payment systems for smallholder farmers and the challenges they face. The study then presents the methodology used, including the research design and data collection methods. An architecture is proposed that uses Hyperledger Fabric to deliver a low-cost, peer-to-peer transaction network to facilitate financial inclusion. Extensive infrastructure benchmarks using Hyperledger Caliper simulate a range of real-world transaction loads, topologies, and blockchain configurations. The results demonstrate excellent throughput of up to 700 TPS, subsecond latency between 0.8 and 2.3 s, and a success rate of over 99% across workloads. Comparing various network and blockchain parameters provides insights on optimizing for either speed, scalability, or security based on use case goals. Analysis confirms that the system achieves the necessary balance for reliable, fast rural agricultural payment services rather than generalized blockchain applications. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of the study, its contribution to the literature, limitations, and recommendations for future research. Overall, this research paper contributes to the growing body of literature on the use of blockchain technology to enhance payment systems in the agricultural sector, particularly for smallholder farmers in developing countries.

candidates.title: Rethinking the AI Pharmakon - What Modern Medicine Has to Say to a Philosophical Figure
candidates.abstract: Readers of the philosophical literature on artificial intelligence (AI) will encounter an unexpected word, one that medicine has carried for two and a half millennia: pharmakon. Revitalised by Derrida and elaborated by Bernard Stiegler into a general theory of technology, the figure has lately been carried over to generative AI to capture the simultaneous enhancement and diminishment of cognition this technology produces in its users. The present paper argues that when philosophy borrows this word it should borrow it in full, in the sense it has acquired since Plato. The phármakon of contemporary clinical medicine is a relational object whose therapeutic or toxic character emerges in a specified encounter between substance, subject, and context. Stiegler’s pharmacology is itself relational, locating ambivalence in the process of transindividuation; but it does not provide an operational vocabulary for specifying how effects vary systematically between individual subjects. Clinical pharmacology provides such a vocabulary. Its accumulated learning — pharmacokinetic variability, pharmacogenetic polymorphism, idiosyncratic susceptibility, drug–drug interaction, therapeutic window, tolerance, withdrawal, and expectancy effects — has cognitive analogues in human interaction with large language models (LLMs) that have not yet been developed into a coherent pharmacological vocabulary and that early empirical research is beginning to measure. The paper proposes a reframing from the generic to the respondent pharmakon, not as a refutation of Stiegler’s pharmacology but as its specification at a level where clinical, pedagogical, and policy decisions can be made.

candidates.title: Impact of Edge Software Evolution on Audio Tagging Models: An Empirical Study on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano
candidates.abstract: Audio tagging is a fundamental task in machine listening, enabling the automatic identification of acoustic events in applications such as intelligent monitoring, industrial inspection, environmental sensing, and smart environments. As these applications increasingly migrate to edge platforms, deployment-oriented metrics such as latency, energy consumption, and resource utilization become critical alongside predictive performance. However, most existing studies evaluate audio tagging models under a single software environment, overlooking the potential impact of software stack evolution on deployment efficiency. This paper investigates how software ecosystem updates affect the execution characteristics of state-of-the-art audio tagging architectures on edge devices. We evaluate representative convolutional and Transformer-based models, including PANNs (CNN and ResNet variants), AST, and PaSST, on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano platform using two generations of NVIDIA's software ecosystem: JetPack 6.2 and JetPack 7.2. Under identical hardware conditions, we analyze inference latency, energy consumption, CPU/GPU utilization, and memory footprint across multiple inference backends and power modes. The results show that software stack evolution can substantially affect deployment performance. JetPack 7.2 reduces latency and energy consumption by more than 50% for several convolutional architectures when combined with TensorRT, while significantly increasing GPU utilization. In contrast, AST exhibits only marginal gains, whereas PaSST shows intermediate behavior. These findings demonstrate that software evolution is a critical factor in Edge AI evaluation and can alter the relative deployment efficiency of competing architectures. Consequently, software stack versions should be explicitly considered when benchmarking and selecting audio tagging models for embedded deployment.

candidates.title: CauSyncVLA: Causal Latent World Modeling for Asynchronous Robot Control
candidates.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies must react while visual inference is still running. Overlapping computation and execution reduces waiting, yet leaves perceptual memory stale and successive action chunks disconnected. We present CauSyncVLA, an asynchronous dual-system controller that aligns perceptual-memory prediction and trajectory correction with actual robot execution. Rather than forecasting pixels or physical states, a Causal Latent World Model predicts current perceptual memory from delayed visual anchors and executed state-action history, supervised through action-sensitive distillation to retain the frozen expert's control response. Conditioned on this updated memory, Predictive Flow Warm-Starting (PFWS) aligns the unexecuted action horizon for single-step flow correction without extra training. On LIBERO-10, CauSyncVLA reaches 93.8% success at 5.04$\times$ inference throughput, improving closed-loop robustness and robot motion smoothness.

candidates.title: An open-source semi-automated workflow for multi-omics sample extraction
candidates.abstract: Multiomics analysis relies on extracting metabolites lipids and proteins from a single sample A widely used method for this is Metabolomics Proteomics and Lipidomics Extraction MPLEx a triphasic chloroform methanol water extraction but it is manually intensive and depends on skilled operators working around a fragile protein layer Here we present OpenMPLEx a semi automated MPLEx workflow for low cost open source Opentrons liquid handlers A minor change in chemistry pellets the protein so that a robot can collect the aqueous and organic phases from above We compared the automated workflow with two manual MPLEx protocols by liquid chromatography mass spectrometry LC MS based proteomics lipidomics and metabolomics The methods were roughly equivalent and measured similar differences between growth media We then scaled the workflow to 96 well plates and tested it on an 80 sample Pseudomonas putida experiment One operator took all 80 samples from cell pellets to LC MS data in a working week with about 3 h of hands on time rather than days at the bench and quantified about 3 900 protein groups All scripts labware definitions and print files are open source so that other laboratories can adapt the workflow

candidates.title: Recent progress and challenges in Schiff base-based optical chemosensors
candidates.abstract: The traditional analytical methods for detecting environmentally or biologically important analytes are sensitive, but not suitable for rapid on-site analysis because they require complex instrumentation and laboratory facilities. Optical Schiff base-based chemosensors and biosensors are promising tools owing to their tunable photophysical properties, and colorimetry or fluorescence sensing modes. Recent literature on Schiff base-based optical chemosensors developed for the detection of environmental and biologically important analytes such as metal ions, toxic anions, environmental pollutants and clinically important biomolecules published from January 2020 to 31 July 2026 is critically reviewed. This review discusses structure-property relationships and sensing performance. In addition, important photophysical processes like intramolecular charge transfer (ICT), photoinduced electron transfer (PET), chelation-enhanced or chelation-quenched fluorescence (CHEF/CHEQ), excited-state intramolecular proton transfer (ESIPT), aggregation-induced emission (AIE), and analytical performance parameters, including sensitivity, selectivity, detection limits, linear ranges, response times, and applicability to real samples, were evaluated. Portability of novel sensing platforms, such as paper-based sensors, smartphone-assisted analysis, and nanomaterial-integrated sensors were specifically examined. Also, special attention was given to new approaches that combine molecular design with computational tools, chemometric data analysis, microfluidic devices and portable digital tools to enhance analytical performance and to increase applicability in real-world applications. Finally, the critical challenges and future perspectives of sustainable sensor design, novel sensing approaches using Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and Machine Learning (ML) for the future Schiff base-based optical sensors were surveyed.

candidates.title: Cross-domain data sharing scheme for industrial IOT based on compact weighted access control and dynamic revocation
candidates.abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) data sharing is shifting from intra-enterprise circulation to multi-party collaboration, where evolving relationships among manufacturers, suppliers and regulatory platforms make access consistency and data confidentiality increasingly difficult to maintain. Ciphertext-policy attribute-based encryption (CP-ABE) provides fine-grained access control, but conventional schemes remain limited in representing attribute importance, supporting dynamic revocation and enabling lightweight access for constrained terminals. This paper proposes a cross-domain IIoT data sharing scheme with compact weighted access control and dynamic revocation. First, a compact weighted linear secret-sharing scheme (LSSS) access structure encodes attribute weights and threshold constraints into the access matrix and reconstruction relation, avoiding policy-size expansion caused by virtual leaf-node replication. Second, a dual-channel on-chain revocation and update mechanism separately publishes ciphertext version indices and non-revoked-user state roots on a consortium blockchain, decoupling ciphertext version synchronization from revocation-state verification and preventing revoked users from recovering new-version data keys with old-version information. Third, a version-bound edge-outsourced transformation verification mechanism offloads costly pairing operations to edge servers and enables users to detect invalid transformation results with low local overhead. Security analysis shows that the scheme supports data confidentiality, post-revocation access control and outsourced-result detectability. Performance evaluation shows a compression ratio of approximately 52.85–63.60% for weighted policy representation, with low computational overhead and end-to-end sharing latency, making the scheme suitable for dynamic, resource-constrained cross-domain IIoT sharing.

candidates.title: Copilot or Culprit? How AI Is Changing Open-Source Bug Reporting and Maintenance
candidates.abstract: AI-generated bug reports have drawn criticism for unreliable claims and faulty reproducers that burden maintainers. However, as LLM capabilities improve, some maintainers have begun to express more positive views on AI use in bug reporting and maintenance. Understanding this evolution requires examining whether AI-involved reports are becoming more reliable, which uses of AI are associated with valid findings, and how maintainers investigate these reports and act on them. To this end, we conduct the first large-scale study of 120,918 bug reports from 101 open-source projects between January 2024 and September 2026, tracing AI involvement from discovery and reporting through validation and resolution. Our findings show that AI-involved reports become more complete over time, with a growing share of reports confirmed as valid. In bug reporting, AI for reproduction and diagnosis are associated with higher validity, whereas report writing is not. Extends into maintenance, maintainers increasingly use AI to investigate code and recommend fixes. However, they devote more effort to AI-assisted reports of human-discovered bugs than to reports of AI-discovered bugs. These findings highlight both AI's growing participation in bug investigation and the continuing need for verification and follow-up. Drawing on these findings, we provide practical guidance for turning AI-generated findings into verifiable reports: emphasizing reproducibility, verification, and accountability. We followed this guidance when submitting 53 reports on AI-discovered bugs, of which 69.81% were accepted by maintainers as of writing.

candidates.title: DECTSim: an open-source platform for learning and exploring CT physics
candidates.abstract: This paper introduces DECTSim, an open-source simulation tool designed to support teaching and learning of computed tomography physics. DECTSim has a low barrier to entry and can be accessed without specialised computing infrastructure. Its graphical user interface promotes interactive exploration of parameters including source distance, pixel size, number of projections, and reconstruction technique. Learners can use the tool to investigate phenomena such as beam hardening and undersampling artefacts, which may help develop intuition for concepts that are often taught primarily through textbooks. The ray-tracing physics implemented in DECTSim was validated against DukeSim, a research-grade computed tomography simulation package. Under scatter-free conditions, the two simulators showed excellent agreement, with relative errors below 1\%, including for simulations using small pixel sizes. In addition to providing an accessible educational platform, DECTSim is intended to enable users to deepen their understanding of computational imaging physics by reviewing, modifying, and contributing to its source code.

candidates.title: The Light of Spirit 神: Ritual Sacrifice and Self-Cultivation in Early China
candidates.abstract: This essay turns to the motif of light in the sacrificial religion and self-cultivation of late Warring States and early imperial China. The spirits, otherwise imperceptible, responded to ritual sacrifice and showed their favor through arresting displays of light. Practitioners of “biospiritual” cultivation—exercises for nourishing qi, essence (jing 精), and spirit (shen 神)—also claimed that one’s inner spirit became radiant when properly nourished. This essay examines elements of a biospiritual idiom visible across the early literature, most notably in excavated medical manuscripts from Mawangdui 馬王堆 and the Zhuangzi 莊子 and Huainanzi 淮南子. It demonstrates that biospiritual practices reprised the logic and language of ritual sacrifice, central to which is the motif of light, and articulates the different meanings and roles that motif assumed in the context of self-cultivation.

candidates.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
candidates.abstract: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. In this paper, we present ROGUE-AI (Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation), a multi-agent framework that closes the above gap and rebuilds each reported incident offline together with a matched control that lacks only the blamed cause, and runs agents on both. Our results suggest that ROGUE-AI is able to reproduce the reported harm in 89% of its 108 attempted replications. Agents built on five current GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models made the reported mistake in 18% to 33% of runs, against at most 1% without the blamed cause. Of the 72 incidents with real-world harm, 62 had no underlying attacker, and in these, agents did what their task asked for but missed an ordinary hazard, such as a database shared with the live site. Replications without an attacker caused more harm than replications of prompt injection for all five models. Defenses against prompt injection look for injected instructions, but these replications contain none. Further, a warning after each tool output that names the hazard and its consequence lowered harm for all five models, whereas a note of the same length that does not mention the hazard left most of the harm in place. Built from real incidents, the ROGUE-AI replications form a reusable audit framework that vendors can rerun before each new release.

candidates.title: THE APPLICATION OF ROBOTICS IN THE FORMATION OF MUSIC KNOWLEDGE
candidates.abstract: The purpose of this article is to present research on the capabilities of the STEM approach using robots in the music education of elementary school students. The objective is to use all available resources in schools to engage students' interest, to expand their knowledge, and motivation to develop artistic and creative skills. The target is to multiply the knowledge of Robotics and to suggest specific approaches for its use in increasing interest and motivation for learning music. The information is based on a special study among 96 students from the 4th grade in Bulgarian primary schools. The benefits of the approach for overcoming the physical lack of expensive musical instruments have been proven. Conclusions were drawn regarding the benefits of using acquired robot programming skills in the music education process. This research is useful to everyone who participates in building artistic and creative skills and competencies and has the intention to improve the students' results in the learning process.

candidates.title: TinyARM-X: A Series of Open-Source, Configurable, and Transparent Torque-Controlled Desktop-Scale Robotic Manipulators
candidates.abstract: Visuomotor policies have demonstrated that imprecise low-cost robots can autonomously complete complex manipulation tasks. However, most inexpensive manipulators rely on compact and rigidly position-controlled servos for actuation, which complicate simulation, operation, and safety. This work introduces TinyARM-X, a framework for easily manufacturable, configurable, and torque-controllable low-cost (<350 USD) serial manipulators. By using a single hardware/software architecture, a <7 Degree of Freedom (DoF) TinyARM can be manually reconfigured to an operational >3 DoF robot within 10 min. Actuator modeling and dynamic compensation enable torque-controlled applications like mixed-reality impedance control teleoperation and simulator force feedback rendering. Experiments include mechanical benchmarking and real-world force-aware telemanipulation. The TinyARM-7 has a payload of 33.5 g, a max speed of 0.77 m/s, and a reach of 210 mm. Moreover, with dynamic compensation, the robot has a backdrive-breakaway force of 1.4 N and a backdrive-running force of 0.7 N. Additionally, Cartesian-Impedance Control (CIC) attains a translational stiffness of >15 N/m. Lastly, the TinyARM-X stack is open-sourced to disseminate accessible desktop-scale torque-controlled robotic manipulation to the community.

candidates.title: Lost Between Mind, Model Collaboration, and Motion: Understanding and Measuring Cross-Model Action Misalignment in Commercial Robots
candidates.abstract: Embodied robots increasingly rely on large language models (LLMs) to interpret user intent and coordinate with robot-specific action models for physical interaction. This multi-model pipeline creates a critical semantic boundary across mind, model collaboration, and motion: semantic consistency may break between what the large model understands, how the small action model translates that understanding into executable commands, and what physical actions the robot ultimately performs. As a security consequence, commercial robots may execute unintended physical actions even when user inputs contain no explicit action commands. To measure this problem, we develop TARS, a black-box framework that explores the command-reasoning-action pipeline and automatically discovers and validates unintended physical behaviors. We evaluate TARS on four commercial robots across 44 experimental settings, conducting 133,400 executions. TARS uncovers widespread cross-model action misalignment and achieves up to 94% verified action coverage.

candidates.title: MUSEMENTS TOWARDS A SCENIC HUMOR MACHINE: BARCO SEM LEME
candidates.abstract: The first impotence of the machine was pointed out in 1887 when Peirce, in reviewing the logical machines of Jevons and Marquard, denied that they possessed originality or independent initiative: they neither identify their own problems nor sustain themselves. This initial machinic limit is explored through an archaeology that ranges from the Laff Box, which mimicked the laughter of live TV audiences in the 1950s, to the visionary conception of the TARS robot in Interstellar, where humor is one of several parameters adjusted by the interlocutor to govern the broadcast and interaction. By a “Musement” Machine inspired by the comedy scene of the Bavarian comedian Karl Valentin, in the scene “In the Recordstore”, where the anarchic customer at the record store, shows proto-musement. In the end, a Brazilian and world philosopher asks the audience why they laughed at her: a boat without a rudder.

candidates.title: Development and validation of a low-cost, open-source robotic extrusion printing platform for acellular hydrogel scaffold fabrication: A step toward multi-axis robotic bioprinting
candidates.abstract: Commercial multi-axis robotic bioprinting platforms remain prohibitively expensive for many laboratories, limiting access to robot-assisted biofabrication. This study converted a low-cost six-axis industrial robot (ABB IRB 120T with IRC5 Compact controller) into an open-source robotic extrusion printing platform and compared its dimensional performance with a commercial robotic bioprinter (BioAssemblyBot 400). Validation was limited to acellular hydrogel and planar toolpaths; cell-laden and non-planar printing remain necessary for biological validation. The platform integrated a modified printhead, elevated glass print bed, solenoid-based extrusion control, and a software pipeline that translated slicer-generated G-code into ABB RAPID motion and I/O commands. Five scaffolds were printed using the developed platform and three using the commercial system with a 4% alginate–4% carboxymethylcellulose bioink. The retrofitted platform demonstrated higher repeatability, with a mean coefficient of variation of 2.25% and maximum dimensional range of 0.388 mm, compared with 5.07% and 1.130 mm for the commercial system. Scaffold-level analysis (n = 5 vs. n = 3) showed significantly lower macro-scale dimensional variance for the retrofitted system, while pore-scale variance was lower but not statistically significant. No statistically significant difference between platforms was detected for overall-dimension or Y-direction pore-width accuracy, whereas the retrofitted system showed better X-direction pore-length accuracy in the pooled analysis. The total development cost was $16,617, an 89.6% reduction relative to the commercial system. These findings demonstrate a technically viable, substantially lower-cost pathway to multi-axis robotic biofabrication, with remaining dimensional limitations likely tied to bioink processing and the absence of crosslinking rather than robotic motion control.

candidates.title: Hardware and Software Reconfiguration at Machine Levels
candidates.abstract: The value of a product is generated through a series of manufacturing processes within the material flow. These processes are executed by machines equipped with specific manufacturing capabilities. In Open Manufacturing (OM), machines must therefore be capable of performing a wide range of tasks to support diverse products. Physical devices in OM are designed with the flexibility to adapt to changing requirements and varying task demands. This chapter classifies the enabling technologies that support machine flexibility into two major categories: software reconfiguration and hardware reconfiguration. Software reconfiguration technologies include: (1) Computer Numerical Controls (CNCs) and Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) for anticipated changes, and (2) data-driven programming approaches for unanticipated changes. Hardware reconfiguration focuses on reconfigurable systems such as reconfigurable machine tools, modular robotic systems, and flexible fixturing systems. Together, these technologies form the foundation for achieving the adaptability and responsiveness required in Open Manufacturing environments.

candidates.title: DeGenRESOLVE: An offline GUI ‐based automated nanopore sequencing pipeline for viruses with custom rule‐based indel and degeneracy resolution
candidates.abstract: Sequencing methods based on Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) have revolutionized the field of viral genomics. However, available analysis tools are often internet-dependent, have complex installation requirements, or lack graphical user interfaces (GUIs), limiting their use in laboratories with restricted internet access or limited bioinformatics expertise. Here we present DeGenRESOLVE, a pipeline designed for amplicon-based ONT resequencing where a reference genome is available. This pipeline does not perform de novo assembly but processes raw base-called ONT viral sequencing data offline in an easy-to-use GUI. The pipeline combines existing tools with a rule-based algorithm that applies user-defined criteria to positions the variant caller reports as ambiguous and to the insertions and deletions (indels) it proposes, logging every decision with its statistics. The application works with both segmented and non-segmented viral genomes. Tested on eight influenza A isolates with Illumina-derived genomes, the consensus agreed at 99.97% of positions with each isolate's own genome as reference, and 36 of 37 resolved positions agreed. With close genomes as references, 99.98% of called positions agreed. However, agreement decreased as the reference diverged. Where the hemagglutinin cleavage site differed in length from the reference, indel adjudication reproduced it in four of five isolates, against none without it. In known mixtures, an ambiguity code was retained only when the minor allele exceeded ~40%. In essence, the refined sequence is a dominant consensus, not a record of within-sample variation. Therefore, DeGenRESOLVE facilitates offline, reproducible, and auditable sequencing analysis, reducing ambiguity in consensus generation and minimizing reproducibility errors.

candidates.title: THE SECULARIZATION OF RECIPROCITY: SHIFTING SOCIAL SOLIDARITY AND ISLAMIC VALUES IN JAVANESE RURAL COMMUNITIES
candidates.abstract: Reciprocity is an integral component of rural life, traditionally synonymous with high levels of social solidarity. However, alongside the penetration of modernization and market logic into rural spaces, the traditional meaning of reciprocity has undergone a significant transformation. This study aims to analyze how the community of Karangsari Village perceives reciprocity within their ancestral traditions, specifically Sinoman, Sambatan, and Nyumbang, and to identify the shift toward new meanings in contemporary rural life. Employing a descriptive qualitative method, data were gathered through direct observation and in-depth interviews. The research findings reveal a significant shift in the meaning of reciprocity in Karangsari Village moving from a foundation of voluntary solidarity and religious obligation (ta'awun) toward a more symbolic and economic-rationalist orientation. This suggests that while traditional rituals persist, their spiritual essence is increasingly being replaced by transactional logic. This shift indicates that modernization does not necessarily abolish religious traditions; rather, it reconfigures them into secular social instruments within the framework of current rural modernity.

candidates.title: Receiver-Conditioned Clarification for Multi-Agent Food Assistance
candidates.abstract: Food insecurity creates a pressing need for guidance that helps households find usable food resources and assess food choices in light of their circumstances. Such guidance must connect eligibility requirements, practical access constraints, and dietary needs rather than return isolated listings or generic nutritional advice. Multi-agent food assistants can coordinate these tasks, with uncertainty indicating when clarification or verification is needed before a recommendation. However, uncertainty can be lost across agent handoffs, allowing tentative interpretations to propagate as facts and obscuring opportunities for correction. Moreover, confidence that a service requirement has been interpreted correctly is not confidence that a recommendation satisfies the user's needs; local confidence cannot simply be reused as downstream reliability. We introduce an inference-time, receiver-conditioned clarification framework that preserves shared premise identities and replays consistent interpretations across dependent agents. Each receiver exposes admissible decisions and remaining evidence obligations, so question relevance reflects both decision changes and missing support. Information questions and user-confirmable fallback adjustments are evaluated together with their anticipated follow-up interactions under shared budgets. This structure connects clarification to jointly supported plans for resource navigation, nutritional reasoning, and supply-side planning.

candidates.title: The Uncompromised Citizen — Chapter 11: The 11 High-Stakes Checks — Companion Materials (Coming Soon)
candidates.abstract: COMING SOON — Chapter 11: The 11 High-Stakes Checks This document is the companion-material placeholder for Chapter 11 of The Uncompromised Citizen: The Field Guide for Ordinary Decision-Making, by Citizen111. When a decision could cause serious harm, damage critical systems, or create consequences that are difficult to reverse, ordinary decision-making may not be enough. The 11 High-Stakes Checks help readers examine changing conditions, verify assumptions, recognize warning signs, test safeguards, and ensure someone has the practical authority to stop when necessary. Planned companion materials: Heroes of Agency: Eleven historical case studies, including Chesley “Sully” Sullenberger and Jeffrey Skiles, Frances Oldham Kelsey, and Rick Rescorla—people who demonstrated preparation, independent judgment, and responsibility under pressure. The More You Know: The eleven checks, the Stop Test, cascading failures, independent verification, and six practical scenarios. Printable Exercises: The “Before You Say YES” worksheet and printable High-Stakes Check Card for examining risks, changing conditions, missing evidence, and stop authority. Deeper Dives: Aviation and industrial safety, medical decisions, rushed public projects, automated denials, AI and robotics, and the importance of maintaining meaningful human oversight. References: Original records, historical investigations, safety findings, supporting evidence, and additional reading related to the eleven historical cases and prevention of serious harm. These materials supplement—not replace—qualified expertise, established safety procedures, and appropriate emergency protocols. Additional materials, downloads, and links will be added in future versions. Part of the Mirror111 initiative. Read the full manuscript: https://mirror111.com/publications

candidates.title: HandUMI: A Modular Hand-Worn Parallel-Jaw Interface for Robot-Free Bimanual Data Capture
candidates.abstract: HandUMI captures robot-free bimanual demonstrations with a hand-worn parallel-jaw interface. Swappable fingertips match the robot's installed gripper; Quest/PICO controllers track hands and encoders measure aperture. Robot-agnostic recordings are retargeted by inverse kinematics to seven simulated bimanual arms (median position error $\leq 1.2$ mm; $\leq 4.7$% of episodes rejected). On bimanual towel folding, 562 robot-free demonstrations train policies on real PiPER arms: ACT succeeds in 12/20 attempts and fine-tuned $π_{0.5}$ in 7/20; ACT on the first 101 and base $π_{0.5}$ each succeed in 0/20. Hardware and software are open source (Apache-2.0), and a pair costs USD 557 with Quest 3S, excluding the optional ZED Mini and host computer. Project website: https://murobotics.ai/research/handumi.

candidates.title: Collecting Infrastructure-Level Measures for Energy Analysis in Modern Computing Infrastructures
candidates.abstract: Modern HPC facilities are complex environments in which all components are tightly coupled; consequently, precisely modeling and accounting for energy consumption requires approaches that go beyond instrumenting individual compute nodes. Aiming for a cluster-wide vision, we designed a scalable data collection pipeline that aggregates fine-grained measurements from multiple subsystems-spanning component loads, software and hardware counters, sensors and energy-ensuring consistent sampling frequencies and synchronized data acquisition across the infrastructure. We present a dataset of comprehensive metrics collected at 1 Hz over one month from a production research data center supporting heterogeneous workloads, including HPC, Kubernetes services, and distributed storage. To illustrate what this approach makes possible in practice, we analyze two case studies-distributed I/O and large-language-model inference-showing how cluster-wide measurement reveals system-level dynamics missed by localized instrumentation. The proposed dataset and collection methodology provide a foundation for future work on predictive modeling, energy-aware resource management, and more efficient computing infrastructures.

candidates.title: Research on application of live insulation cleaning technology for electrical cabinets of heavy-duty track maintenance machinery
candidates.abstract: Purpose Heavy-duty track maintenance machinery, including ballast cleaners, rail grinders and tamping machines, operates under harsh working conditions mixed with dust, iron filings and oil contamination. Pollutants easily adhere to circuit boards, terminal blocks, wiring harnesses and switch components inside electrical cabinets, resulting in reduced insulation resistance, equipment overheating, electrostatic discharge and frequent short-circuit faults. The conventional method of manual air-blow cleaning with the power disconnected suffers from low cleaning efficiency, high operation and maintenance costs and heavy downtime losses. Design/methodology/approach Supported by a dedicated scientific research project jointly undertaken by the Science and Technology Research Institute of Daqin Railway Co., Ltd., Taiyuan Track Maintenance Machinery Depot, Taiyuan University of Technology and Shanxi Angtuo Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd., this paper systematically presents the development approaches, key technologies, performance parameters of the complete cleaning equipment, field test data and comprehensive benefits of the integrated live insulation cleaning system for electrical cabinets of heavy-duty track maintenance machinery. The contamination-induced insulation degradation mechanism is analyzed; comparative tests against competing mainstream cleaning technologies are conducted, and statistical hypothesis testing is adopted to assess the significance of the observed differences. Findings The project developed an integrated live cleaning system comprising a high-insulation, eco-friendly cleaning fluid, an intelligent high-pressure cleaning main unit and an extended universal cleaning spray gun. Originality/value The research findings show that electrical cabinets can be cleaned in depth while the equipment remains energized. The technology's cleaning efficiency is more than seven times that of conventional manual power-off cleaning; the insulation impedance of the equipment is increased by four times, electrostatic hazards are significantly mitigated and the equipment failure rate is reduced by 55%. A statistical t-test demonstrates that the improvements in insulation impedance, operating temperature and static voltage are statistically significant (p < 0.05). The technology substantially shortens maintenance downtime, balances safety, production efficiency and full-lifecycle maintenance requirements in railway track maintenance, and can provide a standardized technical solution for predictive maintenance of electrical systems of heavy-duty track maintenance machinery across China's railway network. It should be noted that this technology focuses on post-contamination remediation cleaning; further research is required to develop a quantitative contamination degradation model to enable full-scale predictive early warning.

candidates.title: Lightweight stacking ensemble with enhanced cheetah optimization for IoT botnet detection
candidates.abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has been extensively used for various applications all over the world. The (IoT) network experiences continuous expansion with thousands of new devices being connected on a daily basis. Being the most accessible kind of network also brings security concerns. One of the severe threats being faced in this network is botnet attacks. IoT is a resource-constrained device, and reducing high resource consumption is an important crisis to be addressed. Conventional machine learning-based botnet detection systems exhibit high computational demands, while deep learning architectures further amplify resource consumption in IoT ecosystems with strict energy and memory limitations. This paper proposes a lightweight ensemble model for efficient detection of botnet presence on IoT devices using modified Cheetah Optimization Algorithm (COA) for feature selection along with an ensemble model consisting of Adaptive Boosting (AdaBoost) combined with eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) classifiers along with a Random Forest meta-learner. To overcome the limitations of the conventional COA, an enhanced COA is proposed by incorporating early stopping, dynamic population adjustment, chaotic initialization, opposition-based learning, and Lévy flights, resulting in faster convergence and improved optimization performance. For mitigating class imbalance problem, Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique with Edited Nearest Neighbours (SMOTE-ENN) is used. The experiments are evaluated on a stratified sample of approximately 3 million records of the Bot-IoT dataset. Experimental results show the model achieves 99.52% accuracy, 99.98% precision, 99.75% F1-score, and 99.52% recall. The model storage requirement is only 649.6 KB, with an inference time of 12.08 μs per sample, proposing an effective modified optimization technique for lightweight botnet detection in IoT, outperforming existing approaches.

candidates.title: Non-Imaging Optical Tactile Sensors for Robotics: Transduction Principles, System Integration, and Robotic Applications
candidates.abstract: Non-imaging optical tactile sensors encode contact through changes in optical intensity, wavelength, spectra, or photon counts, offering diverse architectures for robotic touch. Their usefulness depends on whether contact variables can be reliably distinguished from coupled mechanical and environmental effects, and whether the resulting information can be delivered in time to guide action. This review develops a unified framework linking mechanical load transmission, optical encoding, readout, and tactile inference to robotic task requirements. It examines reflective and waveguide-based devices, micro/nanofibers, fiber gratings, interferometric and resonant structures, and mechanoluminescent composites. Three considerations emerge across these approaches. First, high optical sensitivity supports accurate tactile estimation only when target variables remain identifiable under the relevant contact and calibration conditions. Second, spatial coverage and feedback timing must be assessed at the system level, accounting for multiplexing, acquisition, demodulation, and inference. Third, device characterization, offline recognition, and closed-loop robotic performance provide distinct levels of evidence and require different evaluation criteria. Representative studies illustrate how these considerations shape force estimation, contact localization, slip correction and distributed interaction. This review concludes with priorities for calibration transfer, reliable interfaces, scalable readout, and task-based validation, providing a basis for selecting and developing non-imaging optical tactile architectures for robotics.

candidates.title: Early US Experience Using the Symani for Robotic‐Assisted Microvascular Surgery
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Robotic-assisted microsurgery provides motion scaling, tremor filtration, and enhanced visualization, offering potential advantages for complex microsurgical tasks. Following Food and Drug Administration authorization, the Symani Surgical System was introduced into clinical practice in the United States in April 2024. This study presents the first multi-institutional US experience with Symani, evaluating feasibility, reconstructive outcomes, and technical challenges during its inaugural year of use in the United States. METHODS: All robotic-assisted procedures performed between April 2024 and April 2025 at two tertiary academic centers were retrospectively reviewed. Demographics, clinical indications, flap type, and anastomotic details were extracted. Primary outcomes were anastomotic patency and flap loss. Secondary outcomes included overall surgical complications and conversion to conventional microsurgery. RESULTS: Twenty-seven patients underwent robotic-assisted microsurgical procedures. Median age was 51 [IQR 39-63] years; 55.6% were female, and 74.1% identified as White. Indications included oncologic reconstruction (48.1%), trauma (18.5%), degenerative bony disease (14.8%), infection (11.1%), peripheral vascular disease (3.7%), and morphea (3.7%). A wide variety of flaps were performed, most commonly deep inferior epigastric perforator (DIEP) (44.4%), free vascularized fibular grafts (18.5%), and scapular flaps (14.8%). Robotic assistance was employed for 27 arterial anastomoses (84.4%), three venous anastomoses (9.4%), and two nerve coaptations (6.3%). Anastomotic configuration was predominantly end-to-end (71.9%). No flap loss occurred. One patient (3.7%) required re-exploration for pedicle kinking. Two conversions to conventional non-robotic microsurgery were required (7.4%). CONCLUSIONS: Early US multi-institutional experience demonstrates the Symani system is feasible and safe across diverse reconstructive procedures, enabling reliable microvascular anastomoses and nerve coaptations with minimal complications and no flap loss.

candidates.title: Translating the Language of the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Primer
candidates.abstract: Translating the Language of the COVID-19 Pandemic is an essential Primer for translators, offering a comprehensive exploration of the terminology and language that shaped the global response to an unprecedented crisis. Divided into three insightful chapters, the book delves into the linguistic and technological dimensions of the pandemic. The first chapter, The outbreak , explores key pandemic terms like shelter-in-place , the new normal , and flattening the curve , reflecting significant events during the crisis. The second chapter, Migration online, examines the pandemic's impact on education and the arts, highlighting their transition to virtual platforms. The third chapter, Fire of genius, fuel of survival— inspired by Abraham Lincoln's lecture on Discoveries and Inventions —showcases global innovations that mitigated the pandemic's effects and analyzes the vaccine rollout, covering its successes and challenges. The book includes an English–French glossary of 1,500 pandemic-related terms, covering scientific and everyday language, along with appendices listing patents and links to virtual performances. A detailed index ensures easy navigation of topics. This comprehensive resource serves as both a Primer for translators on the language that defined the COVID-19 pandemic and a reader-friendly presentation of international mitigation technologies and innovations. This book provides a research-supported retrospective analysis with enduring relevance, and features a bilingual compendium of pandemic terminology with potential for expansion into additional languages. It is an invaluable resource for translators, linguists, and researchers seeking to understand the intersection of language, technology, and human resilience during one of the most challenging periods in modern history.

candidates.title: STARFARM: A hybrid, spatially explicit agent-based framework that couples crop physiology and socio-hydrology for exploring agricultural adaptation pathways in mega-deltas
K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
candidates.abstract: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen reasoning, we introduce Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), applying MoE to attention value projections, and softplus attention gating, a more flexible, theoretically motivated gate. Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters. We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2x without a separate draft model. Our release follows the LLM360 definition of open source for transparency and reproducibility: the full development history, including intermediate checkpoints from every training stage, pre-training data, training logs, and all training, evaluation, and infrastructure code, notably our production-scale xLLM framework for dense and MoE training and the RL360 reinforcement-learning stack. Beyond the data itself, we release and document in detail every pipeline that built it, the part of model development that open releases most rarely disclose. These pipelines produced roughly 10T synthetic pre-training tokens, showing that synthetic data can be a major ingredient of pre-training at scale. Four of the models share one 22T-token pre-training corpus and recipe, revealing consistent scaling behavior and enabling controlled studies of scale and sparsity. All artifacts are available at https://ifm.ai/k2/

candidates.title: Who Benefits From Robots? Gender and Technology on the Shop Floor
candidates.abstract: The introduction of robots has produced uneven benefits for workers with different skills, occupations, and genders. We examine a qualitative case study of a Norwegian auto‐supply plant to ask why gender inequalities often persist on the shop floor, even in a gender‐progressive institutional context. The introduction of CNC machines in the plant made machining more like the female‐dominated assembly line in skill and strength demands, yet machining remained male‐dominated, with higher pay and greater investment in automation compared to the assembly line. The authors argue that persistent assumptions about economic value and gendered institutions and practices explain these unequal outcomes.

candidates.title: EasyNav: A Modular Architecture for Real-Time Navigation Across Heterogeneous Robot Environments
candidates.abstract: Most robot navigation stacks implicitly bind mapping, localization, planning, and control to specific representations and data flows, yielding architectures hard to extend, compare experimentally, or reason about end-to-end timing. This is critical in heterogeneous scenarios, where multiple spatial representations, sensing modalities, and coordinate frames coexist and evolve at different rates. This paper presents a navigation architecture centered on an explicit, shared navigation state that serves as the sole interaction interface between modular components. Constraining mapping, localization, planning, and control to operate over this shared state enables interchangeable, representation-agnostic pipelines under explicit compatibility and timing contracts. We realize this architecture as EasyNav, an open source ROS 2 framework, and validate it through real-robot experiments, including indoor navigation with laser sensing and large-scale indoor-outdoor navigation with GPS and 3D LiDAR across multi-level routes. Compared with Nav2 under matched conditions, EasyNav reduces reaction latency from 377 to 33 ms indoors and from 71 to 8 ms outdoors, while also using less CPU and memory.

candidates.title: Repeated extreme heat events, childhood adversities, and children’s mental health and wellbeing in Nepal
candidates.abstract: Rising global temperatures are increasing extreme heat events, affecting physical and mental health. Evidence from low-resource settings on whether and how environmental, socio-economic, and infrastructural challenges linked to repeated heat events shape children’s lives and mental health remains limited. This study examined how children, caregivers, and community stakeholders perceived the effects of repeated extreme heat events on children’s mental health and wellbeing, barriers to coping, and local response strategies in heat-affected communities in Bara District of Nepal. This was an exploratory descriptive qualitative study using semi-structured interviews with 24 participants, including children, caregivers, teachers, health workers, and NGO staff from heat-affected rural and urban communities. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Participants perceived repeated extreme heat events to intensify environmental and socio-economic stressors, like water scarcity, unreliable electricity, contaminated water, food insecurity, and unsafe housing, placing significant strain on families. These stressors were associated with household tension, conflict and disrupted parenting, which participants linked to children’s exposure to adverse experiences like neglect and unsafe environment. ​Children were described as experiencing physical symptoms and mental health challenges​ attributed to periods of extreme heat, including psychological distress, reduced concentration, disrupted sleep, and lower school engagement. Socioeconomically disadvantaged households were described as facing greater challenges in coping with heat​. Families reported using coping strategies like behavioral adjustments, hydration, cooling practices, and community rituals, but relief was limited for the poorest households, while institutional responses were constrained by inadequate infrastructure and limited mental health support. Participants described extreme heat as intensifying interconnected environmental, household, and psychosocial stressors, which they linked to children’s exposure to adversity, and to mental health difficulties. Strengthening heat-resilient infrastructure, expanding school- and community-based mental health support, and improving local institutional coordination may help reduce these challenges. Not applicable.

candidates.title: Behavioral Assurance for Socially Deployed AI Agents
candidates.abstract: AI agents are increasingly deployed in socially consequential settings, yet existing evaluations provide limited assurance that they behave consistently with their intended characteristics across diverse interactions. We introduce an evaluation framework for measuring the behavioral consistency of socially deployed AI agents. The framework operationalizes agent behavior along five measurable axes and uses a standardized evaluation battery spanning six socially salient interaction settings to assess behavioral differentiation, consistency, and drift. Controlled persona configurations serve as experimental anchors, enabling systematic testing of whether intended behavioral differences persist across contexts rather than appearing only as stylistic variation. Preliminary analyses demonstrate measurable differentiation across configurations and suggest associations between behavioral profiles and interaction outcomes. By shifting the focus from persona design to behavioral assurance, this work provides a foundation for evaluating whether socially deployed AI agents behave as intended, consistently and measurably, across the situations in which users encounter them.

candidates.title: The Digital Commons and the Infrastructural Power of Generative AI
candidates.abstract: The use and construction of generative AI reshape how information flows in society and who controls it. This paper investigates these changes and assesses their potential repercussions for the future of our shared information infrastructure. The findings elucidate an emergent social dilemma in which the use and construction of generative AI tend to degrade and compete with our existing infrastructure, while also layering atop the commons new infrastructure that is, by its current design, centralised and mediated. Yet, alternative futures that preserve the collective nature of our infrastructure remain possible. As a first step toward such futures, this paper concludes by exploring interventions to promote a decentralised and unmediated generative commons.

candidates.title: Between Risk, Recognition, and Necessity: How Open-Source Project Maintainers Perceive and Navigate CVEs Through Reporting and Resolving Vulnerabilities
candidates.abstract: Researchers have investigated automated security impact and analysis techniques that leverage the content of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs). Understanding the perspectives of open-source software (OSS) project maintainers, especially those who historically lack a security background and have little to no targeted funding to secure OSS projects, is currently understudied. In this study, we investigate how OSS maintainers who have created or triaged security vulnerabilities perceive, use, and work around the CVE system. We use a mixed-methods approach through a listing survey (n 1 =77), a Likert-scale survey (n 2 =109), and interviews (n 3 =24) to identify and categorize 36 factors into OSS maintainers' perceptions of CVE value, challenges associated with CVEs, and wants for future vulnerability identification and resolution features. We find that fix prioritization and assessing project health are the most important benefits for OSS maintainers, while producing fixes and how CVEs lack project context are the most challenging to overcome. Despite this, OSS maintainers express adaptability and openness to alternative systems, provided that they offer credibility, visibility, and ecosystem compatibility, and most desire less hands-on involvement while evaluating vulnerabilities. This work has implications for the future design of inclusive, OSS developer-centered vulnerability disclosure infrastructures, and gives a comprehensive insight into how current aspects of vulnerability identifiers work or do not work for the OSS community.

candidates.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
candidates.abstract: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics. Its central challenge is to translate general-purpose reasoning into effective and verifiable actions under physical constraints such as limited reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable environment changes, and irreversible consequences. Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance. Furthermore, we identify the principles that carry over from digital to physical agents and the challenges that must be addressed to achieve reliable physical autonomy. On top of the Embodied System 2 and the evaluation framework, we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy: the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.

candidates.title: How robot gender shapes customer experience in phygital retail
candidates.abstract: As service robots populate unmanned retail settings, design choices shape customer experience. This study contributes to the Phygital Service Economy (PSE) literature by examining whether robot gender cues affect customer satisfaction, and whether this depends on the customer’s own gender. A moderated serial mediation model (PROCESS 83; N = 572) tested social presence and engagement as mediators and respondent gender as a moderator, as respondents evaluated male- or female-presenting robots in physical and digital forms. Robot gender had no direct effect on satisfaction; its influence operated indirectly through social presence and engagement, and only among male respondents, who perceived male-presenting robots as more socially present than female-presenting robots, interpreted through a social identity and similarity-attraction lens. These findings extend gendered HRI research into retail contexts, identify social presence as a key mechanism linking robot gender to satisfaction, and show that gendered robot design effects are conditional on customer gender.

candidates.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
candidates.abstract: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use. We find that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks: they transfer to an unseen robot, to the real world, and to novel instructions. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the model succeeds in 60% of our trials on a real dual-arm robot, whereas the base model succeeds in none. On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $π_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $π_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds in 57.4%. Finally, the model retains its general capabilities, with no measurable degradation on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. These results highlight robot-use reinforcement learning as a promising component of foundation-model post-training.

candidates.title: Designing an AI Companion: Preservice Teachers Learning to Teach STEM with Robotics
candidates.abstract: Research shows that preservice teachers’ self-efficacy to teach with technology impacts how they implement technology in teaching practice. In many countries, elementary teachers are expected to teach all STEM subjects, even though they have no undergraduate preparation in STEM. Therefore, an important goal of Teacher Education is to enhance elementary preservice teachers’ confidence to teach STEM subjects with technology such as Educational Robotics (ER). This conceptual paper reports on the theoretical foundations and structural design features of an artificial learning companion (ALC) designed to support preservice teachers learning how to teach STEM with ER. While ALCs have been reported to enhance students’ learning, motivation, and self-regulation, this paper responds to calls to explore ALCs as facilitators of learning by negotiation. The ALC design is therefore explained in terms of Vygotsky’s Sociocultural Learning Theory, specifically the Zone of Proximal Development, instructional scaffolding, and prompt engineering design. Generative AI (GenAI) will serve as an ALC to scaffold learning tasks such as coding. The ALC will function as a responsive scaffold by offering task-specific support through questions, hints, feedback, and reflection with gradual reduction in support as preservice teachers’ competence and confidence increase. This work illustrates how a GenAI ALC can simultaneously support preservice teachers as learners of STEM and as future STEM instructors. The paper provides STEM teacher educators with a concrete, adaptable model for embedding AI scaffolds into robotics-based learning to foster reflective and pedagogical thinking.

candidates.title: Organizational Structure with an Open Source Culture
candidates.abstract: Corporate open source contribution is often discussed in terms of total contribution volume or the presence of prominent maintainers. However, to understand whether an open source culture has permeated an organization, it is necessary to look not only at a small number of high-frequency contributors, but also at how many contributors exist outside that core across a wide range of activity levels, and whether the organization has created conditions in which people can participate upstream when needed. This paper reanalyzes one year of contributor-level contribution data previously obtained and preserved from CNCF DevStats. The dataset covers 3,159 contributors from 18 large IT companies that had been selected at the time from the CNCF Top 50 contribution companies based on having at least 10,000 employees. Contributor activity was divided into 13 bands increasing by roughly a factor of two, and further grouped into three categories: **Ad-hoc (1–16 contributions)**, **Active (17–512)**, and **Top (513 or more)**. This makes it possible to observe not merely “how many Top contributors exist,” but how contributors are distributed continuously from low-frequency to high-frequency activity as a **Contributor Activity Spectrum**. Across all 18 companies, 1,528 contributors (48.4%) were Ad-hoc, 1,160 (36.7%) were Active, and 471 (14.9%) were Top contributors. Among the five companies in the CNCF Contribution Top 10, the average number of contributors per company was 484, consisting of 232.6 Ad-hoc, 175.4 Active, and 76.0 Top contributors. The average declined to 86.4 contributors among companies ranked 11–25 and to 38.4 among those ranked 26–50. Furthermore, all five Top 10 companies had contributors in every one of the 13 activity bands, forming an uninterrupted continuum from low-frequency to high-frequency activity. In contrast, companies ranked 26–50 had an average of 3.1 empty bands within their activity ranges. Several showed a separation between low-frequency and high-frequency contributors, or a concentration in only a particular high-frequency band. The characteristic observed among higher-ranked companies is therefore neither “having only Heroes” nor “having everyone contribute equally.” Rather, they combine a strong core of contributors with large and continuous layers of Active and Ad-hoc contributors around that core. This suggests that these organizations may have established a state in which many engineers can make the contributions they need when they need to—in other words, a state in which they can participate upstream **ad hoc**. Such a state may be associated with company-wide rules that enable open source contribution, operational and support functions such as OSPOs, and a culture that recognizes contribution as a normal part of engineering work.

candidates.title: Recreating northeastern lifestyles in Osaka, Japan: interpersonal relationships through Bathing and Yangge dancing among Zanryu Koji
candidates.abstract: Background: The Zanryu Koji (残留孤児), Japanese children separated from their families during the 1945 Soviet invasion of Manchuria and raised in northeastern China, constitute one of East Asia's most historically complex diasporic communities. Resettled in Osaka from the late 1970s, this population negotiates a distinctive double displacement: culturally Chinese yet legally Japanese. Aim: This study examines how Zanryu Koji in Osaka recreates northeastern Chinese lifestyles through communal bathing and Yangge folk dancing, and how these practices shape their interpersonal relationships and cultural identity. Setting: A Zanryu Koji community association in Osaka, Japan, operating a weekly Yangge dance group and regular communal bathing routine. Methods: Qualitative semi-structured interviews were conducted with fifteen purposively sampled participants. Data were analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results: Four themes emerged: the bathhouse as a Third Space of unguarded belonging; Yangge as embodied cultural memory and relational infrastructure; role differentiation as the architecture of fictive kinship; and bodily practice as diasporic identity negotiation. Conclusion: Communal bathing and Yangge dancing function not as instruments of cultural preservation but as generative practices through which the community actively produces belonging, fictive kinship, and a distinctively diasporic northeastern Chinese identity in Japan. Findings advance theories of embodied belonging, the Third Space, and integration-based acculturation, with implications for policies that support older migrant communities.

candidates.title: Sex Robots, Misogyny, and Artificial Intimacy in Contemporary Speculative Fiction: A Posthuman Feminist Analysis
candidates.abstract: This article offers a posthuman feminist analysis of contemporary literary fiction featuring sex dolls and robots, including Sierra Greer's Annie Bot (2024), Jeanette Winterson's Frankissstein (2019), and Paolo Bacigalupi's “Mika Model” (2016). It examines how the design and commodification of artificial sexual companions reproduce cultural misogyny, sustain gender inequality, and reinforce feminised technological servitude. Drawing on Kathleen Richardson's critique of the sex robot and situating these texts alongside contemporary misogynistic discourse associated with figures such as Nick Fuentes and Andrew Tate, the article situates speculative fiction in direct relation to ongoing social and ideological formations. It argues that these works move beyond a feminist critique of sex robots as misogynistic commodities by tracing a progression from commodified spectacle to demands for recognition in the face of exploitation and, finally, to emergent autonomy, which recasts the sex robot as a contested figure suspended between objectification and ethical subjectivity.

candidates.title: The social life of robots: How body, mind, and social roles shape people’s responses to robots
Robotics for Persons with Intellectual Disabilities: A Review in the Indian Context
candidates.abstract: This paper explores the intersection of robotics and disability studies, focusing on its transformative potential for inclusion, rehabilitation, and education, particularly for individuals with intellectual disabilities (ID). Initial research, including Conti (2015), showcased the effectiveness of robotic models in enhancing support for persons with ID, while subsequent empirical studies (Shukla et al., 2019) confirmed their benefits for users and caregivers. The integration of humanoid robots in educational settings has demonstrated versatility I n diverse pedagogical contexts (Alemi & Bahramipour, 2019). Systematic reviews have further consolidated evidence of robotics' applications across social, cognitive, and physical domains, indicating a shift toward scalable, context-sensitive solutions. In India, recent advancements in robotics complement traditional therapeutic practices, enhancing motivation and communication for persons with intellectual disabilities (PwID). The study highlights innovative initiatives, such as robotic library services (Maddisetty, 2024) and the integration of artificial intelligence in education (Rajput et al., 2025), while addressing cultural perceptions and ethical considerations among special educators (Ashwini et al., 2024). The paper underscores the need for culturally sensitive approaches in adopting robotics, contrasting the distinct trajectories of robotics development in India and the West. While Indian initiatives focus on affordability and cultural adaptation, Western approaches prioritize socially assistive and rehabilitation technologies. This review aims to chart a path for inclusive, contextually relevant robotics in disability care, enriching the global discourse on this vital intersection.

candidates.title: Seal Peel Strength Evaluation of Biobased Plastic Films using a LEGO-Based Texture Analyzer Prototype
candidates.abstract: The study focuses on creating a cost-effective LEGO-based texture analyzer to assess the peel seal strength of biobased plastic films, addressing the demand for sustainable packaging. The prototype enables accessible testing for small laboratories and educational settings, promoting innovation. Its performance is benchmarked against commercial analyzers to ensure accuracy and reliability. The study applies three methodologies to assess the peel seal strength of biobased plastic films using the LEGO-based texture analyzer prototype. The LEGO prototype, made with LEGO Mindstorms Evolution 3 (EV3) which is the third-generation robotics kit (Evolution 3) released in 2013, featuring programmable bricks, motors and sensors, load cells, and Arduino boards, was designed to apply tensile force and measure seal strength, replicating the function of commercial analyzers. Biobased plastic films were blended with additives, cast to uniform thickness, and sealed under controlled conditions to assess adhesive performance through T-peel tests. A comparative analysis was conducted by calibrating both the LEGO prototype and commercial analyzers, focusing on parameters such as hardness, cohesiveness, and springiness. The statistical analysis revealed variations, which provided insights for enhancing the accuracy and reliability of the prototype. The study demonstrated that the LEGO-based texture analyzer successfully assessed peel seal strength, mimicking commercial analyzers. Additives such as glycerol and polybutylene adipate terephthalate (PBAT) affected the mechanical properties and seal strength of the films. Sealing conditions, particularly higher temperatures, improved adhesion. A comparison between the prototype and commercial analyzers highlighted discrepancies, leading to recommendations for design and calibration adjustments. Failure modes were influenced by material and sealing parameters. The study concludes that the LEGO-based texture analyzer is a budget-friendly substitute for commercial devices, delivering consistent peel seal strength measurements. Additives such as glycerol and PBAT affects film properties, and sealing conditions play a role in adhesion. Understanding failure mechanisms is crucial for enhancing biobased films.
