JEV-VAD: Efficient Semantic Endpointing via Task-First Conditioning and Decoder-Prefix Pruning
candidates.abstract: Semantic endpointing must distinguish a completed turn from a temporary pause, yet its binary output does not require the full generation pathway of an audio-language model. We propose JEV-VAD, an ASR-free framework that combines task-first conditioning, a scalar endpoint readout, and decoder-prefix pruning. The question and completion criteria are placed before audio tokens, allowing causal decoder attention to construct audio states conditioned on the endpointing objective. A dedicated scalar head maps the assistant-prefix state directly to a stop probability, removing transcript generation, answer decoding, and vocabulary-sized output projection. To reduce representation cost, decoder-prefix pruning physically retains only the initial decoder blocks. Matched head refitting then identifies which retained depths provide useful endpoint information under a common adaptation budget. The framework is built on Qwen3-ASR-0.6B and adapted through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning for calibrated decisions. Together, these components address input conditioning, output complexity, and decoder depth within one endpointing framework. Experiments on EOT-bench show cross-language transfer from English endpoint supervision and useful discrimination in shallow prefixes, supporting a selectable quality-resource trade-off.

candidates.title: Autonomous Trail Racing with a Bicycle Robot
candidates.abstract: Navigating off-road trails on a mountain bike requires diverse locomotion skills, including aerial maneuvers, cornering, and slip recovery, paired with sophisticated perception for scene understanding. Translating these capabilities to autonomous, two-wheeled robots remains a formidable challenge. We show that autonomous, high-speed trail navigation can be achieved through a single idea: encoding the trail as a semantic layer of the terrain. In simulation, this layer embeds the navigation task into the training environment; during deployment, it is reconstructed onboard from camera and LiDAR data. First, we introduce a unified learning framework that treats local navigation and locomotion as a joint optimization problem, bypassing the twist or pose command interface of classical control hierarchies. With fixed reward weights, the same framework produces both trail racing and agile parkour, shaped only through terrain semantics and episode length. Second, our perception pipeline combines a frozen vision foundation model with a lightweight dual-head decoder that predicts per-pixel terrain semantics and confidence scores, which are fused with LiDAR range measurements into an egocentric semantic elevation map at 30 Hz onboard an NVIDIA AGX Orin. We validate our framework on the Ultra Mobility Vehicle (UMV), a bicycle robot that autonomously raced across all sections of a kilometer-long, unstructured mountain bike trail at speeds exceeding 5 m/s and averaging 3.26 m/s. In simulation, our policy fails up to an order of magnitude less often than hierarchical baselines while driving faster.

candidates.title: sK/n: towards a seamful grammar of distributed sentience
candidates.abstract: This paper argues that technical sensing does not extend the human sensory system but instead establishes a distinct, non-experiential sensory regime. Rather than amplifying human faculties, sensor-based systems register, process and compute signals according to operational logics that are irreducible to embodied experience. To conceptualize this shift, the paper introduces sK/n as a media-theoretical figure that articulates the relationship between technical skin (sK) and human, embodied skin (n). sK/n marks a split sensorium in which heterogeneous sensing regimes become operationally entangled yet remain non-convergent, and is structured by translation, asynchrony and temporal disjunction. Drawing on examples from e-skin technologies, interface design, (soft-)robotic systems, and artistic practice, the paper shows how touch and tactile input are increasingly translated into data-driven processes. This transformation is framed as a shift from multisensual to multisentient configurations of sensing, in which sensing is distributed across bodies, technical infrastructures, and computational systems. Rather than describing the machine sensorium as a system in opposition to a unified human sensorium, the paper proposes sK/n as a media-theoretical grammar for analysing distributed, asynchronous sensing regimes.

Future AI‐Based Clouds and Internet of Things
candidates.abstract: Chapter 3 is dedicated to future artificial intelligence (AI)-based clouds and the Internet of Things (IoT). It covers the ITU framework for cloud and edge computing and cloud service models, including AI as a Service (AIaaS) and ML as a Service (MLaaS). Furthermore, it covers the architecture of AI cloud platforms, including cloud-native and AI-native cloud architectures, AI-based telecom cloud services, and the future telecom transition to AI-based cloud computing, including the evolution of ETSI network function virtualization (NFV) toward telecom clouds. It also addresses the role of AI in the IoT ecosystem and the impact of Big Data and AI on IoT, as well as edge AI and edge cloud computing in IoT. Furthermore, this chapter covers the IoT–AI functional architecture and the Industrial IoT–AI framework. Finally, it includes AI for IoT smart services, such as AI-enabled smart cities, as well as the integration of AI and V2X services.

candidates.title: An Empirical Study of Maintainer-Identified AI Slop Pull Requests in Free and Open Source Software Projects
candidates.abstract: The FOSS ecosystem has always relied on outside contributions, notably through issues or Pull Requests (PRs), to sustain itself. With the advance of GenAI, the barrier to contributing to FOSS projects has never been lower, leading to the emergence of AI slop PRs: low-quality, low-value generated PRs. Past studies have examined AI slop PRs through theoretical, platform-level, or practitioner-account frames, but not at the project level. To this end, this study investigates the incidence of maintainer-identified AI slop PRs in FOSS projects by focusing on PRs flagged as slop by maintainers. Using a mixed-methods approach, we trace the origins of maintainer-identified AI slop PRs, quantify their volume in FOSS projects, describe their characteristics, and highlight maintainers' reasons for flagging or closing them. Our results show that the volume of maintainer-identified AI slop PRs increased in mid-2025, peaking in May 2026. These PRs are mostly additive, rarely merged, and typically closed within 3 days. The authors of these PRs disclosed the use of AI in 14% of cases, with 1% disclosing after a maintainer's request. Most PRs are closed or marked as slop without any reason provided by the maintainer. Based on our open coding, reasons range from concrete elements, like build failures, to ideological or intuitive (i.e., "looks AI to me"). This exploratory study captures a phenomenon in its early stage and highlights GenAI's potential impact on FOSS, emphasizing the pressure it puts on maintainers and the need to shift current open-source development practices.

candidates.title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Water Security in Western Rajasthan: A Study of Selected Renewable Energy Companies
candidates.abstract: The western parts of Rajasthan experience water scarcity owing to the arid nature of the climate and low amount of rainfall in the area. As such, the CSR programs of renewable energy companies have immense importance in conserving the water resources as well as uplifting the rural population. This research analyzes the water-based CSR initiatives of Suzlon Energy Limited and Adani Green Energy Limited (AGEL) in western Rajasthan. Using the descriptive research methodology, the paper is based only on corporate annual reports and any other available corporate public reports. The analysis is conducted by classifying and examining company's interventions in pond construction, desilting, and construction of water infrastructure. It is found that both the companies have carried out many water projects; however, type of activities and places have varied in different financial years. Furthermore, it is found that there is a serious lack of information in the corporation's reports, especially about the number of beneficiaries and project viability in the long run. It is concluded that the water projects by CSR programs have great potential to increase water security of rural areas provided they are monitored constantly.

candidates.title: When does online vision-language inference help? A survey of socially aware robot navigation
candidates.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) and large language models are increasingly built into the navigation stacks of robots that share space with people, where the models read cues that occupancy maps omit, such as a raised hand or a conversing group. This survey organizes 41 cases reported from 2024 to 2026, 34 on socially aware navigation and 7 adjacent mechanism extensions, by where the model enters the stack: scene interpretation, cost modulation, subgoal or path proposal, hierarchical coordination, direct action output and offline transfer or generation. For each of these six patterns we describe representative systems and their reported results, and we review the datasets, simulators, benchmarks and metrics behind them. We then discuss what the reported comparisons establish about running the model online, separating system utility, component contribution and online necessity. In these comparisons, cue-aware systems improved the outcomes that hinge on their cue, although whole-system differences limit attribution to the VLM; in one offline study, a model selector helped on hard selections and hurt on routine ones; in one deployment, delayed advice stayed useful when fused with current plans; model-supervised students navigated without runtime teacher queries, but online, cached and distilled alternatives have not been compared with student computation included; and better answers have not yet been linked to better behavior. We also define an invocation ratio (model requests per control decision), propose a minimum reporting set for deployment comparisons, and outline open challenges in real-time reasoning, spatial grounding and safety.

candidates.title: The double-edged sword of virtual influencer anthropomorphism: a paradoxical framework of social presence and identity threat
candidates.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how the perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers shape consumers’ attitude toward virtual influencers through the competing psychological pathways of social presence and identity threat. Design/methodology/approach Through a cross-sectional survey, a sample of 448 Instagram users in Egypt was collected and analyzed using CB-SEM through AMOS v.23. Findings Both perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers have a positive influence on both social presence and identity threat. Importantly, both social presence and identity threat concurrently mediate the relationships between both dimensions of anthropomorphism and attitudes toward virtual influencers. Therefore, both dimensions of anthropomorphism influence consumers’ attitudes toward virtual influencers through the positive mediating role of social presence and the negative mediating role of identity threat. Research limitations/implications The study expands anthropomorphism research to the virtual influencer context by showing that anthropomorphism is not unequivocally superior. Therefore, grounding in social presence and social identity theory, we suggest that anthropomorphism is a double-edged sword in shaping attitudes toward virtual influencers. Practical implications Both designers and marketers employing virtual influencers should consider the multi-dimensionality anthropomorphism. Moreover, they should aim to maximize social presence while reducing identity threat when utilizing virtual influencers. Originality/value This study conceptualizes anthropomorphism as a multifaceted construct composed of physical and psychological dimensions and it can work through two opposing positive and negative pathways.

candidates.title: The Positronic Aid: The Servitude of Robotic Altruism in Asimov’s I, Robot
candidates.abstract: Science fiction is one of the types of speculative fiction that traverses imagination based on discoveries, scientific techniques, and principles. It is an emerging field in this modern world. It encourages imagination and creativity, allowing authors to envision worlds, technologies, and societies that defy conventional norms and expectations. It challenges many critical interventions on future and the possibilities of science and technology. Today, technology has developed very well. Artificial intelligence is ruling the world of technology till date. Many robots are being developed in many countries. They resemble human beings in general. They do many works like human beings and are also capable of doing things that humans never thought of. They talk and act like humans and possess a lot of memory. One of the biggest achievements in the field of science and technology is the invention of robots. They are developed for the betterment of humans. They can’t replace humans at any cost and are in no way inferior to humans. This research paper discusses the advantages of robots in the present scenario. The book taken into study is I robot by Isaac Asimov. Robots are always beneficial to the entire human race. They are not produced to harm anyone.

candidates.title: Active Inference and Predictive Processing for Skill Learning: Implications for Skill Acquisition in Coaching Practice
candidates.abstract: This paper explores the potential of the Active Inference Framework (AIF) and Predictive Processing (PP) to advance our understanding of skill and motor learning with a key focus on introducing these concepts to coaches and highlighting their practical implications. Conceptual frameworks such as Information Processing (IP) and Ecological Dynamics (ED) have contributed significantly to the field of skill acquisition. Despite recent efforts to reconcile these perspectives, however, their fundamentally different theoretical foundations concerning perception, cognition and learning processes pose substantial challenges for integration. Although ED has made valuable contributions through its focus on perception-action coupling and direct interaction with the environment, it involves adopting a radical ontological stance that emphasises rejecting traditional cognitive constructs that can complicate practical applications in coaching. Conversely, IP's reliance on concepts such as stored motor programs and the view of the brain as a computer-like processor can limit its ability to account for the dynamic, emergent nature of skill acquisition in real-world contexts. We suggest that AIF offers a parsimonious perspective, accommodating the dynamic, embodied and enactive nature of skill acquisition without the necessity of committing to either framework's specific assumptions. This perspective provides practitioners with a coherent and flexible framework for understanding and designing skill learning interventions, offering a practically useful account of skill acquisition for coaching practice.

candidates.title: MSDT v1.0: an open-source multi-method snow drought toolbox
candidates.abstract: Snow drought, characterized by anomalously low snow water equivalent (SWE) relative to climatological conditions, has become an increasingly important cryospheric hazard with substantial environmental and socio-economic impacts. Although numerous snow drought identification methods have been developed, existing implementations are typically fragmented into independent scripts and region-specific workflows, hindering methodological consistency, reproducibility, and systematic intercomparison. Here we present the Multi-method Snow Drought Toolbox (MSDT), an open-source Python software package that provides an end-to-end workflow for snow drought research, encompassing SWE data acquisition, multi-method identification, data visualization, and comparative analysis through an intuitive graphical user interface. MSDT integrates seven widely adopted snow drought identification methods spanning yearly, monthly, and daily temporal scales, with flexible and adjustable parameters that enable users to tailor analyses to different climatic regions and research objectives. The toolbox streamlines data access by supporting automated downloading of state-of-the-art SWE datasets together with a curated catalog of commonly used products, and further supports interactive geospatial visualization for data exploration and methodological comparison. In addition, the toolbox adopts a memory- and performance-efficient architecture that supports large spatiotemporal datasets while maintaining responsive snow drought computing. Its modular architecture enables straightforward integration of additional datasets and identification algorithms. We demonstrate the capability of MSDT using ERA5-Land SWE data to reproduce global snow drought climatology, temporal variability, and representative historical events documented in previous studies. The results show that MSDT consistently reproduces published snow drought characteristics while substantially improving computational efficiency, workflow reproducibility, and methodological comparability. By providing a standardized, extensible, and user-friendly platform, MSDT lowers technical barriers and facilitates reproducible snow drought monitoring, model evaluation, and impact assessment.

candidates.title: BioMARS 2.0: a robotic biologist for formulating and adapting biological experiments
candidates.abstract: Biological experimentation is not reducible to a single optimization problem, but requires decisions at multiple levels of abstraction: translating scientific knowledge into experimental procedures, adapting culture conditions to measured phenotypes and selecting interventions that test biological hypotheses. Automating experimental execution does not, by itself, determine which experiments should be performed next or how they should change in response to biological feedback. Here we introduce BioMARS, a human-in-the-loop multi-agent robotic system that connects knowledge-guided experimental decision-making with robotic execution and biological feedback. At the procedural level, BioMARS generated literature-grounded protocols and traceable action plans, improving expert-reviewed protocol quality scores across four model backends. At the parametric level, BioMARS used image-derived phenotypes from robotic retinal organoid culture to select subsequent experimental conditions, with higher reported scores in later rounds of the three-round experiment. At the intervention level, BioMARS nominated drug-repurposing candidates from biomedical evidence and advanced six candidates to wet-lab testing by researchers. Together, these studies demonstrate feedback-driven robotic biological experimentation within a framework that supports decisions about experimental procedures, culture conditions and biological interventions.

candidates.title: ExoStack: A Modular and Reconfigurable Software Framework for Wearable Robotics Using ROS 2
candidates.abstract: Wearable robots depend on a software chain that links body-worn sensing to gait interpretation, assistance generation, and actuation. Personalization further requires each measured response to remain associated with the assistance parameters that generated it. This paper presents ExoStack, a modular ROS 2 framework for implementing that chain across embedded hubs and a host computer. Its Embedded Sensing and Actuation (ESA) library configures ESP32 boards as microROS sensing and actuation hubs. ExoCore supplies multi-hub synchronization, gait-event detection, profile generation, motion planning, cost evaluation, and human-in-the-loop (HIL) optimization as configuration-instantiated nodes. The PASE desktop application edits configurations, launches the processing stages, and visualizes ROS 2 topics. Hardware drivers and algorithm plugins can be added through defined interfaces without modifying the generic processing nodes. We characterize hub and planner timing on three embedded computers and demonstrate reuse on two pneumatic exosuits.

candidates.title: Soft sensors based on artificial neural networks for advanced bioprocess monitoring
candidates.abstract: This study presents the development and validation of artificial neural network (ANN)‐based soft sensors for the online estimation of key bioprocess variables during fed‐batch cultivations of Pseudomonas putida KT2442 producing medium‐chain‐length polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA), sustainable biopolymer precursors for bioplastics production. Since variables such as cell dry weight (CDW) and PHA concentration are typically accessible only through offline laboratory analyses, soft sensors represent a promising tool for implementing advanced process analytical technology (PAT) strategies for monitoring and control. Historical experimental data from two nominal cultivations and two cultivations with non‐standard behaviour, including significant feeding perturbations, were used for model development. ANN‐based soft sensors were designed in both global and multi‐phase configurations, where dedicated models were assigned to individual cultivation phases. Model training and validation were performed using leave‐one‐batch‐out (LOBO) cross‐validation to assess robustness and generalization capability. The best‐performing soft sensors achieved normalized root‐mean‐squared errors of approximately 4% for both CDW and PHA concentration estimation. The highest prediction accuracy was obtained for models utilizing capacitance measurements as input variables, followed by models combining capacitance measurements with cumulative oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production data. CDW soft sensors demonstrated higher robustness, maintaining reliable performance even for cultivations with non‐standard trajectories, whereas PHA soft sensors showed substantially higher sensitivity to process deviations and perturbations.

candidates.title: Pax Lambayeque? Trauma, interpersonal violence, and environment over 3,000 years in the Lambayeque Valley Complex, Peru
candidates.abstract: Previous research at archaeological sites in the coastal desert of northern Peru suggests strong human behavioral responses to environmental shifts. For example, at the Huaca de la Luna, Sicán, and the Huanchaquitos-las Llamas sites, paleopathological and stratigraphic analyses suggest that sociopolitical elites organized mass human sacrifices between 550−1450 CE in response to sudden intense increases in precipitation, possibly caused by El Niño-Southern Oscillation events. However, there has not yet been quantitative research into the relationship between non-ritualized violence and precipitation over the longue durée. To investigate the role climate change may have had on driving violence in the Peruvian desert coast outside of episodic sacrifice events, as well as accidental injuries, we modeled the relationship between highland precipitation, El Niño flood frequency, and osteological trauma in the Lambayeque Valley Complex. We pull paleoclimate data from the CHELSA climate simulations, and paleopathological data from the extensive work of the Lambayeque Valley Biohistory Project, yielding a total sample size of 1,659 individuals from a period of over 3,000 years. Ultimately, we detect no strong evidence for an association between environmental factors and interpersonal violence and find that non-ritual violence in the Lambayeque Valley Complex was rare (1.6%). These findings support previous meta-analytical work in the south central Andes, which found similar results in coastal and middle elevation communities. This study not only adds to our understanding of the range of human behavioral responses to climate changes but also proposes the hypothesis that mass sacrifice in the Lambayeque Valley Complex was politico-religious in nature rather than a Malthusian consequence of resource stress.

candidates.title: Axiomatic Software Design for Industrial Automation Systems
candidates.abstract: Industrial control and automation systems (iCAS) are not only essential for automating and controlling industrial processes, but they also serve as transformative enablers of progress in modern manufacturing. Their seamless integration with operational systems enhances efficiency, productivity, and reliability while reducing human intervention and operational costs. However, this very integration—central to the transition toward smart, fully digitalized factories and initiatives such as Industry 4.0—introduces an additional layer of complexity. This complexity demands greater flexibility from iCAS, making an anti-coupled design approach increasingly critical. This thesis aims to improve the software design of industrial control and automation systems by systematically addressing the persistent problem of coupling in current design practices. From the perspective of this study, a good design is one that satisfies all functional requirements while adhering to Suh’s two fundamental design axioms: the Independence Axiom, which ensures the elimination of coupling, and the Information Axiom, which evaluates the design’s complexity. Importantly, the Information Axiom can be meaningfully applied only after the Independence Axiom is satisfied; without functional independence, any assessment of design complexity becomes invalid. For this reason, the primary focus of this thesis is on the first axiom—developing and formalizing the principles of anti-coupled design for industrial control and automation systems through a systematic design framework based on axiomatic design theory. Building on axiomatic design theory, this research introduces a systematic method ology that guides iCAS designers from the highest level—interactions among design elements—to the lowest level—the candidates.title: Tutorial: Vision-Based Formation Control with Differential-Drive Robots
candidates.abstract: This tutorial presents a step-by-step introduction to multi-robot formation control using differential- drive robots, an overhead camera, and Python. ArUco markers are used to estimate robot positions and orientations, while desired pairwise displacement vectors define a circular formation. By comparing measured and desired relative positions, the controller computes movement vectors that are converted into differential-drive wheel commands, with basic proximity-sensor-based obstacle avoidance. The tutorial guides readers through hardware and software setup, robot pose estimation, formation geometry, feedback control, system integration, and formation-error evaluation. Motivated by the need to bridge the gap between theoretical understanding and practical implementation in robotics education, we emphasize how mathematical concepts are translated into coordinated behaviors on physical robots. Although the implementation uses a specific robotic platform, the underlying perception and formation-control principles can be adapted to other differential-drive robots and simulation environments. The accompanying open-source GitHub repository provides the Python implementation, setup instructions, and demonstrations to support hands-on learning and further exploration of multi-robot systems.

candidates.title: BUT telepresence: a fully open-source VR framework for low-latency stereoscopic video streaming with end-to-end latency instrumentation
candidates.abstract: Advances in immersive telepresence have enabled compelling virtual reality (VR)-based teleoperation, yet existing systems remain difficult to reproduce, inflexible in their streaming configuration, and largely devoid of end-to-end latency instrumentation. Current research prototypes typically rely on fixed encoding parameters, do not expose a unified interface for real-time reconfiguration, and rarely support hardware-accelerated decoding on standalone VR headsets. As a result, the community lacks an open, validated reference framework for low-latency stereoscopic teleoperation. This paper introduces a fully open-source VR telepresence system that integrates stereoscopic capture on a two-degrees-of-freedom (2-DOF) camera module, low-latency encoding using GStreamer, head-coupled camera actuation, and a native OpenXR application capable of hardware-accelerated decoding on modern standalone VR headsets. A key contribution is a built-in end-to-end latency instrumentation mechanism that timestamps each stage of the pipeline and embeds these measurements into the media stream, enabling continuous monitoring by the VR client. This information enables the user to dynamically adjust codec, resolution, and frame rate to maintain stable operator perception under heterogeneous network conditions, including wireless links. The framework is validated in representative robotics scenarios, demonstrating reliable stereoscopic teleoperation with a measured instrumented end‑to‑end latency of approximately 79 ms on a quiet 6 GHz link and 101 ms with the operator’s link saturated by competing traffic, with the VR headset’s pose prediction helping, in informal use, to mitigate perceived delay for the operator. Because every pipeline stage is timed individually and the reported total is their sum, the instrumentation also localizes degradation to individual components: contention is shown to act almost entirely on receiver-side decoding and not on transport, and reducing frame rate under loss is shown to be counterproductive, neither of which is visible from aggregate latency alone. A pilot evaluation with operators closes the loop from instrumentation to end user: the framework imposes a latency condition, verifies per participant from its own telemetry what was delivered, and records the operator’s presence, workload and task performance on the same sessions. All software, including benchmark datasets and Grafana dashboard configuration, is released publicly at https://github.com/Robotics-BUT/BUT_Telepresence to support reproducibility and future research.

candidates.title: Seventy years of parasocial research: a bibliometric analysis and science mapping, 1956–2025
candidates.abstract: Research using the term ‘parasocial’ has appeared since 1956 in media studies and psychology and, more recently, in influencer marketing. This study maps the development, intellectual structure and recent thematic direction of the 2174 journal works published from 1956 to 2025 that use the term ‘parasocial’ in its media sense. Using records from OpenAlex, it combines performance analysis with co-citation, bibliographic coupling, keyword mapping and topic analysis and tests the robustness of the main mapping results across alternative corpora, periods and network settings. Output increased from one article in 1956 to 521 works in 2025, and, by authors’ affiliations, the USA, Indonesia and China had the most works. Horton and Wohl’s 1956 article is cited by 63.1% of the works with a reference list. Under the main network settings, the most frequently cited references form two co-citation communities, which we interpret as a media-psychology foundation and an influencer-marketing stream; they differ in topic and in the age of their references, and the share of co-citation link weight between them increased across the three periods from 2014–2019 to 2023–2025. The keyword ‘Influencer marketing’ appears in 28.7% of the works published in 2023–2025; in that period the topic ‘Digital Marketing and Social Media’ exceeded ‘Media Influence and Health’, whereas across 2020–2025 the two were nearly equal (397 and 405 works). OpenAlex topic labels identify AI-related topics in 3.0% of the works from 2023–2025. A separate language-model-assisted classification of titles and stored abstracts classified 71 of these works (6.3%) as studying a parasocial bond with an artificial partner; the author examined every such case individually. Together, the widely shared cited reference, the rising co-citation between the two communities and the application of the concept to influencers and artificial agents offer a frame for comparing which conditions of a parasocial bond studies keep and which they change; how studies define or measure the phenomenon, and whether the concept applies to artificial agents, are questions that future content analyses and experiments could examine.

candidates.title: AI companions, human concerns: a pragmatic perspective
candidates.abstract: The rise of agentic AI and so-called AI companions introduces a shift in the modes of interactions between humans and machines. The exact contours of this shift remain unclear, but early signs of social, affective, and even romantic engagements demonstrate areas of potential benefit and potent harms to individuals and to the broader social fabric. A full appreciation of these benefits and harms demands a multi-perspectival account not only of technological innovation and emerging modalities of human-machine interaction, but also of the historical, socio-cultural, psychological, and ethical aspects of companionship. This essay provides such as account through a pragmatist perspective that considers the material, institutional, and psycho-social conditions behind the rise of AI. From this perspective, the essay broadens the notion of “alignment” as one between means and ends rather than the commonly accepted formulation between design goals and outputs. We argue that AI companionship blurs the boundaries between tools and social actors—a dynamic that emerges from the interplay of technical architectures, intentional design practices, user psychology, and political-economic forces. Given that interplay, a set of interrelated questions arise, which we address in three clusters (supply, demand, mediation), highlighting the emerging social and ethical dilemmas, and suggesting pragmatic interventions to inform public discourse and policymaking. In so doing, we hope to curtail the tremendous fallouts that have become evident in other domains such as social media only in retrospect, and ​to contribute to the creation of an environment conducive to social cohesion and individual wellbeing.

candidates.title: Virtual Smartphone Fan Fiction in the Age of AI: Technology Empowerment and Fan Culture Reproduction
candidates.abstract: This study examines virtual smartphone fan fiction, in which fans use large language models (LLMs) and front-end tools to create interactive smartphone interfaces. Through passwords, simulated apps, prewritten content, and AI-generated replies, readers explore a character’s digital space and participate in an unfolding narrative. Using the perspectives of technology empowerment and fan-culture reproduction, this study analyzes the shift from screenshot-based stories to operable interfaces, the redistribution of authorship, the production of virtual intimacy, and the limits imposed by AI models, community norms, and platform governance. It argues that interfaces and AI responses now help shape narrative rhythm and reader agency, while creators increasingly act as system designers. However, greater technical access does not guarantee cultural recognition. The reproduction of fan culture is therefore shaped by the interaction of creators, readers, interfaces, models, and communities.

candidates.title: Taxonomy-Agnostic Neurosymbolic Grounding of Robot Kinematics
candidates.abstract: While symbolic reasoning for task allocation requires grounding a robot’s physical capabilities, standard Unified Robot Description Format (URDF) files provide only low-level kinematics without the formal semantic context needed for reasoning. We present URDF2Ontology, an automated, taxonomy-agnostic neurosymbolic framework that transforms raw URDF files into populated, grounded OWL ontologies. It leverages a Large Language Model (LLM) for targeted semantic reasoning, coupled with an iterative sequential graph-purging mechanism to prevent context window saturation. To process complex kinematic structures, it employs a morphology-aware dual-track architecture featuring a bottom-up Tree Track for branching assemblies and a top-down Chain Track for serial limbs. Guided by neurosymbolic guardrails, the framework extracts functional sub-graphs and asserts populated ontologies aligned with arbitrary user-provided taxonomies. Empirical evaluation across a diverse fleet of heterogeneous robots demonstrates strong schema alignment, valid structural extraction, and a significant reduction in manual domain authoring overhead.

candidates.title: Advancements in Embedded Surveillance Robotics for Defense and Security Applications
candidates.abstract: In military applications, surveillance plays a critical role in ensuring security, particularly in isolated and border areas. This chapter presents a recent approach to surveillance using a robot for military applications. The planned methodology is to substitute soldiers in border areas with robots, to enhance the security and both autonomous and manual control via internet connectivity. Equipped with multiple sensors and various electronic devices, the robot is designed to detect enemy presence, capture camera footage, and live-stream data to authorized personnel. This robot enables armed forces to proficiently monitor isolated areas and respond immediately to potential threats. Human risk is reduced by using this type of robot surveillance system. Deploying robots in high-risk isolated areas minimizes personnel exposure to potential threats while maintaining effective surveillance. The use of autonomous technology increases operational efficiency by enabling continuous surveillance without requiring constant human intervention. By combining cutting-edge embedded technology, real-time monitoring, and remote operability, this robot vehicle delivers a consistent and effective solution for border or boundary security. Integrating advanced technologies, such as artificial intelligence (AI), embedded systems, and very large-scale integration (VLSI), will significantly enhance the capabilities and efficiency of the robot in armed forces. This robot provides not only a human-free system but also an efficient smart system to address military challenges.

candidates.title: Innovator 5.0: Integrating Design Thinking and Responsible Innovation into AI and Robotics Research Environments for Industry 5.0 and Society 5.0
candidates.abstract: Industry 5.0 and Society 5.0 call for a shift in AI and robotics development from a primary focus on automation and technical sophistication to holistic solutions that address human needs, social contexts, stakeholder perspectives, and broader societal impacts. Preparing future engineers for this shift requires educational approaches that connect technical development with design thinking and responsible innovation. To address this need, this study introduces Innovator 5.0, an educational framework that extends the Science–Engineering–Design (SED) model by incorporating responsibility (R + SED) within a design-thinking process. The proposed framework was implemented through seven embedded workshops during a five- to six-month international research internship involving nine undergraduate students across six AI and robotics projects. An exploratory post-programme evaluation examined participants’ design-oriented practices, perceived capability development, and experiences within the research environment. Participants reported high ratings across several evaluated dimensions, particularly for challenging problem statements before solution development (M = 6.78/7), systems thinking (M = 6.67/7), creative innovation (M = 6.56/7), contextual awareness (M = 6.33/7), and iterative revision (M = 6.11/7). They also highlighted project autonomy and facilitative mentoring as valued features, while limited direct stakeholder access was identified as an important implementation constraint. Together, these findings provide practical guidance for preparing engineers to consider the purpose, societal implications, and value of AI and robotics innovations alongside their technical feasibility, supporting people-centric and responsible engineering innovation.

candidates.title: The World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA): Hardware-Algorithm Co-Design for Embedded AI in Robotics
candidates.abstract: Embedded AI is moving from perception to prediction. Robots now use world models$\unicode{x2014}$learned simulators that predict the outcome of candidate actions in a compressed latent space before any is executed. Every predicted step must be computed on board within a tight power and thermal budget, yet the energy these steps fundamentally require, and how far real hardware sits from it, have not been characterized. We derive lower bounds on the arithmetic operations and the CMOS dynamic energy of a latent state transition from information theory and Boolean circuit complexity. Profiling a DreamerV3-style Recurrent State Space Model (RSSM) shows that every rollout operation is memory-bandwidth bound and that a GPU consumes at least $5.9\times10^{10}$ times the CMOS energy floor. Transient 3D thermal simulations show that this inefficiency is also a thermal one, since sustained back-to-back planning heats a millimeter-scale silicon tile to 556 K even behind an ideal copper heat spreader. Guided by this chain from bound to bottleneck, we propose the World Model Planning Accelerator (WMPA), a chip architecture for embedded world model planning that combines near-memory computation, real-time entropy estimation, variable-precision rollout units, and copy-on-write latent scratchpads. With a design target of 40x lower power, the same tile stays near ambient at 306 K in simulation, pointing toward practical planning on thermally constrained robots.

candidates.title: Into the Infinite Possibilities: Omar Yaghi’s Vision for Science in the Era of AI
candidates.abstract: 2025 Nobel Laurent Omar Yaghi is establishing a new center in Tsinghua University, aiming to transform chemistry and materials science through AI and robotics.

candidates.title: Digitalization of tax administrations in European Union: a multi-criteria analysis of digital performance and cross-country disparities
candidates.abstract: This study assesses the level of digitalization of tax administrations in the 27 Member States of the European Union, applying the PROMETHEE II outranking method to 16 evaluation criteria. Denmark and the Netherlands rank highest. The leading performers share a common profile: they have integrated advanced digital technologies, strengthened their technological infrastructure and developed integrated digital services, drawing on artificial intelligence, process automation, cloud computing, blockchain and interoperable information systems. The analysis also reveals marked differences among Member States, reflecting a complex mix of economic, institutional and technological conditions, including the availability of financial resources, government stability, the maturity of digital culture and the current state of information systems. The GAIA analysis identifies Robotic Process Automation (RPA) as the criterion most closely aligned with the overall ranking, while artificial intelligence and virtual assistants contribute positively, though more weakly, to the differentiation among tax administrations. Overall, the results confirm PROMETHEE II as a reliable tool for monitoring comparative digital maturity and as a useful decision-support framework for a coherent and sustainable digital transformation of tax administrations across the European Union.

Adventures in Reproducing and Integrating Open-Source: Developing Guidelines for Modular Software Components in Robot Grasping and Manipulation Pipelines for Picking in Clutter
candidates.abstract: When developing a novel software component of a robot system, researchers typically integrate open-source code for other components in the pipeline, such as perception, grasp planning, and motion planning. However, there are several bottlenecks related to the accessibility and reproducibility of open-source which are stifling research, development, evaluation, and deployment of robots. To this end, we are working to develop community-driven guidelines for modular components in robot software pipelines in the context of picking in clutter. In this work, we investigate reproducing and integrating multiple perception and grasp planning components used in vision-based perception-to-action pipelines. The architecture and methodology used to conduct these exercises are reviewed, highlighting issues encountered along the way. Recommendations for guidelines to improve accessibility, reproducibility, and integration of modular open-source components are shared related to the assets included in an open-source release, methods to modularize components, and practices for development and testing.

candidates.title: Regulatory governance and full-scale digital transformation for prediction-based food safety management: Global trends and future perspectives
candidates.abstract: Background The global food safety paradigm is shifting from traditional, reactive hazard control toward proactive, predictive risk management to address increasingly complex supply chain vulnerabilities. However, current digital implementations remain fragmented, creating structural bottlenecks that hinder the transition to next-generation regulatory science. Scope and approach To our knowledge, this study provides one of the first comparative critical analyses of the HACCP-based data governance frameworks of six major jurisdictions. We compare jurisdictions in which private actors play a relatively larger role in certification and implementation ('market-led': the United States, the European Union, Canada, and Japan) with those in which public institutions play a dominant role ('state-led': South Korea and China), positioned along a governance continuum in which all systems combine public and private functions, focusing on their capacity for real-time risk prediction, public-private data integration, and global interoperability. Key findings and conclusions The market-led systems examined tend to foster food safety culture but are affected by 'Data Silos' that limit actions to retrospective tracebacks. The state-led systems examined may enhance data integrity but can create a 'Data Island' paradox due to an over-reliance on automating isolated physico-chemical Critical Control Points. To overcome these limitations, we propose a conceptual framework for Full-Scale Digital Transformation (Full DX). Converging prerequisite programs, structured food safety culture assessment (e.g., Shapley-FAHP), and intentional threat mitigations (TACCP/VACCP) into an interoperable predictive network powered by ensemble machine learning could support a more resilient regulatory ecosystem for mitigating multidimensional global supply chain threats; this framework requires empirical validation.

candidates.title: Designing a Small Language Model Lexicon in Natural Language for Robotic Applications
candidates.abstract: In this paper, the aim is to present a project report of a method, based on which a small natural language lexicon is designed, or otherwise a small language model, for robotic applications. In this direction, a reference is made to Controlled Natural Languages, and their characteristics are determined for application in operational robotic vehicles. In addition, criteria are established for the selection of the nationality of the language, which constitutes the basis of the lexicon. A small introspection is made in the natural language unit of a human–robot interface, and a method is presented that examines the adequacy of the selected language in relation to the purpose of use of the system and the control criteria. The use of the lexicon’s method is presented, and an example of the analysis and inclusion of selected Greek language words is given. The reproduction of words from the lexicon’s stored data is also explained, as the reverse process that functions as a confirmation of the method. Received: 22 August 2025 | Revised: 20 April 2026 | Accepted: 12 October 2026 Conflicts of Interest The authors declare that they have no conflicts of interest to this work. Data Availability Statement Data sharing is not applicable to this article as no new data were created or analyzed in this study. Author Contribution Statement Ioannis Giachos: Conceptualization, Methodology, Software, Investigation, Resources, Writing – original draft, Visualization. Evangelos Papakitsos: Conceptualization, Methodology, Investigation, Resources, Writing – original draft. Nikoletta Samaridi: Investigation, Resources, Data curation. Michail Papoutsidakis: Validation, Formal analysis. Nikolaos Laskaris: Writing – review & editing, Supervision.

candidates.title: Insect-inspired hexapod robot with magnetically coupled compliant and modular drive system
candidates.abstract: Legged robots are increasingly inspired by insects’ ability to combine rigidity and compliance for agile, damage-tolerant locomotion in cluttered terrain. Herein, we introduce INSECTRON, a centimeter-scale hexapod robot that employs magnetic transmission to achieve robust mobility with minimal mechanical complexity. Each leg connects to the drivetrain via neodymium magnets, forming a self-aligning micro-clutch that transmits torque under normal load and safely slips under overload, while additional magnetic couplings between drive modules accommodate load imbalances and perturbations. Hall effect sensors provide proprioception for a phase-domain controller maintaining persistent anti-phase coordination. The magnetic transmission architecture introduces intrinsic mechanical adaptability, functionally analogous to biological preflex mechanisms, enabling rapid responses to external perturbations without additional control complexity. Experiments demonstrated stable locomotion across multiple slopes and substrates. Maneuverability was achieved through differential turning and spin-in-place. A minimum Cost of Transport (CoT) of 30 was achieved during locomotion experiments. Under vertical perturbations, INSECTRON autonomously recovered in over 90% of trials, highlighting strong passive impact tolerance. The architecture eliminates the need for precision alignment and mechanical fasteners, enabling tool-free leg replacement and rapid mechanical reconfiguration. This work establishes a scalable route toward modular, resilient, and field-deployable miniature legged robots for confined and uncertain environments.

candidates.title: Vision-Based Human–Computer Interaction System for Mexican Sign Language Recognition and Robotic Reproduction: Toward Inclusive Educational Applications
candidates.abstract: Mexican Sign Language (MSL) plays an essential role in communication within the Deaf community, yet access to sign-language learning resources remains limited in some educational settings. This study presents a vision-based Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) system for MSL recognition and robotic reproduction, developed as a proof of concept toward inclusive educational applications. The system uses an RGB camera and MediaPipe Hands for hand-landmark extraction, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) for recognition of 29 static classes, and a TimeDistributed-Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model for 10 dynamic classes. Recognized signs are mapped to predefined motion sequences executed by an ATmega2560-controlled robotic arm. Under stratified random and sequential partitioning protocols, the static model achieved accuracies of 100.00% and 99.88%, respectively, while the dynamic model achieved 100.00% under both protocols. Additional comparisons with Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Random Forest classifiers, using three random seeds, demonstrated competitive performance and low variability within the original single-participant dataset. To assess generalization beyond the training participant, a preliminary signer-independent evaluation was conducted with three previously unseen participants, without model retraining or adaptation. Across 585 recognition attempts involving 39 classes, the system achieved an overall accuracy of 89.06%, providing initial evidence of recognition performance across different signers. Furthermore, 92 accepted recognition trials successfully triggered their corresponding robotic sequences, demonstrating functional integration between recognition and actuation. These findings support the technical feasibility of the proposed contactless HCI architecture as a potential foundation for interactive MSL learning tools. Nevertheless, broader signer-independent validation and user-centered evaluations are required to establish its accessibility, usability, and educational effectiveness.

candidates.title: A Search for Exoplanets around Northern Circumpolar Stars. XI. A Planetary Companion around HD 112987 and a Planetary Companion Candidate around HD 58545
candidates.abstract: We present precise radial velocity (RV) measurements of the northern circumpolar giant stars HD 58545 and HD 112987 obtained over 8 yr with the Bohyunsan Observatory Echelle Spectrograph and supplemented during the final 3 yr by the Network of Robotic Echelle Spectrographs. RV variations in giant stars may arise from orbiting companions or intrinsic phenomena, including pulsations, chromospheric activity, and rotational modulation. To distinguish these possibilities, we analyzed line-profile variations, line bisectors, chromospheric activity indicators, and photometric data, and modeled the RV time series with Keplerian orbits using Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling. For HD 58545, the best-fitting Keplerian model yields an orbital period of 450.44 − 4.63 + 3.35 days and a minimum companion mass of 3.65 − 0.58 + 0.61 M J. For HD 112987, we derive an orbital period of 554.96 − 4.67 + 4.14 days and a minimum companion mass of 8.48 − 0.73 + 0.96 M J. None of the activity diagnostics for HD 112987 exhibits significant variability at the RV period, consistent with a Keplerian interpretation. In contrast, several activity diagnostics of HD 58545 exhibit periodicities comparable to the RV period, which is also consistent within the uncertainties with the projected rotational timescale, P rot / sin i = 462 ± 33 days. Thus, rotationally modulated stellar variability may contribute to the RV signal. Although the signal can be described by a Keplerian model, the current data cannot distinguish unambiguously between a planetary companion and intrinsic stellar variability. We therefore conclude that HD 112987 hosts a planetary companion, whereas further monitoring is required to determine the origin of the RV signal in HD 58545.

candidates.title: Intimacy Robots and Inward Decline: From Individual Symbolism to Civilisational Consequence
candidates.abstract: Philosophical work on intimacy robots has kept to two registers: the welfare of the individual user, and the symbolic wrong done to the classes of person such artefacts represent. Danaher’s symbolic-consequences argument, the fullest statement of the critical case, concedes that the downstream effects of that symbolism are hard to establish, and recommends an experimental posture. This paper takes the concession as its problem. The debate has no macro-social level of analysis, and without one it cannot say which consequences to look for. Drawing on the sociology of solidarity, Vallor’s account of moral deskilling, and the older literature of civilisational decline, it sets out three mechanisms by which individually rational uses of intimacy technology could aggregate into collectively costly outcomes: demographic subtraction, relational deskilling, and the habituation of desire to objects that cannot reciprocate. Each is put as a conditional with its defeaters named, not as a prediction. Tested against current evidence, including a nationally representative survey of adolescent companion-AI use and experimental work finding that AI companions do reduce loneliness, the third mechanism proves best supported analytically and the first least supported empirically. The result is a framework for aggregation, not a forecast of collapse; the paper closes by saying what would disconfirm it.

candidates.title: Open-HumanWAM: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
candidates.abstract: Egocentric human video offers a scalable source of manipulation priors for robot learning, yet translating raw data scale into generalizable robot policies demands rigorous data curation and training recipes. We introduce Open-HumanWAM, the first fully open recipe for scaling egocentric pretraining to 50,000 hours, anchored by Open-HumanWAM-50K---a curated egocentric video corpus densely annotated with hand motion and natural language. Leveraging this corpus, we systematically investigate pure human pretraining via closed-loop simulation evaluations and uncover an empirical log-linear scaling law linking pretraining data hours to downstream robot success rates. Grounded in these findings, we develop HumanWAM-Vanilla, a world--action model pretrained exclusively on 50k hours of egocentric human video. Upon robot post-training, HumanWAM-Vanilla reaches 92.08% success on RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Clean and 68.88% on Clean2Random, alongside a 14.17% mean success rate and a 19.00 mean progress score on RoboDojo. To push the capability frontier further, we explore joint human--robot pretraining with HumanWAM-Goal, a visual-goal-conditioned world--action model. Hybrid data scaling unlocks broad zero-shot generalization across both simulation and physical benchmarks, propelling post-trained RoboTwin 2.0 performance to new state-of-the-art levels: 92.70% on Clean2Clean and a substantial leap to 84.60% on Clean2Random. On physical robots, HumanWAM-Goal further exhibits emergent embodied in-context learning, dynamically adapting its manipulation behavior to unseen visual goals without parameter updates. To support reproducible scaling research in embodied AI, we open-source the Open-HumanWAM-50K corpus, data curation and pretraining pipelines, alongside the pretrained and post-trained HumanWAM checkpoints, inference code, and simulation evaluation suites.

candidates.title: Software-Defined Context-Aware Virtual Fixture for Teleoperation via Vision-Language Model
candidates.abstract: Precise teleoperation in unstructured environments remains challenging, because human errors and system-inherent limitations such as control jittering can significantly degrade task success and operational efficiency. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a software-defined Context-Aware Virtual Fixture (CAVF) system that leverages the open-world understanding of a Vision-Language Model (VLM). The proposed system automatically generates motion guidance for the robot end-effector (EEF) to assist teleoperation, preserving critical task-relevant motion while suppressing unnecessary translation and rotation components. This framework enables the autonomous generation of context-aware, haptic-free assistance without relying on handcrafted rules or physical force-feedback devices. Quantitative experiments in both simulation and real-world environments demonstrate that the proposed system significantly improves success rates, reduces completion times, and enhances trajectory efficiency compared to conventional teleoperation.

candidates.title: A human-centric large language model interface for monitoring and control of autonomous mobile robots via digital twins in industry 5.0
candidates.abstract: The diversity of industrial robot manufacturers, proprietary programming languages, and graphical interfaces complicates robotic system deployment and operation. This heterogeneity highlights the need for intuitive, accessible, and human-centric interaction methods. This paper presents a framework for natural language-based monitoring and selected control of autonomous mobile robots using a Large Language Model (LLM) interface, structured API communication, and digital twin visualization. The approach enables operators to interact with robots through natural language without requiring detailed knowledge of robot-specific interfaces or technical commands. The framework is evaluated from the operator’s perspective, focusing on its ability to simplify access to robot information, reduce interaction complexity, and support selected control tasks. Digital twin integration provides additional visual feedback on robot status and its operating environment. The proposed framework contributes to the development of more transparent, accessible, and human-oriented robotic systems aligned with Industry 5.0 principles.

candidates.title: V1: An Open-Source Shallow-Water Stereo Research ROV — Hardware Design Files and Software
candidates.abstract: V1 is an open-source remotely operated underwater robot developed initially for supervised shallow-water stereo data collection and intended for reuse in related shallow-water visual research. It combines commercial propulsion, flight-control and computing components with a single acrylic watertight enclosure, six thrusters and a common multilayer internal payload rack that can be withdrawn from the rear for equipment access. A custom stereo mount behind a shared flat front viewport provides 80, 100 and 120 mm nominal mechanical camera separations for manual selection and fixation before a task. This deposit provides an engineering-only distribution based on public source release v0.1.1 (4 November 2026). It includes 11 editable SolidWorks 2018 custom parts; DXF, STEP and STL exports; five editable R1 manufacturing-review drawings, associated custom models and PDFs; functional wiring diagrams; the bill of materials and cost basis; assembly, deployment and operating instructions; onboard acquisition/communication software; and selected offline calibration and processing tools. Temperature validation data, statistics, audit logs and thermal analysis scripts are excluded at the author's request. The original GitHub release and ZIP remain unchanged. PACKAGING_NOTE.md records the selected scope; manifest.json and SHA256SUMS are regenerated for this distribution. FILE_INDEX.md lists the actual 122 files, purposes and licences. Mixed licences apply by file: CERN-OHL-P-2.0 for hardware and functional wiring; MIT for supplied engineering software; and CC BY 4.0 for project-authored documentation, BOM and metadata. Original licence texts, directory notices and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md remain authoritative. Commercial reference CAD, private complete assemblies and separately licensed upstream drivers, kernels, SDKs and SLAM algorithms are excluded. York-Tank is a separate research output associated with https://doi.org/10.3390/s26206567. Its complete raw dataset is not included in this hardware archive. The supplied R1 drawings retain manufacturing-review/nominal status. Dependencies, calibration inputs and processing scope are documented in the package.

candidates.title: Machine Learning-Enabled Rover For Autonomous Navigation In Rough Terrain
candidates.abstract: A hybrid perception-control framework for navigating rough terrains by remote YOLOv8n-based terrain classification combined with on-board safety-based control of rover is proposed. The system uses ESP32-WROOM-32 module for controlling motors, ultrasonic sensors for detecting obstacles, infrared sensors for detecting cliff edges, and watchdog communication, whereas ESP32-CAM is responsible for sending terrain images to a laptop where the inference algorithm works. Four-class terrain data consisting of 800 images of grass, sand, gravel, and soil is employed for fine-tuning YOLOv8n using stratified dataset. Terrain predictions control movements depending on traversability coefficients, while safety controls take precedence over remote controls when an obstacle or communication link is detected. The evaluation over 60 trials of outdoor navigation has resulted in terrain classification with an accuracy of 78.3% and successful navigation with an 80.0% success rate. The perception-to-action latency was 170±23 ms, fail-safe time was 1.02±0.04 s, and emergency braking was 310±45 ms. The power consumption of the rover was 4.22±0.35 W, and the estimated operational time was around 4.5 h. Such values characterize the performance of the limited resources rover that implements the separation of complex computation-based inference from motion control in embedded systems.

candidates.title: SenTrojan: Revealing Analog Hardware Trojan Attacks on Sensors
candidates.abstract: Sensors bridge the physical and digital worlds, making their integrity critical to cyber-physical system security. Existing sensor attacks largely exploit unintended and sensor-specific physical vulnerabilities, limiting their generalizability and motivating a different threat model, i.e., whether an adversary can implant hidden attack surfaces into sensors before deployment. In this paper, we present SenTrojan, an analog hardware Trojan framework for sensors. SenTrojan embeds malicious functionality into analog signal circuitry commonly shared across diverse sensor architectures, and activates the hidden behavior through crafted external physical signals. Once activated, SenTrojan can induce sensor malfunctions ranging from permanent denial-of-service to static or dynamic spoofing. To achieve these effects under different architectural constraints, we introduce two complementary designs. The Logic-Rule-Driven (LRD) Trojan adds lightweight analog monitoring logic to detect trigger features such as frequency and amplitude, enabling reliable activation across various sensor types. The Physical-Effect-Driven (PED) Trojan targets sensors with exploitable native analog effects, e.g., nonlinearity and rectification, and realizes attacks with minimal component insertion. We evaluate SenTrojan on 14 sensors spanning 6 transduction principles and demonstrate its effectiveness across diverse real-world scenarios. Overall, SenTrojan achieves an average successful trigger rate above 95%, maintains over 97% similarity to benign behavior, incurs zero false-trigger rate for LRD designs, and introduces less than 5% average deviation in drift, noise floor, and response time. To our knowledge, this work is the first systematic study of analog sensor Trojans, broadening sensor security from unintended physical vulnerabilities to intentional supply-chain compromise.

candidates.title: Haptic Shared Control for Multi-Robot Systems
candidates.abstract: Multi-agent systems offer significant advantages in terms of flexibility and redundancy, enabling the efficient distribution of complex tasks among multiple robots. However, their deployment requires advanced control strategies to ensure optimal cooperation between autonomous agents and human operators. We propose a modification of the global connectivity maintenance algorithm to incorporate measurements taken in agent's local frame, using sensors with limited fields of view. This algorithm, responsible for the autonomous behavior of the multi-robot system, is combined with different adaptive supervision strategies, allowing the user to exert control at varying scales over the entire group. (i) Single Agent Control (S): The operator directly controls a single robot, (ii) Pinning Control (P): The operator imposes constraints on multiple robots to influence the group, (iii) Centroid Control (C): The operator acts on the system's center of mass to steer the entire fleet. In conjunction with the connectivity maintenance algorithm, these methods ensure compliance with inter-agent constraints while providing haptic feedback to the user regarding the system's connectivity state. The effectiveness of these approaches was evaluated through a user study, comparing performance with and without haptic feedback across multiple scenarios tailored to the different control modes.

candidates.title: Prosthetic Heart Valve Orifice Area Detection By Using A Combined Shock-Anisotropic Coherence Filter To Improve Level Sets Algorithm
candidates.abstract: Prosthetic valve is a synthetic or tissue substitute for the natural valve. It is designed to mimic the natural valve’s normal opening and clos-ing motions. The need for replacing heart valves increased drastically as the heart valve diseases became one of the dangerous death cause in the world. “Global demand for prosthetic heart valve market expected to reach USD 5,302.1 million in 2021 and growing of 9% from 2016 to 2021”. Unfortunately, Biological valves tend to fail over time, requir-ing replacement in 30% of patients within 10 years and 50% within 15 years. The demands for testing prosthetic valves are crucial to main-tain a robustness, durability and compatibility to improve patient health care which insure a place in the global market. This article discuss a novel method for automatic detection of a leaflet edges around ori-fice area opening for PHV (Prosthetic Heart Valve). A pre-processing algorithm using a combination of Anisotropic and Shock filter is proposed to enhance image quality before using a level set to detect PHV edges. This technique shows great capabilities to detect leaflet edges and provide additional enhancement compared to the other works.

candidates.title: Large Language Models for Industrial Robots: Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
candidates.abstract: With the accelerating intelligent transformation of global manufacturing, industrial robots have become critical equipment in modern smart factories. However, the growing prevalence of multi-variety, small-batch production has made the high programming threshold, tedious reconfiguration, and limited environmental adaptability of traditional industrial robots increasingly prominent. Over the past few years, large language models (LLMs) have proven to have strong semantic comprehension, knowledge reasoning, and task planning abilities, a new avenue in the intelligent upgrading of industrial robots. The systematic review of the literature on the topic of the industrial robot driven by LLM is presented in this paper, including the mainstream technical directions, and the representative studies in five areas of application: industrial inspection, assembly and collaboration, maintenance and fault recovery, manufacturing operation planning, and robot navigation. Based on this, the paper examines the key challenges to be addressed at present, including model output reliability and safety, the simulation-to-reality gap and real-time constraints, and data scarcity and distribution shift. It also discusses future research opportunities, including knowledge enrichment and reliable reasoning, lightweight deployment and edge computing, and life-long learning and domain adaptation. The purpose of this paper is to serve as a reference in future studies and implementation of LLMs in industrial robots.

candidates.title: Asynchronous Robot Policies
candidates.abstract: Scaling vision-language foundation models has significantly advanced generalist robot manipulation, but the increased model scale introduces computational latency that degrades real-time physical reactivity. Existing Vision-Language-Action (VLA) architectures execute high-level semantic reasoning and action ex- ecution sequentially within the primary control loop, creating a fundamental tension between semantic-reasoning capability and robot agility. To address this, we propose Asynchronous Robot Policy (ARP), an architectural framework that decouples semantic reasoning from low-level action generation using asynchronous processes operating at independent frequencies. In ARP, a high-capacity Vision-Language Model (VLM) asynchronously updates a semantic memory at low fre- quency, while a lightweight Vision-Action Expert, conditioned on this semantic memory, generates robot actions at a much higher control frequency. Such a formulation, enables having a fast perception-action loop without compromising on the semantic capability. To overcome asynchronous memory staleness, ARP trains the vision-action expert on the semantic staleness and execution delay, with temporally mismatched observation across processes. On Franka manipulation tasks, ARP achieves an 18% higher success rate and 20% less time need for execution in quasi-static setups, while 3-5 times baseline performance in dynamic simulation environments. Furthermore, ARP enables operating the VLM at 10 times lower than its nominal frequency with no significant performance loss making it much more efficient than the baseline. These results highlight the architectural advantages of modeling robot policies as asynchronous processes, enabling real-world reactive deployment without sacrificing the scale of foundation models.

candidates.title: Analysing responses to digital activism in Indonesia and Malaysia using AIDA framework
candidates.abstract: This article examines how six youth-led X accounts in Indonesia and Malaysia generated engagement and were associated with different forms of participation during the 2024 Indonesian presidential election and the 2022 Malaysian general election. Using the AIDA (Attention–Interest–Desire–Action) framework as a non-linear interpretive heuristic, it draws on platform metrics, interactional traces, and interviews with organisers. The study compares four candidate-centred volunteer accounts in Indonesia with two reform-oriented and civic education initiatives in Malaysia as an analytical contrast rather than a like-for-like national test. The findings show that spectacle and gamified formats scale Attention and affective Desire within platform attention economies, yet frequently remain associated with discursive, platform-proximate Action, revealing an action gap. In contrast, the Malaysian civic initiatives demonstrate stronger organisational and institutional linkages between online coordination, procedural participation and civic education. Situating AIDA within hybrid media ecologies and platform governance, the article argues that democratic effects depend less on visibility metrics than on organisational capacity and linkages to institutional processes. The study contributes to eParticipation research by distinguishing discursive-amplificatory, material-participatory, and institutional forms of Action and by specifying how platform logics condition their relationship to online engagement
